Implementation: ScienceDiscovery (ours) — PR follows within 24h. Do not pick up without a `pickup-ok` comment on this issue.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claim-Id: 9d9ba398ccce4763b47f946f890661f6
Branch: dev2/fix/777-named-entity-decoding
Base: 7942ad1fd495cc623df67234d8a01201430da204
At: 2026-11-03T02:07:55Z

## ScienceDiscovery evidence-backed issue

**Live main:** `7942ad1fd495cc623df67234d8a01201430da204` (`test(cas): cover the multi-chunk intact layout and align the materialize contract with #708`)
**Area:** `packages/data-source` — HTML text extraction used by the free search engines
**Filed by:** ScienceDiscovery Product

### Problem

`decodeEntities` resolves only five named references (`amp`, `lt`, `gt`, `quot`, `nbsp`) and leaves every other named reference literal, so search-result titles and snippets reach the model and the report as `café`, `5–10`, `—`, `…`, `O'Brien`.

### Reproduction on live main

```
$ cd packages/data-source && node --experimental-strip-types -e '
  import("./src/web/native/html.ts").then(m => {
    for (const s of ["café — 5–10 … O'Brien", "&lt;b&gt; stays text", "♦ … ’"])
      console.log(JSON.stringify(s), "->", JSON.stringify(m.textOf(s)));
  })'
```

Actual output (main `7942ad1f`):

```
"café — 5–10 … O'Brien" -> "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"
"&lt;b&gt; stays text" -> "<b> stays text"
"♦ … ’" -> "♦ … ’"
```

Expected (browser-equivalent text): `café — 5–10 … O'Brien`, `<b> stays text` (single pass preserved), `♦ … ’`.

### Evidence (file:line on this main)

- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts:27-33` — `NAMED_ENTITIES` contains exactly `amp`, `lt`, `gt`, `quot`, `nbsp`.
- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts:46-53` — `decodeEntities` matches **any** named reference (`([a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*)`) and returns `NAMED_ENTITIES.get(name) ?? match`, i.e. everything else falls through as literal text.
- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts:55-58` — `textOf` (strip tags → decode → collapse) is the shared extractor.
- Call sites that turn this into user-visible text: `packages/data-source/src/web/native/free-engines.ts:64`, `:69`, `:136`, `:141`, `:183`, `:192` (titles/snippets), plus `:68`, `:135`, `:181` for result URLs.

### Impact

DuckDuckGo/Bing/Brave result titles and snippets are what `web_search` returns to the model and what reports cite; a page title like "Café culture — a review" is rendered literally, so the evidence shown to the user (and fed back into the prompt) carries entity codes instead of text. Entity-heavy pages are exactly the older/European and encyclopedia sources a science search hits often.

### Expected vs actual

- Expected: named references decode the same way a browser renders them (at minimum the typographic and Latin-1 names that appear in titles: `mdash`, `ndash`, `hellip`, `rsquo`, `lsquo`, `ldquo`, `rdquo`, `eacute`, `egrave`, `ouml`, `apos`, `middot`, `times`, `deg`, `plusmn`, …).
- Actual: only 5 names decode; the rest stay literal.

### Acceptance

1. `decodeEntities` resolves the named references it matches (full HTML5 named set, or a documented bounded table that covers at least the names listed above).
2. The single-pass guarantee from #672 is preserved: `&lt;` → `<`, `&amp;` → `&`; decoded output is never rescanned.
3. Surrogate / non-character rejection stays as it is (`�` etc. remain literal).
4. `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.test.ts` gains cases for the named references above, and the existing five keep passing.
5. No change to numeric-reference behavior (`A`, `A`, `😀`).

### Not a duplicate

Open-issue search for `entity`, `entity decode`, `html text extraction`, `named entity` returns no open report; the only entity issue is closed #672 (double decoding), whose fix this preserves. No open PR touches `html.ts` (`#663`/`#678` are the UTF-16 truncation family in other modules).

issue:779.body:
## Title

Node.js API server crashes with ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT during streaming session messages — missing `response.headersSent` guard in catch-all error handler

## Summary

The ScienceDiscovery API server (`@sciencediscovery/api`) crashes with an uncaught `ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT` exception when an error occurs during streaming response to `POST /api/sessions/{id}/messages`. The crash is caused by a missing `response.headersSent` check in the catch-all error handler at `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3639`. The correct guard pattern already exists elsewhere in the same file at line 3159. The crash kills the Node.js process (exit status 1), which triggers a full stack restart via tini, causing approximately 20 seconds of service unavailability and returning 502 Bad Gateway to the client.

This bug has been observed 3 times in production-like testing. The exact error that triggers the catch block inside `streamAgentRun()` after headers have been flushed has not been identified.

## Affected Version

- **Package**: `@sciencediscovery/api` version `0.0.0`
- **Source file**: `services/api/src/http/index.ts` (3718 lines)
- **Defect location**: Line 3639 (catch-all error handler)
- **Correct pattern location**: Line 3159 (streaming error handler with guard)
- **Image**: `sciencediscovery-pure:incremental-002` (built 2026-11-02)

## Runtime Environment

| Component | Version |
|-----------|---------|
| Node.js | v22.23.4 |
| OS | Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm) |
| Container runtime | Docker (tini as init) |
| Architecture | x86_64 |

## Steps to Reproduce

**Stable reproduction has NOT been achieved.** The crash occurs non-deterministically during streaming session message requests. The following describes the observed conditions:

1. Start the ScienceDiscovery stack (`services/api` + adapter + JiuwenSwarm gateway/agentserver)
2. Create or access an existing session
3. Send a `POST /api/sessions/{id}/messages` request with a message that triggers agent execution
4. The agent begins streaming its response (SSE)
5. At some point during streaming, after response headers have been flushed, an error occurs inside `streamAgentRun()`
6. The error propagates to the catch-all handler at `index.ts:3607`
7. The error is not matched by any specific error type check, falls through to the `else` branch
8. `sendError(response, 500, "Internal server error")` is called at line 3639
9. `sendError` → `sendJson` → `send` → `response.writeHead()` throws `ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT`
10. The uncaught exception crashes the Node.js process

**Observed frequency**: 3 crashes in ~1 hour of active testing with multiple concurrent sessions.

**Suspected triggers** (not confirmed):
- Client disconnects during SSE streaming
- LLM Gateway returns 503 during agent execution
- Internal timeout during long-running agent tasks

## Expected Behavior

When an error occurs during streaming response (after headers have been sent), the server should:
1. Log the error with full context
2. Check `response.headersSent` before attempting to send an error response
3. If headers are already sent, destroy the connection gracefully (`response.destroy(error)`)
4. If headers are not yet sent, send the appropriate error response
5. The Node.js process should NOT crash

This is the pattern already implemented at `index.ts:3159`:
```typescript
if (response.headersSent) {
  response.destroy(error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error)));
} else {
  sendError(response, 502, error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error));
}
```

## Actual Behavior

The catch-all error handler at `index.ts:3633-3640` does not check `response.headersSent`:

```typescript
} else {
  apiLog.error("unclassified_request_error", {
    errorMessage: shortErrorMessage(error),
    method: request.method ?? "UNKNOWN",
    path: requestPath,
    status: 500,
  });
  sendError(response, 500, "Internal server error");  // ← crashes if headers already sent
}
```

When `sendError` is called after headers have been flushed, Node.js throws:

```
node:_http_server:354
    throw new ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT('write');
          ^

Error [ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT]: Cannot write headers after they are sent to the client
    at ServerResponse.writeHead (node:_http_server:354:11)
    at send (file:///app/services/api/dist/http/response.js:15:14)
    at sendJson (file:///app/services/api/dist/http/response.js:24:5)
    at sendError (file:///app/services/api/dist/http/response.js:27:5)
    at Server.<anonymous> (file:///app/services/api/dist/http/index.js:3237:17) {
  code: 'ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT'
}
```

This uncaught exception crashes the Node.js process with exit status 1.

## Error Stack Trace

```
node:_http_server:354
    throw new ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT('write');
          ^

Error [ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT]: Cannot write headers after they are sent to the client
    at ServerResponse.writeHead (node:_http_server:354:11)
    at send (file:///app/services/api/dist/http/response.js:15:14)
    at sendJson (file:///app/services/api/dist/http/response.js:24:5)
    at sendError (file:///app/services/api/dist/http/response.js:27:5)
    at Server.<anonymous> (file:///app/services/api/dist/http/index.js:3237:17) {
  code: 'ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT'
}

Node.js v22.23.4
A ScienceDiscovery process exited with status 1; stopping the stack.
```

**Cascade failure** (Adapter layer):
```
legacy_proxy_failure request_id=<sanitized>
  method=POST
  path=/api/sessions/<session-id>/messages
  phase=headers
  elapsed_ms=1993
  causes=[RemoteProtocolError in proxy.py:91]

→ Client receives: 502 Bad Gateway
```

## Timestamped Failure Sequence

| Time (relative) | Event | Source |
|-----------------|-------|--------|
| T+0s | `POST /api/sessions/{id}/messages` → 200 OK (prior successful request to same session) | API access log |
| T+0s | `GET /health` → 200 OK | Health check log |
| T+1s | **ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT thrown** at `index.js:3237` | Node.js stderr |
| T+1s | `A ScienceDiscovery process exited with status 1; stopping the stack.` | tini supervisor |
| T+2s | `legacy_proxy_failure ... RemoteProtocolError ... elapsed_ms=1993` | Adapter log |
| T+2s | `POST /api/sessions/{id}/messages` → 502 Bad Gateway | API access log |
| T+3s | `Shutting down` × 2, `Finished server process [215]`, `[48]` | Service shutdown log |
| T+3s | `Starting the sandbox runner daemon...` | tini auto-restart |
| T+10s | All services started, health checks passing | Service startup log |
| T+20s | `run-binding start/release` operations resume | Agent run log |

**Total downtime**: ~20 seconds (from crash to full recovery)

## Impact on API and Agent Sessions

### Direct Impact
- **Node.js API process crash**: The entire `services/api` process exits with status 1
- **Full stack restart**: tini supervisor stops and restarts all services
- **Service unavailability**: ~20 seconds of complete service downtime
- **Client impact**: In-flight requests receive 502 Bad Gateway

### Data Impact
- **No data loss observed**: Session state is persisted before the crash point
- **No state corruption observed**: Service recovers fully after restart
- **Agent runs interrupted**: Any in-flight agent run is terminated; run status may be left in an intermediate state

### Recurrence
- **3 occurrences** in ~1 hour of active testing
- **Non-deterministic**: Depends on timing of error during streaming
- **Auto-recovery**: Service restarts automatically each time

## Root Cause Assessment

### Classification
**B. PROBABLE_UPSTREAM_BUG** — The code defect is confirmed in upstream ScienceDiscovery native code, but the exact triggering error (what fails inside `streamAgentRun()` after headers are sent) remains unidentified.

### Defect
Missing `response.headersSent` guard in the catch-all error handler at `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3639`.

### Contributing Factor
The triggering error occurs during streaming response inside `streamAgentRun()`. After response headers have been flushed to the client, any error that propagates to the catch-all handler will cause the crash. The specific error has not been captured because the crash destroys the in-flight error object.

### Why the Correct Pattern Was Not Applied Everywhere
The correct guard pattern exists at `index.ts:3159` (in a different catch block for streaming responses). The catch-all handler at `index.ts:3639` was likely added later and did not include the guard, suggesting an oversight rather than a design choice.

## Evidence References

1. **Crash stack trace**: Captured from Node.js stderr (see Error Stack Trace section above)
2. **Source code location**: `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3639` (TypeScript source)
3. **Compiled code location**: `services/api/dist/http/index.js:3237` (compiled JavaScript)
4. **Correct pattern**: `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3159` (existing guard in same file)
5. **Historical occurrences**: 3 crashes in Docker container logs over ~1 hour
6. **Cascade failure log**: Adapter `legacy_proxy_failure` with `RemoteProtocolError`
7. **Recovery log**: tini auto-restart, all services recovered in ~20 seconds

## Workaround / Recovery Observation

### Current Workaround
The service auto-recovers via tini supervisor. No manual intervention is required. Downtime is approximately 20 seconds per crash.

### Proposed Fix
Add `response.headersSent` guard to the catch-all handler at `index.ts:3639`:

```typescript
} else {
  apiLog.error("unclassified_request_error", {
    errorMessage: shortErrorMessage(error),
    method: request.method ?? "UNKNOWN",
    path: requestPath,
    status: 500,
  });
  if (response.headersSent) {
    response.destroy(new Error("Internal server error (after headers sent)"));
  } else {
    sendError(response, 500, "Internal server error");
  }
}
```

This follows the exact pattern already used at `index.ts:3159`.

### Additional Recommendation
Audit all other catch blocks in `index.ts` that call `sendError()` to ensure they include the `headersSent` guard. There may be other locations with the same defect.

### Diagnostic Improvement
Consider logging the full error object (not just `shortErrorMessage`) in the `unclassified_request_error` handler to aid diagnosis of the triggering error:

```typescript
apiLog.error("unclassified_request_error", {
  errorMessage: shortErrorMessage(error),
  errorStack: error instanceof Error ? error.stack : undefined,  // ← add this
  method: request.method ?? "UNKNOWN",
  path: requestPath,
  status: 500,
});
```

## Sanitization Notice

This issue report has been sanitized:
- ✅ No API keys or authentication tokens included
- ✅ Session IDs replaced with `{id}` placeholders
- ✅ Request IDs replaced with `<sanitized>` placeholders
- ✅ Internal IP addresses limited to standard Docker networking (127.0.0.1, 172.18.0.1)
- ✅ No user data or conversation content included
- ✅ Internal file paths limited to source code locations relevant to the bug

## Metadata

- **Reporter**: CatalystPI project (Huawei collaboration)
- **Date**: 2026-11-03
- **Severity**: High (service crash with data plane impact)
- **Priority**: High (affects production stability)
- **Component**: `services/api` (Node.js HTTP server)
- **Labels**: `bug`, `crash`, `error-handling`, `streaming`

issue:780.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

`/evolve-design` stops at **Checkpoint 3** so the user can approve the spend. That checkpoint is only meaningful if the per-call ceiling it shows is the one the run will actually get.

Today the agent can show a ceiling that is either:

- below the floor preflight enforces, so the user approves a run that then refuses itself; or
- the cheap "thinking off" ceiling on an endpoint that ignores the request to disable thinking.

The second case is measured, not hypothetical. On a custom OpenAI-compatible gateway (`apiVariant: openai`, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash), every call was sent with thinking disabled, reasoned anyway, hit the 16k quiet ceiling and returned no content at all. The real price on such an endpoint is the thinking ceiling: 96,000 tokens per call for `puct` and 128,000 for `openevolve`, whatever the request says.

Today the budget is also arithmetic the agent performs in prose, so the number in the checkpoint and the number preflight accepts are written in two different places.

Related: #561 concerns reasoning/output token accounting after the fact; this issue is about what the user is asked to approve before the spend.

## Design Ideas

- **One source of truth for the arithmetic.** `services/api/src/evolution/call-budget.ts` exposes `describeEvolveBudget(model, requestedThinking)`, returning `{ maxSeconds, model, perCallCeiling, thinking: { effective, note? }, totalTokenCap }`. Preflight, the run proposal and the agent all read the same function.
- **Detect whether the endpoint can disable thinking.** `endpointCanDisableThinking` (`services/api/src/evolution/model-thinking.ts`) decides per model, with a `facts.thinkingSupported` override for endpoints whose behavior is known.
- **Let the agent read the plan instead of guessing.** A new built-in tool, `get_evolve_budget`, returns the plan for the model the turn is using. The platform runtime wires it to `describeEvolveBudget` for that model.
- **Keep the gate and the checkpoint agreeing.** When thinking cannot be turned off, preflight applies the thinking floor even if the goal says `thinking: "disabled"`, and stops offering "turn thinking off" as a fix. `startProposedRun` clamps the started goal to `thinking: "enabled"` and takes `maxTokensPerCall` from the same ceiling.
- **Say it in the checkpoint.** `skills/evolve-design/SKILL.md` requires Checkpoint 3 to call `get_evolve_budget`, quote the money line, and disclose "thinking enabled — this endpoint has no thinking control" when the plan carries a note.

## Involved Public APIs

- New agent tool `get_evolve_budget` (input `{ thinking? }`, output `EvolveBudgetPlan`), documented in `docs/en/reference/builtin-tools.md` and `docs/zh/reference/builtin-tools.md`.
- New exported type `EvolveBudgetPlan` in `packages/schema`.
- No HTTP API change; the `/api/evolve/*` routes are untouched.
- Two existing behaviors tighten: preflight's `max_tokens_too_low` applies the thinking floor on endpoints that cannot disable thinking, and its `fix` no longer names a control the endpoint does not have.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `services/api`: `evolution/preflight.ts`, `evolution/proposal.ts`, `evolution/call-budget.ts`, `evolution/model-thinking.ts`, `bootstrap/platform.ts`.
- `packages/evolve`: the new tool and its registration; `packages/schema`: the plan type.
- `skills/evolve-design`: Checkpoint 3 wording.
- The desktop and web UIs need no change: the checkpoint is agent prose, and the acceptance surface is a desktop run against a custom-gateway model.

## Test Design and Test Plan

Unit tests:

- `services/api/src/evolution/call-budget.test.ts` — ceilings per algorithm and thinking mode, total cap and wall-clock defaults, the note for endpoints without a thinking control.
- `services/api/src/evolution/model-thinking.test.ts` — variants that can and cannot disable thinking, and the `facts` override.
- `services/api/src/evolution/preflight.test.ts` — for both algorithms and `apiVariant` unset/openai/deepseek: the ceiling the checkpoint shows passes the gate, and the quiet ceiling on an endpoint that cannot disable thinking is refused; the refusal never suggests turning thinking off.
- `services/api/src/evolution/proposal.test.ts` — the started goal's `thinking`, `maxTokensPerCall`, `maxTokens` and `maxSeconds` equal the plan shown at the checkpoint.
- `packages/evolve/src/index.test.ts` — the tool returns the plan for the turn's model.

Commands: `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api test`, `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/evolve test`, `pnpm check`.

End-to-end (desktop, manual):

1. Select a custom gateway model with `apiVariant: openai` (thinking cannot be disabled).
2. Run `/evolve-design --algorithm puct …` and reach Checkpoint 3.
3. The reply must show 96,000 tokens per call, state that thinking cannot be turned off on this endpoint, and quote 600,000 tokens / 7,200 s.
4. Approve without edits; the started run must carry `maxTokensPerCall: 96000` and `thinking: "enabled"`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On an endpoint that cannot disable thinking, Checkpoint 3 shows the thinking ceiling (96k for `puct`, 128k for `openevolve`) and discloses that thinking is enabled.
- [ ] The ceiling shown at Checkpoint 3 passes preflight; approving without edits starts a run whose budget equals the shown plan.
- [ ] On endpoints that can disable thinking, the quiet ceiling (8k / 16k) is still shown and accepted.
- [ ] A too-low ceiling is never answered with "turn thinking off" when the endpoint has no such control.
- [ ] `pnpm check` passes.

Command that must pass: `pnpm check`

## Additional Information

- Implemented in #715.
- Verified in the desktop UI on 2026-11-03 with a custom-gateway DeepSeek model: the agent called `get_evolve_budget`, then showed 96,000 tokens per call, 600,000 tokens / 7,200 s total, and 5 × 96,000 = 480,000 worst case, before any run was created.

Base: 2f22d16ff8fd329e14cf38ea3140d2d4fa2bae9a
At: 2026-11-03T03:17:30Z

The desktop app's workbook preview reads an `.xlsx` far enough to draw each sheet as a table (`apps/desktop/src/app/xlsx.ts`). Excel stores a cell's phonetic guide — Japanese furigana, Chinese pinyin — as an `<rPh>` run inside the string element (`<si>` in `sharedStrings.xml`, or `<is>` for an inline string). The spreadsheet grammar for that element is `CT_Rst = (t | r | rPh)*`, and `<rPh>` is a reading shown above the text, never part of the cell value. The reader collects **every** `<t>` under the string element, so the reading is appended to the cell.

## Actual

A cell whose shared string is

```xml
<si><t>漢字</t><rPh sb="0" eb="2"><t>カンジ</t></rPh></si>
```

previews as `漢字カンジ`. Excel shows `漢字`.

The inline-string form (`<is><t>東京</t><rPh sb="0" eb="2"><t>トウキョウ</t></rPh></is>`) previews as `東京トウキョウ`; Excel shows `東京`.

Every cell and every column header that carries a guide is doubled this way, so a workbook written in Japanese or Chinese Excel opens with a table that reads as garbage.

## Expected

`漢字` and `東京`: the text runs of the cell, without any `<rPh>` content. Rich-text `<r>` runs (`<si><r><t>東</t></r><r><t>京</t></r></si> → `東京`) must keep working.

## Where

- `apps/desktop/src/app/xlsx.ts:66-71` — `textRuns` appends the text of every `<t>` in the string element, including the `<t>` inside `<rPh>`.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/xlsx.ts:77` — `readSharedStrings` applies it to each `<si>`.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/xlsx.ts:199-202` — `inlineStr` cells apply it to `<is>`.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/xlsx.ts:278` — `readWorkbook` loads the shared-string part.

## Reproduction

On `2f22d16ff8fd329e14cf38ea3140d2d4fa2bae9a`, with the probe below (it needs only the desktop app's existing `fflate` dependency):

```bash
cd apps/desktop
cat > xlsx-rph.ts   # paste the probe below, then Ctrl-D
node_modules/.bin/tsx xlsx-rph.ts
```

```ts
// apps/desktop/xlsx-rph.ts — a throwaway probe, deleted after it prints.
import { zipSync, strToU8 } from "fflate";
import { readWorkbook } from "./src/app/xlsx.ts";

const archive = zipSync({
  "xl/workbook.xml": strToU8(`<workbook><sheets><sheet name="S" sheetId="1" r:id="rId1"/></sheets></workbook>`),
  "xl/_rels/workbook.xml.rels": strToU8(`<Relationships><Relationship Id="rId1" Target="worksheets/sheet1.xml"/></Relationships>`),
  "xl/sharedStrings.xml": strToU8(
    `<sst><si><t>漢字</t><rPh sb="0" eb="2"><t>カンジ</t></rPh></si>`
    + `<si><t>漢字</t></si>`
    + `<si><r><t>東</t></r><r><t>京</t></r></si></sst>`),
  "xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml": strToU8(
    `<worksheet><sheetData><row r="1">`
    + `<c r="A1" t="s"><v>0</v></c><c r="B1" t="s"><v>1</v></c><c r="C1" t="s"><v>2</v></c>`
    + `<c r="D1" t="inlineStr"><is><t>東京</t><rPh sb="0" eb="2"><t>トウキョウ</t></rPh></is></c>`
    + `</row></sheetData></worksheet>`),
});

const [sheet] = readWorkbook(archive) ?? [];
console.log("A(shared+rPh)  =", JSON.stringify(sheet?.table.columns[0]));
console.log("B(shared only) =", JSON.stringify(sheet?.table.columns[1]));
console.log("C(rich runs)   =", JSON.stringify(sheet?.table.columns[2]));
console.log("D(inline+rPh)  =", JSON.stringify(sheet?.table.columns[3]));
```

Output on that revision:

```
A(shared+rPh)  = "漢字カンジ"
B(shared only) = "漢字"
C(rich runs)   = "東京"
D(inline+rPh)  = "東京トウキョウ"
```

`B` and `C` are the controls: without a guide, and with plain rich-text runs, the reader is already correct, so the defect is the `<rPh>` subtree and nothing else.

The existing suite is green and does not cover this: `cd apps/desktop && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/xlsx.test.ts` → `# tests 10 # pass 10 # fail 0`.

## Acceptance

1. A shared string with `<rPh>` (`apps/desktop/tests/xlsx.test.ts`) yields the cell text without the reading.
2. An inline `<is>` with `<rPh>` behaves the same.
3. Rich text with `<r>` runs plus an `<rPh>` run yields only the `<r>` text.
4. The 10 existing `tests/xlsx.test.ts` cases keep passing; no other reader behaviour changes (date serials, inline strings, booleans, sheet order, column mapping).

Out of scope: the CSV/TSV preview path (`table-data.ts`), HTML entity decoding, workbook formats other than `.xlsx`.

## Lane

`apps/desktop` → Dev-1 (web/desktop), suggested branch `dev1/fix/<n>-xlsx-phonetic-runs`.

issue:785.body:
## Summary

Opening a `.docx`, `.pptx`, `.odt`, `.zip` (or any other binary container without a renderer) in the desktop panel shows garbage text. `apps/desktop/src/app/document-payload.ts:21-23` states the contract itself: a document this app has no renderer for is *"kept out of the tab entirely rather than shown as mojibake"*. The dispatch does the opposite, because the kind has no "unrenderable" member and the unknown-extension fallback is `source`.

## Where it lives

- `apps/desktop/src/app/preview-kind.ts:54-56` — `isBinaryDocument` is true only for `image`, `pdf`, `sheet`; everything else is decoded as text.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/preview-kind.ts:83` — the catch-all `return "source"` gives `.docx`, `.pptx`, `.odt`, `.zip`, `.7z`, `.tar`, `.gz`, `.xls`, `.xlsb`… the same kind as a `.log` or a `.toml`.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/document-payload.ts:102-104` — `!isBinaryDocument(kind)` ⇒ `new TextDecoder("utf-8").decode(bytes)`, so the zip container is decoded as text.
- The panel already has a state for "cannot show this document": `tooLarge` (`document-payload.ts:34,101`, rendered by `apps/desktop/src/views/DocumentPreview.tsx` with strings in `apps/desktop/src/text/en.ts` and `zh.ts`). An unrenderable binary document needs the same treatment, not a `<pre>` of replacement characters.

## Reproduction (on `main` `a429ba1d4eca17af8cfabb9f28abe9d651e38e6c`)

```
cd apps/desktop && node --import tsx --input-type=module -e 'import{documentPayload}from"./src/app/document-payload.ts";import{documentKind}from"./src/app/preview-kind.ts";import{zipSync,strToU8}from"fflate";const b=zipSync({"word/document.xml":strToU8("<w:document/>")});const k=documentKind("r.docx","application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document");console.log(k,JSON.stringify(documentPayload(b,"r.docx","application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document").content.slice(0,8)))'
```

Actual:

```
source "PK\u0003\u0004\u0014\u0000\u0000\u0000"
```

Expected: the document is not offered as decoded text at all — the tab reports that this build has no renderer for it (name, size and the download stay available), which is what the module's own contract says.

Scope check: the same probe with a `.log`, `.toml`, `.py` or `.txt` must keep returning decoded text — this is about binary containers that happen to have no renderer, not about narrowing the text path.

## Acceptance

1. `.docx`, `.pptx`, `.odt`, `.zip` (and the other archive/legacy-office extensions that have no renderer) no longer produce decoded text, by extension and by the media types the server answers for them (`application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document`, `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation`, `application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.text`, `application/zip`).
2. The panel shows the same kind of message the oversized-document path already shows, with an English and a Chinese string, rather than mojibake.
3. `apps/desktop/tests` covers: the new unrenderable state for a `.docx` payload, and regression cases proving `.log`/`.toml`/`.py`/`.txt` and the existing image / pdf / xlsx paths are unchanged.
4. `xlsx` keeps working as a sheet: a workbook is still read as a table, not sent down the new path.

## Notes

- No open issue or open PR mentions `docx`, `odt` or `pptx` (searched issues and PRs, open and closed); `#782` is the `.xlsx` phonetic-run fix and `#778` is HTML entity decoding in `packages/data-source` — different paths.
- Found while checking the `.xlsx` phonetic-run fix for the same shape of defect; the probe above is read-only and reproducible from a clean checkout.

Base: a429ba1d4eca17af8cfabb9f28abe9d651e38e6c
At: 2026-11-03T05:16:02Z

## Summary

`chembl_search_molecules` (and `chembl_similarity_search`, which also returns molecules) emit record URLs on the retired `explore/molecule` route. Every returned molecule record — `url`, `primaryCitation.url` and the rendered `primaryCitation.markdown` — points at a page that now returns **HTTP 404**, so a user or an agent clicking the citation lands on a ChEMBL error page instead of the compound.

ChEMBL's live molecule page is `compound_report_card`. The `target` branch of the same template still works, so only the molecule kind is broken.

## Where

- `services/gateway/src/sciencediscovery_gateway/public_biomed_mcp.py:840-855` — `_chembl_records`; the URL is built at `:848-852` from `data_sources.chembl.explore_template` with `kind=kind` and `identifier=identifier.removeprefix("CHEMBL")`.
- `config/external-urls.json:94` — `"explore_template": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chembl/explore/{kind}/CHEMBL{identifier}"`.
- Call sites that pass `kind="molecule"`: `:868-870` (`chembl_search_molecules`), `:894-907` (`chembl_similarity_search`).
- The same template is correct for `kind="target"` (`:873-876`), so it cannot simply be changed in place.

## Expected vs actual

- Expected: `chembl_search_molecules("aspirin")` returns a molecule record whose `url` opens the compound page for `CHEMBL25`.
- Actual: the record carries `https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chembl/explore/molecule/CHEMBL25`, which returns **404**. The live page is `https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chembl/compound_report_card/CHEMBL25/` (200).

## Reproduction (one command, from the repo root)

```
cd services/gateway && PYTHONPATH=src python3.12 <probe>
```

The probe imports the shipped module (only the third-party `mcp`/`httpx` transports are stubbed, because this sandbox does not have them installed), lets the real `_get_json` hit ChEMBL over HTTPS, and calls the real tool function:

```
record   : CHEMBL25 | ASPIRIN
url      : https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chembl/explore/molecule/CHEMBL25
markdown : [Chembl:CHEMBL25](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chembl/explore/molecule/CHEMBL25)
record   : CHEMBL5314595 | ASPIRIN TRELAMINE
url      : https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chembl/explore/molecule/CHEMBL5314595
markdown : [Chembl:CHEMBL5314595](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chembl/explore/molecule/CHEMBL5314595)
tool     : search_molecules
```

Provider check of exactly those URLs (same box, `curl -L`):

```
404 https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chembl/explore/molecule/CHEMBL25
200 https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chembl/compound_report_card/CHEMBL25/
404 https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chembl/explore/molecule/CHEMBL5314595
200 https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chembl/compound_report_card/CHEMBL5314595/
200 https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chembl/explore/target/CHEMBL1806
```

The last line is the control: the template itself is fine for targets, so this is a per-kind route change on ChEMBL's side, not a wrong host or a transient outage.

## Smallest fix

1. Add `"molecule_template": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chembl/compound_report_card/CHEMBL{identifier}/"` to the `chembl` block of `config/external-urls.json`.
2. In `_chembl_records`, use that template when `kind == "molecule"` and keep `explore_template` for `target` (the activity branch is already tracked separately in the open PR #441 and must not be duplicated here).

## Acceptance criteria

- New gateway unit test (no network): `_chembl_records("molecule", [{"molecule_chembl_id": "CHEMBL25", "pref_name": "ASPIRIN"}])[0]["url"] == "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chembl/compound_report_card/CHEMBL25/"`.
- Same test asserts `_chembl_records("target", [{"target_chembl_id": "CHEMBL1806"}])[0]["url"]` is unchanged (`.../explore/target/CHEMBL1806`).
- `primaryCitation.url` and `primaryCitation.markdown` match the corrected `url`.
- `uv run --project services/gateway python -m unittest discover -s services/gateway/tests -p 'test_*.py'` stays green.

## Dedupe

Searched issues and PRs (open + closed) for `chembl`, `compound_report_card`, `explore/molecule`: no issue covers a dead molecule link. #420 is the umbrella "complete MCP domain databases" feature and #441 (open, `feat(mcp)`) rewrites `_chembl_records` only to send **activity** links to the API JSON — it leaves the molecule URL on the retired route, so this is not a duplicate of #441.

## Lane

`services/gateway` (Python) — Dev-2 by the repo's lane split. Flagging explicitly because Dev-1 was the preferred target this round: I found no Dev-1-lane defect with comparable evidence that is not already covered by #785 / #777 / #781 / #783.

## Verification environment

- base: `main` at `a429ba1d4eca17af8cfabb9f28abe9d651e38e6c`
- `python3.12` (the gateway requires 3.11+ for `datetime.UTC`)

issue:792.body:
## What happens

Once #791 (fix for #788) lands, a chunked download — a response without `content-length`, which is every in-repo MCP source since none of them sets `expectedBytes` — correctly stops reporting `totalBytes: 0` and stops claiming 100%. But the download card then renders **0% for the whole download**, including after it completes, because it substitutes a zero for the now-absent value:

```tsx
// apps/web/src/GovernedDownloadCards.tsx:151
t(JOB_STATE_KEYS[job.state])··· {job.progress.percent ?? 0}% · {bytesDownloaded}
```

`percent` is `undefined` when the total is unknown (`packages/artifact-manager/src/governed-download-manager.ts`, `totalBytes ? … : …` progress branch), so the user sees a progress bar of text saying `0%` while the byte counter next to it climbs from 1.0 MB to 2.0 MB and the job reaches `completed`. "Unknown size" reads as "not started".

## Expected

When `progress.percent` is absent the card must not print a percentage: show the byte count alone, or an explicit unknown marker in the same slot. When `percent` is present nothing changes.

## Evidence

- `apps/web/src/GovernedDownloadCards.tsx:151` — `{job.progress.percent ?? 0}%`.
- `packages/artifact-manager/src/governed-download-manager.ts:684` — `percent: totalBytes ? … : 100` (removed by #791; the key is then absent rather than 0).
- The mid-flight job shape asserted by #791's new test: `{"bytesDownloaded":1048576,"filesCompleted":0,"filesTotal":1}` — no `percent`, no `totalBytes`.
- Verified by reading that render line against that job shape; no browser journey exists for the downloads panel, so the acceptance is a component-level assertion plus the existing page tests staying green.

## Acceptance

- A job whose progress has no `percent` renders no `NN%` text (byte count and state still shown).
- A job with `percent: 42` still renders `42%`.
- The `apps/web` test suite stays green; no change to `packages/artifact-manager` or the job shape.

issue:794.body:
## What happens

The desktop composer sends the message when Enter confirms an IME candidate. Both Enter paths only look at the key and shift, never at the composition state:

```tsx
// apps/desktop/src/views/Composer.tsx:836  (skill "/" menu: Enter picks an entry)
if (event.key === "Tab" || (event.key === "Enter" && !event.shiftKey)) {
// apps/desktop/src/views/Composer.tsx:843  (composer: Enter submits)
if (event.key === "Enter" && !event.shiftKey) {
```

With a Chinese / Japanese / Korean IME the user presses Enter to accept the candidate word; that keydown reaches `submit()` with the uncommitted text still in the field, so a half-typed message is sent, the input is cleared, and a real run starts (tokens spent). In the `/` menu the same keydown also accepts an entry the user did not choose.

`apps/web` already guards the same keydown, which is what makes the desktop behaviour a gap rather than a design choice:

```tsx
// apps/web/src/App.tsx:5051
if (event.key !== "Enter" || event.shiftKey || event.nativeEvent.isComposing) return;
```

The same missing guard exists on two other desktop Enter handlers: `apps/desktop/src/views/Sidebar.tsx:164` (commit rename) and `apps/desktop/src/views/PromptDialog.tsx:109` (submit dialog).

## Expected

While an IME composition is in progress (`KeyboardEvent.nativeEvent.isComposing` true, with `keyCode === 229` as the fallback for engines that do not set it), Enter must not submit, must not pick from the `/` menu, must not commit a rename and must not submit a dialog. After the composition ends, Enter behaves exactly as it does today.

## Evidence

Reproduced on `main` `99298fe7cc6aba54181b93cd071d5357cd0073a0` by rendering the real desktop `Composer` component with a synthetic keydown that carries `isComposing: true` and the uncommitted text `蛋白`:

```
# SENT-WHILE-COMPOSING ["蛋白"]
not ok 1 - Enter while the IME is composing does not send the half-typed message
# SENT-AFTER-COMPOSING ["protein "]
ok 2 - Enter after composition ends still sends
# tests 2
# pass 1
# fail 1
```

The control case (composition already ended) is green, so the failure is the composing path and not the probe.

## Acceptance

- Enter with `isComposing: true` submits nothing, clears nothing and starts no run, in the composer and in the `/` menu; the composed text stays in the field.
- Enter after composition ends still submits, still picks from the menu, still commits the rename and still submits the dialog.
- The guard is a pure function (no DOM) so it can be unit tested in `apps/desktop`, where the test environment has no DOM; the desktop `tsc` and the existing suites stay green.

issue:797.body:
## Background Description

ScienceDiscovery already has trusted, build-time installed plugins. This issue defines how to evolve that implementation into a clearer, maintainable extension architecture without breaking existing execution, permissions, settings, or historical data.

Current implementation:
- `packages/plugin-sdk` defines manifests, service contracts, configuration, and create/start/dispose lifecycle. Plugin scopes resolve dependencies and clean up failed activation in reverse order.
- Runtime contributions include tools, context factories, state providers, batch policies, and optional result submission.
- Skill, MCP, scheduler, Plan, source connectors, and JSON artifact viewing have plugin entry points.
- Settings inherit across global/project/session scopes; Run composition is frozen at execution start.
- Web extensions have settings, project-view, and artifact-viewer registration points.

Remaining boundaries:
- `services/api/src/plugins/catalog.ts` and `runtime.ts` explicitly register installed packages and wire their factories. New plugins still require host/build integration.
- Some capabilities reuse Workspace factories; some domain control-plane logic remains in the API host.
- The contribution contract does not allow general replacement of AgentLoop or the harness.
- Native and JiuwenSwarm use different loop/context execution paths. Plugin registration alone does not establish equivalent behavior across backends.
- Plugins are trusted in-process code; manifest permissions do not provide code isolation.

This issue delivers an architecture proposal and implementation breakdown. Dynamic installation, hot reload, and runtime replacement are options to assess, not implementation commitments.

## Design Ideas

1. **Preserve the existing capability model.** Keep domain-owned packages, public exports, explicit Ports, and one authoritative state store. Avoid exposing the whole Store or NativeAgent through a global container.
2. **Separate installation from activation.** Describe the flow as installed package → dependency/service/permission checks → effective scoped settings → frozen Run composition → lifecycle → contributions. Keep installed, available, authorized, and active states distinct.
3. **Reduce duplicate registration.** Evaluate build-time generation of separate API and client catalogs from an installation description. Server factories must not leak into browser bundles. Compare this with retaining explicit registration before selecting an approach.
4. **Define backend capabilities explicitly.** Produce a native/JiuwenSwarm matrix for every contribution type. Unsupported combinations must be rejected or diagnosed explicitly. Main, child, and reviewer agents must use the same frozen selection, with documented role-specific behavior.
5. **Add replaceable contracts only for concrete needs.** Evaluate runtime backend, model, and execution-provider seams. Specify cancellation, events, recovery, tool permissions, and artifact/result submission before proposing a new interface.
6. **Retain Run stability.** Configuration changes affect subsequent Runs. Evaluate draining old instances before disposal; an upgrade must not mix implementations inside a running composition. Define package/API/state-schema versions separately and retain historical read support.
7. **Make conflicts deterministic.** Specify tool-name collision handling, context budget allocation, batch-policy ordering, result-submission ownership, and dependency-disable behavior.

Options to compare:

| Option | Scope | Main tradeoff |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Strengthen current capability plugins | Catalog consistency, Ports, diagnostics, lifecycle contracts | Lowest migration cost; host integration remains controlled |
| Add replaceable harness contracts | Backend/model/execution seams driven by concrete use cases | More flexibility; requires cross-backend semantic contracts |
| Introduce dynamic distribution | Package resolution, installation, client assets, upgrades and rollback | Largest operational and compatibility cost; untrusted code requires isolation |

Recommended starting direction: strengthen the current mechanism, then add narrowly scoped replacement contracts. Record evidence and alternatives in an architecture decision before choosing dynamic distribution.

## Involved Public APIs

This analysis does not change public APIs. Inventory and assess compatibility for:
- `PluginManifest`, `PluginDefinition`, `PluginInstance`, and `createPluginScope` in `packages/plugin-sdk`.
- `RuntimeContribution` in `packages/plugin-sdk/src/runtime.ts`.
- Plugin settings and scoped Bridge under `/api/projects/:projectId/plugins`, including configuration revisions, query/command authorization, and events.
- Domain package `./plugin`, `./manifest`, and `./web` exports.

Any proposed API change must include consumer impact, versioning, migration, and failure behavior. Distinguish proposed interfaces from contracts already implemented.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

| Module | Relationship and analysis responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/plugin-sdk` | Manifest, lifecycle, negotiation, services, configuration and Bridge contracts |
| `services/api/src/plugins` | Installation catalog, factory wiring, scoped settings and control plane |
| `services/api/src/native-agent` | Run composition, contribution assembly, lifecycle and backend integration |
| `packages/runtime-core`, `packages/tools` | Loop invariants, tool execution, permissions, cancellation and result ownership |
| `packages/context` | StateView capture, state schema/revision, projection consistency and context budgets |
| `packages/workspace`, capability packages | Remaining factory coupling; domain Ports and ownership; avoid duplicate tool injection |
| JiuwenSwarm integration and adapter | Backend capability parity, event translation, cancellation and recovery boundaries |
| `apps/web/src/plugins` | Current UI registration, authenticated Bridge and server/client import separation |
| `apps/desktop` | Inventory actual client extension needs and current coverage; do not assume Web registration automatically applies |
| Store, CAS, Recorder and provenance | Settings transactions, frozen composition metadata and historical readability |
| Build and architecture checks | Package exports, dependency cycles, distribution completeness and browser-safe entry points |

## Test Design and Test Plan

The following cases are proposed validation requirements for follow-up implementation. They are not claims of tests executed by this analysis. Map each case to existing coverage first, then identify additions.

| Layer / case | Setup or action | Expected result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit: dependency validation | Missing/disabled dependency, duplicate ID, dependency cycle or incompatible service | Deterministic failure before unsupported contributions execute; useful plugin-specific diagnostic |
| Unit: lifecycle failure | Factory/start throws after earlier instances acquire resources | Created resources released once in reverse order; cleanup failures remain observable |
| Unit: cancellation | Cancel during start or tool execution, then dispose | Cancellation reaches async work; no remaining listeners, timers or child work |
| Unit: configuration | Combine global/project/session overrides, including explicit disable and inheritance | Correct effective settings; invalid fields rejected; existing Run stays unchanged |
| Unit: conflicts | Register duplicate tool names or competing policies/result owners | The documented conflict rule is enforced deterministically |
| Unit: state projection | Change live state after checkpoint capture; supply missing or incompatible state | Context and Recorder use the fixed checkpoint; incompatible state fails explicitly |
| Integration: backend matrix | Exercise each contribution through native and JiuwenSwarm | Supported contributions have observable effects; unsupported combinations produce explicit diagnostics |
| Integration: scope consistency | Start main, child and reviewer agents; change settings mid-Run | All use the frozen selection; only subsequent Runs use new settings |
| Integration: settings writes | Concurrent updates and stale expectedRevision through existing write paths | Existing transaction/CAS behavior preserved; conflicts do not partially apply configuration |
| Integration: package boundaries | Build API/client entries and run dependency checks | No reverse host imports, package cycles, duplicate registration or Node-only imports in browser entries |
| E2E: enable/disable journey | Configure a capability → run → disable → start another Run → open previous output | Disabled capability contributes no new execution; historical Plan/artifacts remain readable |
| E2E: clients | Exercise supported settings/view paths through Web and desktop | Scope and authorization preserved; client support gaps documented rather than silently hidden |
| Upgrade/recovery | Load a historical checkpoint after a plugin/schema change or failed upgrade | Supported migration/read path succeeds; unsupported versions fail clearly without corrupting history |

For implementation follow-ups, select affected UT/ST/E2E suites and run `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm architecture:check`, and affected builds. Record exact commands, results, and backend evidence. Real model/connector journeys are required only where mocks cannot establish backend or external execution semantics. Documentation-only analysis does not claim runtime validation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Publish a source-linked inventory of implemented extension points, registration paths and remaining coupling, including Web/desktop coverage.
- [ ] Publish a native/JiuwenSwarm contribution matrix with evidence, unsupported cases and links to follow-up gaps; coordinate backend findings with #572.
- [ ] Record an architecture decision comparing the three options in migration cost, security, deployment, compatibility and maintenance; explain the chosen scope and rejected alternatives.
- [ ] Define lifecycle ownership, in-flight work handling, conflict rules, settings consistency, Run version freezing and historical state compatibility.
- [ ] Describe one minimal capability integration end to end: package exports, installation, Ports, contributions, UI entry, build and verification.
- [ ] Map the test cases above to existing tests and proposed additions, with observable pass/fail conditions and responsible modules.
- [ ] Break implementation into bounded follow-up issues with dependencies, migration/rollback considerations and validation gates.
- [ ] Review the proposal against existing permission, approval, storage and execution semantics; unresolved decisions have explicit owners and follow-up items.

## Additional Information

- Current architecture: `docs/en/developer-docs/plugins.md` and `docs/zh/developer-docs/plugins.md`.
- #572 covers remaining plugin delivery/acceptance for JiuwenSwarm reuse; reuse its findings without duplicating implementation scope.
- Dynamic package installation, plugin marketplaces, untrusted in-process code, and arbitrary live AgentLoop mutation are outside this issue's implementation scope; any future adoption requires a separate reviewed proposal.

issue:798.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

The desktop app (`apps/desktop`, Electron + React) is the primary client, but program evolution (evolve) can only be designed, started, and watched from the web UI or the CLI via `/evolve-design`. Evolve is the one capability that keeps running after the turn that started it and keeps producing candidates: a user needs one surface to design the search, confirm its checkpoints, watch it live, inspect candidates and scores, and return to a finished search later. The desktop app has no such entry point or panel, so users must switch to the web client.

This issue tracks the full desktop delivery: the design entry point, checkpoints, the live panel, and result inspection, with the official tutorial's sample as the acceptance path.

Related issues: checkpoint token budget #780, natural-language entry point #310, `/evolve` documentation #55 / #567, desktop client delivery #400.

Related pull request: #715 — budget for the thinking a model cannot be told to stop (closes #780). It is the source of the per-call ceiling the checkpoint cards show.

## Design Ideas

- **A confirmation switch, chosen up front.** A toggle at the very start of the flow decides whether the checkpoints require a human confirmation. When it is off, the agent runs the remaining checkpoints and launches the search in one pass without stopping to wait; when it is on, each checkpoint pauses for confirmation as described below. The switch is set before anything is designed, so the user decides the pace once, not at every checkpoint.
- **Conversation-first.** No configuration form is added. `/evolve-design` opens the algorithm picker and a create dialog that collects only the two things a person knows — what should get better, and which search fits the problem — then hands that sentence to the conversation as the command it would have typed. The agent still designs the plan and scorecard and runs the checkpoints in the session.
- **Checkpoints stay in the conversation.** The four checkpoints (requirements, evaluation, scale, launch) appear as cards in the message stream; the user confirms or edits them there instead of navigating to another page.
- **A persistent session shelf.** A thin row under the session header lists the session's searches (running and finished); closing the panel never makes a running search unreachable, and a session that never used evolve renders nothing.
- **A result cockpit.** The panel answers the questions a person watching a search actually asks, in order: did it get better (best score), how did it get there (chart), what did it try (candidate table), why was that one rejected (inspector). On a narrow window the inspector becomes a drawer over the table.
- **Runtime install up front.** A first-time install of the evolve runtime happens inside the create dialog, not after the user has written a whole goal.
- **Events first, polling as fallback.** Subscribe to the evolve SSE stream; fall back to polling the run list when the stream is unavailable, and make an idle session cost nothing.

Alternatives considered and rejected: embedding the web page inside the desktop shell (splits interaction and state handling, and ships the whole web bundle), and a standalone search window (a search belongs to a session; a separate window makes both "return to the conversation" and "start another search" awkward).

## Involved Public APIs

No new public API. The desktop app reuses the existing evolve REST/SSE routes (runtime status, init, run list and detail, candidates, event stream), wrapped in `apps/desktop/src/api/evolve.ts`. The shared `EvolveRun` and evolve event types come from `packages/schema`, the same ones the web client uses. Any route change must keep the web client and CLI behavior unchanged and be described here.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `packages/schema`: evolve run and event types; the desktop app does not duplicate them.
- Desktop run pipeline: `run-stream` model and reducer must carry checkpoint and evolve state without disturbing text placement in ordinary conversations.
- Internationalization: every new string lands in both `text/zh.ts` and `text/en.ts`.
- The web evolve dashboard reads the same data; any behavioral difference between the two surfaces must be deliberate and documented.
- End-to-end tests: the desktop e2e fixtures need a mocked evolve runtime.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- **Unit tests:** command parsing (`/evolve-design`, the algorithm flag, a seeded goal); run status and label mapping; candidate reduction and best score; shelf folding (a running search is never folded away).
- **Component tests:** the create dialog's runtime install and error path; checkpoint cards; panel selection (clicking a row fills the inspector); the narrow-window drawer.
- **End-to-end (`apps/desktop/e2e/evolve.spec.ts`, mocked runtime):** start a search from a session → checkpoints → run → live updates → select a candidate and inspect it → stop; plus a session with no search rendering exactly as before.
- **Two complex math smoke cases:** (a) symbolic regression — recover a closed-form expression for a nonlinear function from sampled points, scored by fit error; (b) numerical optimization — improve a numerical routine's accuracy or runtime (for example an ODE integrator or a linear solver), scored by error against a reference. In each case the pass bar is that evolve triggers normally and runs through several nodes (at least three expansions with recorded candidates); the full search does not have to finish.
- **Regression:** the web evolve dashboard and the CLI behave unchanged; ordinary sessions keep their text placement, tool cards, and artifact panel.

Commands that must pass: `pnpm check` (typecheck and unit tests); `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` in `apps/desktop`; the desktop e2e suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The sample in the Evolve tutorial runs successfully: complete one PUCT search from the desktop app following `docs/en/domains/evolve-a-solution.md` (Chinese: `docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`) — design checkpoints, launch, watch live, finish, and open the result.
- [ ] The UI design passes review: the create dialog, checkpoint cards, session shelf, and result panel are reviewed against the agreed design and all review comments are closed.
- [ ] A session with no search looks exactly as it did before the change.
- [ ] Commands that must pass: `pnpm check`; `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` in `apps/desktop`; the desktop e2e suite.

## Additional Information

Tutorial sample: `docs/en/domains/evolve-a-solution.md` (Chinese: `docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`). The implementation lives in the desktop worktree, and the panel follows the existing session shell and settings visual language.

---

## 🚀 背景描述

桌面端（`apps/desktop`，Electron + React）是主要客户端，但程序演进（evolve）目前只能在 Web 界面或命令行里通过 `/evolve-design` 完成设计、启动和观察。evolve 是唯一一个在对话结束后仍在后台运行、并且会持续产生候选产物的能力：用户需要在一个界面里完成方案设计、确认检查点、实时观察搜索、查看候选与得分，并随时回到已结束的搜索。桌面端缺少这套入口和面板，用户必须切到 Web 才能使用。

本 issue 跟踪桌面端支持 evolve 的完整交付，覆盖设计入口、检查点、实时面板与结果查看，并以官方教程中的样例作为验收路径。

相关 issue：evolve 检查点的预算展示 #780、自然语言入口 #310、`/evolve` 文档 #55 / #567、桌面客户端交付 #400。

相关 PR：#715——为无法被要求停止思考的模型预留预算（关闭 #780）。检查点卡片展示的单次调用上限即来自该改动。

## 设计思路

- **人工确认开关（开始时选定）**：流程最开始提供一个开关，决定检查点是否需要人工确认。关闭时，Agent 一次跑完余下的检查点并直接启动搜索，中途不停下等待；开启时，每个检查点仍按下面的方式暂停等待确认。开关在设计开始前就确定，用户只需决定一次节奏，而不是在每个检查点重复决定。
- **对话优先**：不新增配置表单。`/evolve-design` 打开算法选择器与创建对话框，只收集两件人真正知道的事——想让什么变好、哪种搜索适合这个问题——然后把这句话作为命令送进对话；方案、评分卡与检查点仍由 Agent 在会话中完成。
- **检查点留在对话里**：需求、评测、规模、启动四个检查点以卡片形式出现在消息流中，用户在对话里确认或修改，不跳到另一个页面。
- **常驻会话书架**：会话头部下方一条细书架列出该会话的搜索（运行中与已结束）；关闭面板不会让运行中的搜索不可达，没有搜索的会话不显示任何东西。
- **结果驾驶舱**：面板按观察搜索的人真正会问的顺序回答——有没有变好（最优分数）、怎么变的（曲线）、试过什么（候选表）、为什么没选那个（检查器）。窄窗口时检查器变为覆盖在表格上的抽屉。
- **运行时安装前置**：首次安装 evolve 运行时在创建对话框内完成，而不是写完全部目标后才发现没装。
- **事件优先、轮询兜底**：优先订阅 evolve SSE 事件；流不可用时退回运行列表轮询，空闲会话不产生请求。

考虑过但未采用的方案：在桌面端内嵌 Web 页面（交互与状态处理被割裂，且会带上整份 Web 资源）；单开一个独立搜索窗口（搜索属于会话，独立窗口会让"回到会话"和"再开一个搜索"都变得别扭）。

## 涉及的公共 API

不新增公共 API。桌面端复用现有的 evolve REST/SSE 接口（运行时状态、初始化、运行列表与详情、候选、事件流），客户端封装在 `apps/desktop/src/api/evolve.ts`。共享类型 `EvolveRun` 与 evolve 事件来自 `packages/schema`，与 Web 端使用同一份定义。任何接口调整都必须保持 Web 端与命令行行为不变，并在本 issue 中说明。

## 与其他模块的关联

- `packages/schema`：evolve 运行与事件类型；桌面端不复制定义。
- 桌面端运行流水线：`run-stream` 的模型与 reducer 需要承载检查点与演进状态，同时不能打乱普通对话的文本归位。
- 国际化：新增文案同时进入 `text/zh.ts` 与 `text/en.ts`。
- Web 端演进面板读取同一份数据；两套界面之间的行为差异必须是有意为之并记录下来。
- 端到端测试：桌面 e2e 的 fixture 需要模拟的 evolve 运行时。

## 测试设计与测试计划

- **单元测试**：命令解析（`/evolve-design`、算法参数、带初始目标的命令）；运行状态与文案映射；候选归并与最优分数；书架折叠规则（运行中的搜索永不折叠）。
- **组件测试**：创建对话框的运行时安装与错误路径；检查点卡片；面板选择语义（点击一行填充检查器）；窄窗口抽屉。
- **端到端（`apps/desktop/e2e/evolve.spec.ts`，模拟运行时）**：从会话发起搜索 → 检查点 → 运行 → 实时更新 → 选择候选并查看检查器 → 停止；另外验证没有搜索的会话与改动前完全一致。
- **两个复杂数学冒烟用例**：（a）符号回归——从采样点恢复某非线性函数的闭式表达式，按拟合误差评分；（b）数值优化——改进某个数值例程的精度或耗时（例如 ODE 积分器或线性求解器），按与参考解的误差评分。两个用例的通过标准都是 evolve 正常触发、并能跑过若干节点（至少三次扩展且有候选记录），不要求完整跑完整个搜索。
- **回归**：Web 端演进面板与命令行行为不变；普通会话的文本归位、工具卡片与产物面板不受影响。

必须通过的命令：`pnpm check`（类型检查与单元测试）；`apps/desktop` 下的 `npm run typecheck` 与 `npm test`；桌面 e2e 套件。

## 验收标准

- [ ] 成功运行 evolve 介绍文档中的样例：在桌面端按 `docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`（英文版 `docs/en/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`）完整走完一次 PUCT 搜索——设计检查点、启动、实时观察、结束并打开结果。
- [ ] UI 设计通过评审：创建对话框、检查点卡片、会话书架、结果面板均通过对照设计稿的评审，评审意见全部关闭。
- [ ] 没有搜索的会话在界面上与改动前完全一致。
- [ ] 必须通过的命令：`pnpm check`；`apps/desktop` 下的 `npm run typecheck` 与 `npm test`；桌面 e2e 套件。

## 补充信息

教程样例：`docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`（英文 `docs/en/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`）。实现在桌面端工作树中进行，面板沿用现有的会话外壳与设置页视觉规范。

issue:799.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

**Start point — what a user actually waits today.** On installed builds, the first message of a session takes **~60–135s** (field measurements from our Windows-desktop tracker: ~85s typical, ~135s on a fresh-install cold boot), while the same-session second message takes **~6s**. Every boot profile — cold first boot, warm restart, or a new session in a running app — pays the same kind of first-message tax.

**What the tax is made of** (log-line-timed decomposition, dev stack + field forensics):

| Chunk | Size | Owner | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| MCP catalog cold-start | **~48s** (zero once warm) | **SD side** | the bundled stdio MCP servers spawn and enumerate tools on the catalog's first refresh; a fresh install delays that refresh to the first chat run. Verified locally: catalog warmed at boot → first message pays zero here. |
| SD-side run preparation | **~14s** | SD API | serial RPC chain per run (`skills.list` ×3, `permissions.tools.update`, per-run MCP re-registration) plus API acceptance (~4s) |
| Session assembly | **~5.3s** warm / ~17s pre-0015 | JiuwenSwarm | per-session `create_instance`; the 0015–0017 patches already moved the ~5.2s import tax off this path |
| Tool-schema handling | **~7–8s every turn** | upstream default | ~72 tool definitions ≈ 28k input tokens ride every model call (`progressive_tool_enabled=false`; #582 measured the same) |
| Model network/TTFT + machine tax | remainder | — | real model latency, cold-file reads, antivirus scanning on installed machines |

**Where the "26.09s" figure belongs** (an earlier draft of this issue wrongly led with it): it is an **anatomy anchor, not the user-facing start point** — a dev-stack first message measured with a *warm catalog* and a *mock model*, versus 8.67s for the second message. Its only purpose is attributing each chunk to its owning side: it proves the 48s chunk is the SD catalog (JW `reconcile` only opens one local loopback shared-tools server, milliseconds), and it sizes the SD-side run-preparation chain. Quoting it as the baseline would understate the real-world problem by the catalog chunk and the model time.

**End point (expected, to be replaced by packaged A/B measurements).** With the full plan below landed: first message **6–10s** on a warm-restart profile (vs ~60–135s today), second message ~5s (vs ~6s), cold-install first message no longer carrying the ~48s catalog chunk. Total optimization space: **~50–120s off the first message, plus ~3.5s off every subsequent turn**.

Related upstream context: #582 documented the input-side half (72 tools ≈ 28k tokens on a short "你好"); jiuwenswarm has adjacent requests openJiuwen-ai/jiuwenswarm#6683 (on-demand MCP registration), #7101 (request-level MCP registration failure bypass), #9938 (blocking snapshot out of the chat data plane).

## Design Ideas

Ordered by measured value. Options already invalidated by measurement are recorded so the discussion does not restart them.

1. **S1 — Warm the MCP catalog right after agent-ready** (implemented in this repo's desktop shell; PR to follow).
   The shell's `watchAgentReady` already probes `/agent/info`. The moment `jiuwenswarm.reachable` turns true it now issues `GET /api/mcp/sources` in the background — the exact request the MCP settings page uses to refresh the catalog. The stdio spawns and tool enumeration then overlap the user's "ready screen" time instead of the first message. Best-effort: failures are logged to `shell.log` only; if the warmup loses the race the run path re-runs the same steps, so behaviour never forks.
   Direct evidence: catalog refreshed at boot → first message at +3min paid **zero** MCP chunk.

2. **S3 — Trim the per-run preparation chain in the control API** (planned, highest remaining value in the warm-catalog scenario).
   `executeAgentRun`'s head runs a serial RPC chain against JiuwenSwarm before `chat.send`: `skills.list` ×3 (~4s in the anatomy anchor), permission updates, and per-run MCP re-registration (~1–2s). Candidates: cache the skills list with invalidation on skill-set changes, collapse the three lists into one, and let the API prove "tool table unchanged" so the adapter skips its re-registration round trips. Session-creation-time pre-warm follows once the chain is idempotent.

3. **J2 — Progressive tool exposure** (needs upstream discussion; JiuwenSwarm native).
   `DEFAULT_PROGRESSIVE_TOOL_ENABLED=False` sends all ~72 tool schemas on every call (~28k tokens; ~7s of per-turn cost under a mock endpoint — not model time). Enabling the existing `ProgressiveToolRail` with a small direct-exposure whitelist would cut input tokens ~3× on **every** turn, first and subsequent. Upstream note: the constant's comment/docstring already says "enabled by default" while the code returns `False` — the drift is a low-controversy entry point. Recall-rate validation on real tasks is required before flipping any default.

4. **J3 — Session-assembly warm pool** (second batch).
   Extend the existing `AgentWarmPool` so the per-session adapter is pre-built on session create; measured remaining value ~5.3s → ~1–2s on hit, with a mandatory seamless fallback to today's full path.

**Invalidated by measurement (recorded to save re-litigating):**
- *J1 — concurrent MCP connect with timeouts in JW*: the JW-side reconcile only opens one local loopback server (ms-level); the 48s was the SD catalog. Kept only as a small upstream-hygiene proposal.
- *S2 — adapter-side pre-registration at lifespan*: the tool table is assembled by the control API per run and handed over `/agent/runs`; the adapter has no table to pre-register at startup, and an empty pre-registration would force a generation bump on the first real run.

## Involved Public APIs

- Existing: `GET /api/mcp/sources` (MCP settings page's refresh endpoint; now also called by the shell after agent-ready).
- No new HTTP APIs, IPC channels or configuration surfaces in S1. S3 may add an internal invalidation signal for the skills cache; any new surface will be listed in its PR.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `win_desktop`: shell `watchAgentReady` warmup hook + `first-chat-warmup.ts` (new, unit-tested).
- `services/api`: S3 target — `executeAgentRun` head, `jiuwenswarm-skills.ts` reconcile chain.
- `services/adapter`: `ensure_shared_tools` already diffs tool tables; S3 may hand it an "unchanged" fast path proof.
- JiuwenSwarm patches (`jiuwen_swarm/patches/`): no new patches for S1/S3; J3 would land as patch 0020+ (numbering shared with a parallel packaging workstream).
- `apps/desktop`: no UI change; the ready screen timing is unchanged.
- #582 (input-token analysis): complementary — J2 addresses that input directly.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- **S1 (landed in branch)**: unit tests for URL/header construction and timeout (`win_desktop/test/first-chat-warmup.test.ts`); full shell suite 116/116 green; `win_desktop` builds clean (esbuild + tsc).
- **Integration A/B** (per change, D5 measurement discipline): dev stack, mock OpenAI endpoint on loopback, `agent_server.log` line-timestamped segmentation; baseline vs change measured in the **same host-load window** (parallel packaging builds invalidate absolute numbers); first message of a fresh session vs second message of the same session, median of 3.
- **Cold-scenario check**: with the MCP catalog forcibly cold (fresh data dir), confirm the shell warmup completes before a human-plausible first message and the first run no longer contains the stdio-spawn chunk.
- **Regression**: shell build + full shell suite; `pnpm test` for the api package after S3; JiuwenSwarm smoke (gateway / agentserver / main chat / memory) where patches are touched.
- **Packaged validation**: GUI-interactive install (per project rule, no `/S`), three boot profiles (cold first boot / warm restart / attach) with first-message timing recorded and the second message non-regressed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Shell warmup: after `jiuwenswarm.reachable` becomes true, `shell.log` shows `[warmup] first-chat /api/mcp/sources -> 200` (or a failure line) without any change to the ready-screen timing or user-visible behaviour. Warmup failure never surfaces to the user.
- Cold-install first message no longer contains the stdio-spawn/tool-enumeration chunk (field: ~48s of the 60–135s).
- Warm-restart first message: field baseline ~60–135s → **≤20s after S1+S3** 【expected, replaced by packaged A/B】 → **6–10s after the full plan** 【expected】; second message ~6s not regressed beyond noise, trending to ~5s with J2.
- Every-turn input: J2, where accepted upstream, cuts tool-schema tokens by ≥50% with zero regression on a fixed set of real-task scenarios (recall rate held).
- Commands that must pass: `pnpm --dir win_desktop build`, `node --test win_desktop/test/*.test.ts`, `pnpm test` (api/desktop scopes touched), plus the packaged three-profile run above.

## Additional Information

- Measurement note: anatomy-anchor numbers were taken while a parallel packaging build was running on the host; they may read 10–25% high. Field numbers (60–135s) are user-measured and unaffected. The structural findings (chunk boundaries, catalog-warm ⇒ zero MCP chunk, JW loopback being ms-level) are load-independent. A/B pairs are always measured within one load window.
- Revision note (2026-11-03): this body was re-aligned after review — the original draft led with the 26.09s anatomy anchor as the baseline, which understated the user-facing start point. The start point is now the field measurement (~60–135s); the 26.09s figure is kept only as the internal attribution anchor it was measured to be.
- E1 evidence pack (internal): session-creation timestamped `agent_server.log` segmentation, mock endpoint fixture, and the run-preparation RPC chain listing are archived in the workstream's knowledge base.

issue:8.body:
### 🚀 背景描述

ScienceDiscovery 已通过 operational logger 将服务日志写入数据目录下的 `logs/`，默认位置为 `.sciencediscovery-data/logs/`。其中 `api.log` 已包含 API 启动、部分组件状态与未分类异常，`runner.log` 记录 Runner 请求和沙箱执行，`run.log` 记录 Agent Run 生命周期。

当前缺口集中在 **Agent/LLM 看不到的框架内部链路**：

- MCP 客户端连接、重连、关闭及工具目录加载缺少完整的成功/失败日志；
- MCP stdio 子进程的 stderr 被忽略，进程启动或协议握手失败时缺少服务端原始线索；
- MCP 代理配置解析和运行时切换存在静默失败，且日志无法区分“配置了代理”和“当前传输实际应用代理”；
- 远端 Runner 的主机探测、直连、断线与 SSH 隧道错误主要停留在内存状态中，进程退出后难以追溯；
- 启动阶段部分组件初始化失败缺少统一、可检索的阶段事件。

本功能的目标是复用现有滚动日志，为这些框架链路补齐结构化、可关联、经过脱敏且有体积上限的诊断事件，让开发人员在 MCP、代理、远端 Runner 或启动组件发生故障时，能够仅通过日志定位失败阶段、目标、错误类别、耗时和重试情况。

本方案不是 Agent 操作审计能力，不要求 Agent 或 LLM 感知这些日志。

### 设计思路

#### 1. 存储与日志形式

- 复用现有 `<dataDir>/logs/api.log`，默认即 `.sciencediscovery-data/logs/api.log`；
- 继续使用 operational logger 的文本行格式、级别过滤和滚动策略；
- 沿用 `SCIENCE_AGENT_LOG_LEVEL`、`SCIENCE_AGENT_LOG_DIR`、`SCIENCE_AGENT_LOG_MAX_BYTES`、`SCIENCE_AGENT_LOG_MAX_BACKUPS` 配置；
- 默认单文件上限 10 MiB、保留 5 个备份；
- 不新增独立 audit JSONL、日志索引、日志文件清单、数据库表或 UI。

日志事件采用稳定事件名和扁平字段，例如：

```text
2026-09-10T08:00:00.000Z INFO [api] event=mcp.connection.succeeded serverId=... transport=stdio durationMs=42
```

#### 2. 覆盖范围

| 链路 | 需要记录的事件 | 关键字段 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 框架启动 | 组件初始化开始、成功、失败 | `component`、`durationMs`、`errorCode`、`error` |
| MCP 连接 | 开始、成功、失败、关闭、关闭失败 | `serverId`、`transport`、`endpointProtocol`、`endpointHost`、`durationMs` |
| MCP 工具目录 | 全部加载成功、单服务加载失败 | `serverId`、`toolCount`、`errorCode`、`error` |
| MCP 代理 | 配置加载、配置变更、解析失败 | `proxyMode`、`proxyApplied`、代理协议与主机 |
| MCP 调用 | 非语义性传输/服务端/超时/限流失败及重试调度 | `serverId`、`toolName`、`requestId`、`attempt`、`delayMs`、`errorCode` |
| 远端主机 | SSH 主机探测开始、成功、失败 | `hostId`、`host`、`port`、`durationMs`、`errorCode` |
| 远端 Runner | 连接开始、成功、失败、断线、关闭 | `runnerId`、`connectionMode`、`endpointHost`、`durationMs` |
| SSH 隧道 | 转发、stream、socket 失败 | `hostId`、`runnerId`、`errorCode`、`error` |

启动组件首批覆盖 Skill Catalog、自定义 MCP Server、Session Store、Artifact 恢复和 Run 恢复。已有 Runner、Memory Graph 等模块的日志继续使用原通道，本功能不重复记录其业务载荷。

#### 3. MCP stdio stderr

MCP stdio 子进程的 stderr 从忽略改为受控采集：

- 内存中最多保留 4 KiB 尾部，避免持续输出导致内存增长；
- 仅在连接、调用或关闭失败时附带最后 4 个非空行；
- 单条日志中的 stderr 摘要不超过 1 KiB；
- 成功路径不输出 stderr 内容；
- 摘要进入日志前执行统一脱敏。

该内容用于保留 MCP Server 自身的启动报错、依赖缺失、协议错误等直接证据，同时避免把完整进程输出写入日志。

#### 4. 代理语义

日志必须区分：

- `proxyMode`：当前解析到的代理配置模式；
- `proxyApplied`：当前 MCP transport 是否实际应用了该代理。

例如 stdio transport 不经过 HTTP 代理；HTTP/SSE transport 若底层实现尚未接入代理，也不能仅因存在代理配置就记录为已应用。日志只记录代理协议和主机，不记录完整 URL、用户名、密码或敏感查询参数。

#### 5. 脱敏、体积与可靠性边界

- 统一通过 `redactLogValue` 处理日志字段；
- 脱敏 Authorization/Bearer、token、secret、password、cookie、URL userinfo 及敏感 query 参数；
- 不记录 `args`、`body`、`content`、`input`、`messages`、`output`、`prompt`、`request`、`response`、完整 stdout/stderr 等大载荷；
- 错误消息及 stderr 摘要设置明确长度上限；
- 用户会话内容、模型输入输出、工具参数、工具结果正文不进入框架诊断日志；
- operational logger 保持 best-effort，日志目录创建、写入或轮转失败不能打断服务主路径。

#### 6. 代码落点

- `services/api/src/bootstrap/platform.ts`：框架组件初始化，以及 MCP/远端计算 logger 注入；
- `services/api/src/mcp/node-client.ts`：MCP 连接、目录、代理、调用重试与受控 stderr；
- `packages/executor/src/remote-compute.ts`：主机探测、远端 Runner 与 SSH 隧道生命周期；
- `packages/operational-logging/src/index.ts`：URL 凭据和敏感查询参数脱敏。

#### 7. 明确不在本功能范围内

- 不提供日志查看、搜索或下载 UI；
- 不生成日志索引或所有日志文件的清单；
- 不新增 Agent 可见事件，也不改变 Agent、Tool、MCP 的业务返回值；
- 不把用户会话、LLM 请求/响应、工具输入/输出复制到框架日志；
- 不实现代理健康检查、自动故障转移或代理管理面板；
- 不将本日志定义为不可篡改的合规审计账本；
- 不在本轮扩展 Paper Worker、模型供应商 SDK、Web Search 或 Memory Graph 的业务级事件。若后续确认这些模块存在框架故障不可定位的缺口，再分别补充稳定事件。

### 涉及到的对外API

无对外 API、SSE schema 或 UI 变更。

内部构造接口增加可选的结构化 logger 注入：

- MCP Node Client 使用 API 现有 operational logger；
- Remote Compute 依赖最小 `info/warn/error` logger 契约，避免 executor package 反向依赖 service；
- 未注入 logger 时保持兼容，不改变已有调用行为。

运维侧继续使用现有日志环境变量，不增加新的必填配置。

### 与其他模块的相关性描述

- `services/api`：作为 composition root 注入已有 operational logger，并记录启动阶段和基础设施 adapter 的生命周期；
- `packages/executor`：通过最小 logger 接口记录 Remote Compute 生命周期，不反向依赖 API service；
- `packages/operational-logging`：继续负责文件写入、级别过滤、轮转和集中脱敏；
- MCP Tool Registry、Agent Runtime、SSE 与 UI：业务接口和事件 schema 不变，不接收本功能新增的框架诊断事件；
- Runner 与 Memory Graph：保留各自已有日志通道，不将既有业务日志重复写入 `api.log`。

### 测试设计与测试计划

#### 功能测试

- [ ] API 启动成功时，组件初始化产生 start/ready 事件并包含耗时；初始化失败时产生 failed 事件且原异常行为不变；
- [ ] MCP stdio Server 正常连接、加载工具目录和关闭时，事件顺序及 `serverId`、`transport`、`durationMs` 正确；
- [ ] MCP Server 不存在、握手失败或调用失败时，记录错误码、有限错误消息和重试信息；
- [ ] MCP stdio 子进程输出大量 stderr 时，仅保留 4 KiB 尾部，失败日志最多包含最后 4 行/1 KiB；成功日志不泄露 stderr；
- [ ] HTTP/SSE/stdio 各 transport 的 `proxyMode` 与 `proxyApplied` 符合真实应用情况；运行时代理变更产生变更事件；
- [ ] 远端 Runner 直连成功、连接失败、断线和关闭均产生对应事件；
- [ ] SSH 主机探测及隧道 forward/stream/socket 失败包含可关联的 `hostId`/`runnerId`。

#### 安全与可靠性测试

- [ ] URL 中的用户名、密码、token/secret 等查询参数不可出现在日志；
- [ ] Authorization/Bearer、password、cookie 等敏感字段不可出现在日志；
- [ ] 工具参数、响应正文、用户会话和 LLM 内容不进入框架日志；
- [ ] 错误消息、stderr 和重复事件在极端输入下不会突破体积边界；
- [ ] 日志写入与轮转失败不会改变 MCP、远端 Runner 或 API 初始化主路径结果；
- [ ] 轮转继续遵守 `maxBytes`/`maxBackups` 配置。

#### 工程验证

- [ ] MCP、Remote Compute、operational logging 定向单测通过；
- [ ] `packages/operational-logging`、`packages/executor`、`services/api` 类型检查通过；
- [ ] 架构依赖检查通过，executor 不反向依赖 API service；
- [ ] 在 Linux/WSL 环境完成涉及真实子进程与文件轮转的回归验证。

## 🚀 Background Description

The desktop UI (`apps/desktop`) has four waits a user feels, and on a real
workspace all but one of them were slow. Measured on the live catalog behind
the work in #699 — 71,000 provenance records, 39 subagents, 500 workspace
files — with the catalog, artifact-listing, deletion and CAS changes reverted:

| Flow | Scale | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Switch to a Session | 70,000 provenance rows, 500 files | 4.7 s | 2.0 s first visit (1.7–4.1 s across runs), 0.24 s warm |
| Delete a Session | 2,000 messages, 3,000 files | 8.1 s | 70 ms |
| Delete its Project | ten such Sessions | 14.4 s | 304 ms |
| Open a Settings list | empty Project | 17 ms | 16 ms |

Switching sessions took several seconds and the sequence of subagents looked
stuck; deleting a Session or a Project was the request users describe as a
hang. Opening 技能 / MCP 服务器 / 专家 was fast but always drew the dashed
`正在读取…` frame first, so the pane looked like it reloaded from scratch on
every visit — the reason the Settings dialog felt slower than other agent
platforms, whose settings open instantly.

The cause was structural, not a slow query: every write rewrote the whole
catalog, and delete requests reclaimed the Session's data before answering.
Settings panes had no memory: the dialog unmounts a pane when another group is
selected, so every visit started from an empty `useLoaded`.

## Design Ideas

- **Write path (#699).** Stop rewriting the catalog on every write; commit the
  catalog entry and reconcile artifacts behind it.
- **Deletion (#699).** Answer the delete when the catalog commits, then
  reclaim the Session's data in the background.
- **Settings paint (#796).** Keep each page's last answer beside its client
  (`WeakMap<client, Map<key, value>>`, the shape `apps/web/src/settings-cache.ts`
  already uses), seed the pane from it on mount, paint that value, and refresh
  behind it. Keys are per page; the Skills key carries the Project id because
  the enabled set is project-scoped. Pages whose first paint is a form the user
  is about to edit keep the loading gate.
- **Guards (#775).** Store-shape guards, a 10x save-latency ratio, and four
  wall-clock budgets so the regressions cannot come back unnoticed.

Alternatives considered and rejected: optimistic UI for settings writes (the
server owns the value, so a write must be computed from what the server
confirmed); a global spinner-free skeleton (still shows the user nothing on the
first visit); server push for deletions (does not remove the synchronous
reclaim from the request path).

## Involved Public APIs

No public API changes. The HTTP endpoints keep their shapes and semantics; the
only visible difference is timing — a delete response returns after the catalog
commits rather than after full reclamation, and settings list endpoints are read
from a client-side cache for the first paint.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `services/api` store, catalog, artifact listing and deletion paths.
- `apps/desktop` settings panes (技能, MCP 服务器, 专家) and `useLoaded`.
- `apps/web` — `settings-cache.ts` is the reference shape the desktop copy
  follows.
- Provenance index and workspace scanning, which the first session switch
  reconciles against.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- `services/api/src/performance-budget.test.ts`: the four flows above on a
  fixture (800 messages, 200 runs, 500 files; project case 6 × 200/20/100) with
  budgets of 1 s / 0.5 s / 1 s / 1.5 s. Against the pre-#699 store the two
  deletion cases fail their budgets (1,822 ms and 1,999 ms), so the guards
  would have caught the regression.
- `services/api/src/store-performance.test.ts`: catalog row growth under
  256 B, catalog under 64 KiB, side-table rows, 10x save-latency ratio.
- `apps/desktop/tests/settings-cache.test.tsx`: a remembered list paints
  without the loading frame; one client's list never paints under another; one
  Project's enabled Skills never paint as another's.
- `apps/desktop/e2e/settings-interactions.spec.ts`: holds the `/api/skills`
  response, switches 技能 → 专家 → 技能, and asserts the list is on screen while
  the refresh is still in flight.
- Full gates: `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, `pnpm ci:e2e`, `pnpm check`.

## Acceptance Criteria

Measured on the 71,000-record / 500-file catalog above, reverted baseline vs.
current build:

- [ ] Switching to a Session is at least **57% faster** on the first visit
      after a workspace change: **4.7 s → ≤ 2.0 s** (measured 2.0 s, 1.7–4.1 s
      across runs), and at least **94% faster** once warm: **0.24 s**.
- [ ] Deleting a Session (2,000 messages, 3,000 files) is at least **99%
      faster**: **8.1 s → ≤ 0.4 s** (measured 70 ms).
- [ ] Deleting that Session's Project (ten such Sessions) is at least **97%
      faster**: **14.4 s → ≤ 1.0 s** (measured 304 ms).
- [ ] Opening 技能 / MCP 服务器 / 专家 **shows the list instantly and loads in
      the background**: the last answer is painted on mount with no
      `正在读取…` frame, and the refresh replaces it when it lands. This
      scenario did not get faster (17 ms → 16 ms); the acceptance is the
      absence of the loading frame, not a percentage.
- [ ] The four wall-clock budgets in `performance-budget.test.ts` pass, and the
      pre-#699 store still fails the two deletion budgets.
- [ ] Command that must pass: `pnpm test:shared` (full CI plan); for the
      desktop scope, `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test` and
      `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck`.

## Additional Information

Implementation: #699 (merged), guards: #775, settings paint: #796.
