items.author: ink999107
items.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

The desktop app (`apps/desktop`, Electron + React) is the primary client, but program evolution (evolve) can only be designed, started, and watched from the web UI or the CLI via `/evolve-design`. Evolve is the one capability that keeps running after the turn that started it and keeps producing candidates: a user needs one surface to design the search, confirm its checkpoints, watch it live, inspect candidates and scores, and return to a finished search later. The desktop app has no such entry point or panel, so users must switch to the web client.

This issue tracks the full desktop delivery: the design entry point, checkpoints, the live panel, and result inspection, with the official tutorial's sample as the acceptance path.

Related issues: checkpoint token budget #780, natural-language entry point #310, `/evolve` documentation #55 / #567, desktop client delivery #400.

Related pull request: #715 — budget for the thinking a model cannot be told to stop (closes #780). It is the source of the per-call ceiling the checkpoint cards show.

## Design Ideas

- **A confirmation switch, chosen up front.** A toggle at the very start of the flow decides whether the checkpoints require a human confirmation. When it is off, the agent runs the remaining checkpoints and launches the search in one pass without stopping to wait; when it is on, each checkpoint pauses for confirmation as described below. The switch is set before anything is designed, so the user decides the pace once, not at every checkpoint.
- **Conversation-first.** No configuration form is added. `/evolve-design` opens the algorithm picker and a create dialog that collects only the two things a person knows — what should get better, and which search fits the problem — then hands that sentence to the conversation as the command it would have typed. The agent still designs the plan and scorecard and runs the checkpoints in the session.
- **Checkpoints stay in the conversation.** The four checkpoints (requirements, evaluation, scale, launch) appear as cards in the message stream; the user confirms or edits them there instead of navigating to another page.
- **A persistent session shelf.** A thin row under the session header lists the session's searches (running and finished); closing the panel never makes a running search unreachable, and a session that never used evolve renders nothing.
- **A result cockpit.** The panel answers the questions a person watching a search actually asks, in order: did it get better (best score), how did it get there (chart), what did it try (candidate table), why was that one rejected (inspector). On a narrow window the inspector becomes a drawer over the table.
- **Runtime install up front.** A first-time install of the evolve runtime happens inside the create dialog, not after the user has written a whole goal.
- **Events first, polling as fallback.** Subscribe to the evolve SSE stream; fall back to polling the run list when the stream is unavailable, and make an idle session cost nothing.

Alternatives considered and rejected: embedding the web page inside the desktop shell (splits interaction and state handling, and ships the whole web bundle), and a standalone search window (a search belongs to a session; a separate window makes both "return to the conversation" and "start another search" awkward).

## Involved Public APIs

No new public API. The desktop app reuses the existing evolve REST/SSE routes (runtime status, init, run list and detail, candidates, event stream), wrapped in `apps/desktop/src/api/evolve.ts`. The shared `EvolveRun` and evolve event types come from `packages/schema`, the same ones the web client uses. Any route change must keep the web client and CLI behavior unchanged and be described here.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `packages/schema`: evolve run and event types; the desktop app does not duplicate them.
- Desktop run pipeline: `run-stream` model and reducer must carry checkpoint and evolve state without disturbing text placement in ordinary conversations.
- Internationalization: every new string lands in both `text/zh.ts` and `text/en.ts`.
- The web evolve dashboard reads the same data; any behavioral difference between the two surfaces must be deliberate and documented.
- End-to-end tests: the desktop e2e fixtures need a mocked evolve runtime.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- **Unit tests:** command parsing (`/evolve-design`, the algorithm flag, a seeded goal); run status and label mapping; candidate reduction and best score; shelf folding (a running search is never folded away).
- **Component tests:** the create dialog's runtime install and error path; checkpoint cards; panel selection (clicking a row fills the inspector); the narrow-window drawer.
- **End-to-end (`apps/desktop/e2e/evolve.spec.ts`, mocked runtime):** start a search from a session → checkpoints → run → live updates → select a candidate and inspect it → stop; plus a session with no search rendering exactly as before.
- **Two complex math smoke cases:** (a) symbolic regression — recover a closed-form expression for a nonlinear function from sampled points, scored by fit error; (b) numerical optimization — improve a numerical routine's accuracy or runtime (for example an ODE integrator or a linear solver), scored by error against a reference. In each case the pass bar is that evolve triggers normally and runs through several nodes (at least three expansions with recorded candidates); the full search does not have to finish.
- **Regression:** the web evolve dashboard and the CLI behave unchanged; ordinary sessions keep their text placement, tool cards, and artifact panel.

Commands that must pass: `pnpm check` (typecheck and unit tests); `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` in `apps/desktop`; the desktop e2e suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The sample in the Evolve tutorial runs successfully: complete one PUCT search from the desktop app following `docs/en/domains/evolve-a-solution.md` (Chinese: `docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`) — design checkpoints, launch, watch live, finish, and open the result.
- [ ] The UI design passes review: the create dialog, checkpoint cards, session shelf, and result panel are reviewed against the agreed design and all review comments are closed.
- [ ] A session with no search looks exactly as it did before the change.
- [ ] Commands that must pass: `pnpm check`; `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` in `apps/desktop`; the desktop e2e suite.

## Additional Information

Tutorial sample: `docs/en/domains/evolve-a-solution.md` (Chinese: `docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`). The implementation lives in the desktop worktree, and the panel follows the existing session shell and settings visual language.

---

## 🚀 背景描述

桌面端（`apps/desktop`，Electron + React）是主要客户端，但程序演进（evolve）目前只能在 Web 界面或命令行里通过 `/evolve-design` 完成设计、启动和观察。evolve 是唯一一个在对话结束后仍在后台运行、并且会持续产生候选产物的能力：用户需要在一个界面里完成方案设计、确认检查点、实时观察搜索、查看候选与得分，并随时回到已结束的搜索。桌面端缺少这套入口和面板，用户必须切到 Web 才能使用。

本 issue 跟踪桌面端支持 evolve 的完整交付，覆盖设计入口、检查点、实时面板与结果查看，并以官方教程中的样例作为验收路径。

相关 issue：evolve 检查点的预算展示 #780、自然语言入口 #310、`/evolve` 文档 #55 / #567、桌面客户端交付 #400。

相关 PR：#715——为无法被要求停止思考的模型预留预算（关闭 #780）。检查点卡片展示的单次调用上限即来自该改动。

## 设计思路

- **人工确认开关（开始时选定）**：流程最开始提供一个开关，决定检查点是否需要人工确认。关闭时，Agent 一次跑完余下的检查点并直接启动搜索，中途不停下等待；开启时，每个检查点仍按下面的方式暂停等待确认。开关在设计开始前就确定，用户只需决定一次节奏，而不是在每个检查点重复决定。
- **对话优先**：不新增配置表单。`/evolve-design` 打开算法选择器与创建对话框，只收集两件人真正知道的事——想让什么变好、哪种搜索适合这个问题——然后把这句话作为命令送进对话；方案、评分卡与检查点仍由 Agent 在会话中完成。
- **检查点留在对话里**：需求、评测、规模、启动四个检查点以卡片形式出现在消息流中，用户在对话里确认或修改，不跳到另一个页面。
- **常驻会话书架**：会话头部下方一条细书架列出该会话的搜索（运行中与已结束）；关闭面板不会让运行中的搜索不可达，没有搜索的会话不显示任何东西。
- **结果驾驶舱**：面板按观察搜索的人真正会问的顺序回答——有没有变好（最优分数）、怎么变的（曲线）、试过什么（候选表）、为什么没选那个（检查器）。窄窗口时检查器变为覆盖在表格上的抽屉。
- **运行时安装前置**：首次安装 evolve 运行时在创建对话框内完成，而不是写完全部目标后才发现没装。
- **事件优先、轮询兜底**：优先订阅 evolve SSE 事件；流不可用时退回运行列表轮询，空闲会话不产生请求。

考虑过但未采用的方案：在桌面端内嵌 Web 页面（交互与状态处理被割裂，且会带上整份 Web 资源）；单开一个独立搜索窗口（搜索属于会话，独立窗口会让"回到会话"和"再开一个搜索"都变得别扭）。

## 涉及的公共 API

不新增公共 API。桌面端复用现有的 evolve REST/SSE 接口（运行时状态、初始化、运行列表与详情、候选、事件流），客户端封装在 `apps/desktop/src/api/evolve.ts`。共享类型 `EvolveRun` 与 evolve 事件来自 `packages/schema`，与 Web 端使用同一份定义。任何接口调整都必须保持 Web 端与命令行行为不变，并在本 issue 中说明。

## 与其他模块的关联

- `packages/schema`：evolve 运行与事件类型；桌面端不复制定义。
- 桌面端运行流水线：`run-stream` 的模型与 reducer 需要承载检查点与演进状态，同时不能打乱普通对话的文本归位。
- 国际化：新增文案同时进入 `text/zh.ts` 与 `text/en.ts`。
- Web 端演进面板读取同一份数据；两套界面之间的行为差异必须是有意为之并记录下来。
- 端到端测试：桌面 e2e 的 fixture 需要模拟的 evolve 运行时。

## 测试设计与测试计划

- **单元测试**：命令解析（`/evolve-design`、算法参数、带初始目标的命令）；运行状态与文案映射；候选归并与最优分数；书架折叠规则（运行中的搜索永不折叠）。
- **组件测试**：创建对话框的运行时安装与错误路径；检查点卡片；面板选择语义（点击一行填充检查器）；窄窗口抽屉。
- **端到端（`apps/desktop/e2e/evolve.spec.ts`，模拟运行时）**：从会话发起搜索 → 检查点 → 运行 → 实时更新 → 选择候选并查看检查器 → 停止；另外验证没有搜索的会话与改动前完全一致。
- **两个复杂数学冒烟用例**：（a）符号回归——从采样点恢复某非线性函数的闭式表达式，按拟合误差评分；（b）数值优化——改进某个数值例程的精度或耗时（例如 ODE 积分器或线性求解器），按与参考解的误差评分。两个用例的通过标准都是 evolve 正常触发、并能跑过若干节点（至少三次扩展且有候选记录），不要求完整跑完整个搜索。
- **回归**：Web 端演进面板与命令行行为不变；普通会话的文本归位、工具卡片与产物面板不受影响。

必须通过的命令：`pnpm check`（类型检查与单元测试）；`apps/desktop` 下的 `npm run typecheck` 与 `npm test`；桌面 e2e 套件。

## 验收标准

- [ ] 成功运行 evolve 介绍文档中的样例：在桌面端按 `docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`（英文版 `docs/en/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`）完整走完一次 PUCT 搜索——设计检查点、启动、实时观察、结束并打开结果。
- [ ] UI 设计通过评审：创建对话框、检查点卡片、会话书架、结果面板均通过对照设计稿的评审，评审意见全部关闭。
- [ ] 没有搜索的会话在界面上与改动前完全一致。
- [ ] 必须通过的命令：`pnpm check`；`apps/desktop` 下的 `npm run typecheck` 与 `npm test`；桌面 e2e 套件。

## 补充信息

教程样例：`docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`（英文 `docs/en/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`）。实现在桌面端工作树中进行，面板沿用现有的会话外壳与设置页视觉规范。

items.author: JinhZhao
items.body:
`packages/model/src/client.ts:171-174` already documents the problem:

> "A reasoning model bills its hidden thought against this same budget, so the default that is comfortable for a chat reply can be exhausted before the first visible character."

`packages/model/src/usage.ts:32-100` normalizes usage into `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `totalTokens` (plus cache fields), but does not extract `reasoning_tokens` from the API response — even though the raw response includes it (e.g., `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` for OpenAI-compatible, `output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` for Responses API). The test file (`usage.test.ts:15,17`) confirms the raw data is present but discarded during normalization.

For thinking-model workloads (GLM-Pro, DeepSeek R1, QwQ), this means:

1. The shared `maxTokens` budget (default 16,384) can be exhausted by reasoning alone, producing empty outputs
2. There is no visibility into how much of the budget reasoning consumed
3. Users cannot tune reasoning vs. output budgets independently

**Suggested fix:**

1. Extract `reasoning_tokens` from the API response into `NormalizedUsage` (e.g., a `reasoningTokens` field)
2. Consider separate budget configuration for reasoning and output tokens, or raise the default `maxTokens` for known reasoning models
3. Surface reasoning token consumption in run diagnostics so users can identify budget exhaustion

**Context:** Discovered during a 4-round evaluation of ScienceDiscovery for catalysis research workflows (44 runs, 2 models). Thinking-model runs (GLM-Pro) spent up to 60 minutes in planning loops where reasoning tokens consumed the entire budget before any visible output was produced.
items.title: [Feature] Token budget should separate reasoning and output tokens for thinking models

items.author: wyhohyw
items.body:
## Summary

Biomni real E2E shows large endpoint-dependent variation in model-request latency and total generation time. Earlier runs through an OpenAI-compatible relay also ended after a terminal model turn with no text or tool call. We need enough safe wire-level diagnostics to tell an upstream empty completion from an SSE/parser defect, and to separate model/API latency from agent work.

This is distinct from #232, which records explicit HTTP 500/503 gateway errors.

## Local measurements

The two Biomni cases were run in parallel on the same Windows/WSL machine, with evaluation disabled, the `task` tool removed (no subagents), and no Jina key. `generation` is the benchmark's generation duration; request timing is the elapsed time of completed `[model-stream]` requests in `stack.log`. All rows below passed delivery. The relay run used `https://yibuapi.com/v1` with model alias `deepseek-v4.1-flash`; the direct runs used `https://api.deepseek.com` with model alias `deepseek-flash`.

| Case | Endpoint / runs | Generation | Completed model requests | Median request | Reported total tokens |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DA-13-3 | relay, r5 | 37.46 min | 71 | 25.16 s | 504,634 |
| DA-13-3 | direct, r6/r7/r9/r10 | 5.71–20.67 min | 26–44 | 6.10–13.93 s | 118,066–140,022 |
| DA-14-1 | relay, r5 | 31.31 min | 63 | 20.18 s | 177,043 |
| DA-14-1 | direct, r6/r9/r10 | 20.75–35.79 min | 54–72 | 11.59–19.01 s | 191,883–284,635 |

The seven direct samples all passed delivery, with zero reported SSE parse errors or SSE error records. Earlier local relay samples had a normalized final model turn with empty text, no tool call, and `finish_reason=stop`, after which the run was marked completed without the expected deliverable. Those older samples did **not** retain raw SSE records, so they cannot establish whether the upstream service sent an empty completion or the local stream adapter lost content. The direct samples also used a local empty-turn guard and SSE parsing fixes, so the passing rate is **not** an isolated endpoint A/B result.

## Why the current evidence is insufficient

- The relay and direct runs used different model aliases. The model's chosen steps, request counts, and token totals varied substantially, so total-duration differences are not an estimate of API latency alone.
- Even with the same direct endpoint, DA-13-3 varied from 5.71 to 20.67 minutes, and DA-14-1 from 20.75 to 35.79 minutes. Agent behavior and task content remain major contributors.
- A normalized empty final turn does not reveal whether the wire response was empty, malformed, or incorrectly mapped locally.

## Requested investigation / acceptance criteria

1. Save privacy-safe per-request diagnostics in real E2E artifacts: endpoint identity and model alias, request ID, HTTP status, dispatch/headers/first byte/first SSE record/completion timestamps, SSE record and parse-error counts, final content/tool-call presence, `finish_reason`, and retry/error classification. Do not save credentials or prompt/response bodies in the default diagnostic log.
2. Treat an empty terminal assistant turn with no tool call as an error rather than a successful final answer. Preserve the upstream request ID and framing summary when this occurs.
3. Compare relay and direct endpoints with the same model, request body, workload, and concurrency. Report per-request latency distributions separately from total agent duration and token use.
4. In CI summaries, identify explicit provider failures, empty completions, and local parse/mapping failures separately from research-quality failures.

I can provide the local benchmark metrics and sanitized `[model-stream]`/`[model-sse-summary]` excerpts if useful. No API keys or prompt contents are included here.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claim-Id: 9d9ba398ccce4763b47f946f890661f6
Branch: dev2/fix/777-named-entity-decoding
Base: 7942ad1fd495cc623df67234d8a01201430da204
At: 2026-11-03T02:07:55Z

## ScienceDiscovery evidence-backed issue

**Live main:** `7942ad1fd495cc623df67234d8a01201430da204` (`test(cas): cover the multi-chunk intact layout and align the materialize contract with #708`)
**Area:** `packages/data-source` — HTML text extraction used by the free search engines
**Filed by:** ScienceDiscovery Product

### Problem

`decodeEntities` resolves only five named references (`amp`, `lt`, `gt`, `quot`, `nbsp`) and leaves every other named reference literal, so search-result titles and snippets reach the model and the report as `café`, `5–10`, `—`, `…`, `O'Brien`.

### Reproduction on live main

```
$ cd packages/data-source && node --experimental-strip-types -e '
  import("./src/web/native/html.ts").then(m => {
    for (const s of ["café — 5–10 … O'Brien", "&lt;b&gt; stays text", "♦ … ’"])
      console.log(JSON.stringify(s), "->", JSON.stringify(m.textOf(s)));
  })'
```

Actual output (main `7942ad1f`):

```
"café — 5–10 … O'Brien" -> "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"
"&lt;b&gt; stays text" -> "<b> stays text"
"♦ … ’" -> "♦ … ’"
```

Expected (browser-equivalent text): `café — 5–10 … O'Brien`, `<b> stays text` (single pass preserved), `♦ … ’`.

### Evidence (file:line on this main)

- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts:27-33` — `NAMED_ENTITIES` contains exactly `amp`, `lt`, `gt`, `quot`, `nbsp`.
- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts:46-53` — `decodeEntities` matches **any** named reference (`([a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*)`) and returns `NAMED_ENTITIES.get(name) ?? match`, i.e. everything else falls through as literal text.
- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts:55-58` — `textOf` (strip tags → decode → collapse) is the shared extractor.
- Call sites that turn this into user-visible text: `packages/data-source/src/web/native/free-engines.ts:64`, `:69`, `:136`, `:141`, `:183`, `:192` (titles/snippets), plus `:68`, `:135`, `:181` for result URLs.

### Impact

DuckDuckGo/Bing/Brave result titles and snippets are what `web_search` returns to the model and what reports cite; a page title like "Café culture — a review" is rendered literally, so the evidence shown to the user (and fed back into the prompt) carries entity codes instead of text. Entity-heavy pages are exactly the older/European and encyclopedia sources a science search hits often.

### Expected vs actual

- Expected: named references decode the same way a browser renders them (at minimum the typographic and Latin-1 names that appear in titles: `mdash`, `ndash`, `hellip`, `rsquo`, `lsquo`, `ldquo`, `rdquo`, `eacute`, `egrave`, `ouml`, `apos`, `middot`, `times`, `deg`, `plusmn`, …).
- Actual: only 5 names decode; the rest stay literal.

### Acceptance

1. `decodeEntities` resolves the named references it matches (full HTML5 named set, or a documented bounded table that covers at least the names listed above).
2. The single-pass guarantee from #672 is preserved: `&lt;` → `<`, `&amp;` → `&`; decoded output is never rescanned.
3. Surrogate / non-character rejection stays as it is (`�` etc. remain literal).
4. `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.test.ts` gains cases for the named references above, and the existing five keep passing.
5. No change to numeric-reference behavior (`A`, `A`, `😀`).

### Not a duplicate

Open-issue search for `entity`, `entity decode`, `html text extraction`, `named entity` returns no open report; the only entity issue is closed #672 (double decoding), whose fix this preserves. No open PR touches `html.ts` (`#663`/`#678` are the UTF-16 truncation family in other modules).

items.body:
## Problem

The nightly real journey `J5` (shard `research-9`) failed with `locator.click: Test timeout of 600000ms exceeded` while reading the run timeline. Playwright had already resolved the first `details.timeline-disclosure.tool` summary, but the element never became visible and 1049 click retries consumed the whole test budget.

## Cause

A live run folds adjacent exploration steps into a collapsed `<details class="timeline-exploration">` (`apps/web/src/timeline/RunTimeline.tsx`). Whether that wrapper exists depends on the tool sequence the model happens to produce, which a journey does not pin. `test/helpers/journeys.ts` expanded only the tool card itself, so a card nested in a closed group stayed invisible.

The trigger is model-dependent, which is why it is intermittent: reruns on a local model that only called `run_shell` passed 4/4 and produced no exploration group.

A second gap surfaced in review: the region name is localized, and the two `zh-CN` journeys that call `expandToolStep` resolved zero regions, so the expansion was a silent no-op there.

## Fix

PR #735 expands the timeline's own grouping containers before reading or locating tool cards, matches both UI locales (`Agent activity` / `Agent 活动`), and caps a card-summary click at 30s so a future timeline layout change fails fast with an attributable visibility error instead of spending the 600s test budget.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `J5` passes repeatedly against the nightly model, including runs that produce exploration tool steps.
- [ ] `journey-first-run` and `journey-artifact-archive` (`zh-CN`) still expand and read tool steps.
- [ ] A timeline layout change fails a journey in seconds with a visibility error, not in 600s.

## Evidence

- Nightly failure: first summary resolved, `element is not visible`, 1049 retries, 600s timeout.
- Local DOM probe with the same structure: the nested summary is invisible while the group is closed, and expands/clickable after the group is opened.
- Local reruns on the helper: `research-9` planned 1 / executed 1 / passed 1, twice (1.1m, 2.5m).

Refs #735

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
## What happened

`E2E_SWARM_TASK` is a test-only variable. `.ci/run-e2e.sh` exports `E2E_SWARM_TASK=1` whenever the backend is JiuwenSwarm, together with `SCIENCE_AGENT_JIUWENSWARM_SUBAGENTS=task`. Twelve specs then gate on it: `expect(process.env.E2E_SWARM_TASK !== "1", "BLOCKED: …").toBe(false)`. No product code reads it.

The precondition it stands for is real: these journeys exercise sub-agents delegated through the platform `task` tool (sandbox, deliverables, sub-agent cards), and some of them exercise JiuwenSwarm itself. As a switch, though, it does not do that job:

- It is a declaration, not a check. A stack started with `SCIENCE_AGENT_JIUWENSWARM_SUBAGENTS=jiuwenswarm`, the one configuration where the precondition fails, still passes if someone exports `E2E_SWARM_TASK=1`.
- In CI it is always `1` on the default backend, so it never stops anything there.
- It blocks journeys that do not depend on JiuwenSwarm. The built-in (native) loop also delegates through the platform `task` tool, but DRB, TC-E2E-01 and BiomniBench report BLOCKED on it unless the variable is set by hand.
- Anyone running a real journey by hand has to remember it; three benchmark READMEs say so.
- `deepresearchbench-swarm.spec.ts` and `biomnibench-da-swarm.spec.ts` write `backend: "jiuwenswarm"` into their score metrics as a constant, so a native run is labelled as JiuwenSwarm.

## Proposal

- `/health` (and `/api/health`) reports how the stack runs agent turns, from the API's own configuration: `agent: { executor: "jiuwenswarm" | "native", subagents: "task" | "jiuwenswarm" }`. The native loop always delegates through `task`. The API is the component that makes this decision in both modes; the adapter's `/agent/info` does not exist when the stack runs natively.
- One E2E helper reads it. Real research journeys (DRB, TC-E2E-01, BiomniBench) require platform `task` delegation on either executor. Journeys that test JiuwenSwarm's own behaviour (`swarm-*`, `literature-review-*`, `artifact-revision`) also require the `jiuwenswarm` executor. A mismatch is reported as BLOCKED with what the stack actually reported.
- `E2E_SWARM_TASK` is removed from `run-e2e.sh`, the specs and the READMEs.
- Score metrics record the executor the stack reported, not a constant.
- `E2E_SWARM_EXCLUSIVE`, `E2E_SWARM_COMPACTION`, `E2E_LITERATURE_FIXTURE` and `E2E_MCP_FAULT_PROXY` stay. They protect exclusive stacks and fixtures, not the stack's identity.

items.author: wyhohyw
items.body:
## Background

After a long-running tool execution fails, an Agent often has to infer completed work, reusable outputs, and possible continuation points from free-form logs. Execution state and logs alone do not provide a consistent basis for deciding where to continue.

Support recovery of failed long-running tasks: after the failure is addressed and the prerequisites are verified, the Agent can reuse completed results and continue from a supported recovery point, reducing unnecessary recomputation.

A shared, optional recovery metadata contract for tools and task adapters provides the supporting evidence. The LLM uses it to decide the next action; the framework persists and exposes it alongside the existing execution record, reusing existing execution tools and permission checks.

## Requested functionality

- Identify the original execution and expose completed stages or work units, the failed stage, and the failure reason when the task adapter can determine them.
- Reference reusable outputs and available task checkpoints using stable artifact/file/version identifiers where supported. Distinguish verified completed outputs from partial files.
- Explicitly report whether continuation is supported, unsupported, or unknown, including available continuation entry points and required inputs when supported.
- Describe conditions that must be checked before continuation, such as original execution termination, input/configuration changes, environment availability, and output validity.
- Preserve the metadata across refresh/reconnect and make it available through existing execution inspection and Agent tool results. Keep existing tools without recovery metadata compatible.
- Let the Agent inspect the evidence and choose repair, continuation, or a fresh attempt through existing execution tools and permission checks. Metadata itself must not automatically launch a replacement task.

The exact schema should follow the existing execution/tool-result architecture. Framework code should remain independent of specific scientific pipeline stages; task adapters supply domain-specific recovery information.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A shared, documented optional recovery metadata contract is available to long-running tools/task adapters.
- [ ] At least one supported long-running task adapter or representative test fixture demonstrates completed work, failed work, reusable result/checkpoint references, and continuation prerequisites.
- [ ] The Agent can retrieve persisted metadata after reconnecting and use it to identify a supported continuation point without relying solely on free-form logs.
- [ ] Unsupported or unknown recovery capability is explicit; the framework does not invent missing checkpoints or treat file existence alone as proof of completion.
- [ ] A running or unknown original execution is not automatically resubmitted because recovery metadata was returned.
- [ ] Tests cover supported/unsupported/unknown continuation, partial or invalid outputs, changed prerequisites, and persistence/readback.

## Scope and related work

- #398 covers reconnecting to the original NPU task, recovering its state/results, and avoiding duplicate submissions. This issue supplies structured evidence for Agent decisions after a confirmed failure.
- #278 covers in-conversation configuration and task continuation.
- This first version does not include arbitrary Agent-history rollback, restoration of process/NPU memory, or implementing model-specific computational checkpointing. Actual computational continuation depends on task-program support.
- Target release: **v0.3.0, October 30, 2026**, tracked in #249.

---

## 需求背景

长任务执行失败后，Agent 往往需要从自由文本日志中推断哪些工作已经完成、哪些结果可以复用、可以从哪里继续。仅有执行状态和日志，缺少统一的信息契约支撑这些判断。

支持长任务失败后的恢复：处理失败原因并确认接续前提后，Agent 能复用已完成结果，从受支持的恢复点继续，减少不必要的重复计算。

工具和任务适配器提供共享、可选的结构化恢复信息，作为上述能力的支撑。LLM 根据这些证据决定下一步；框架负责随现有执行记录持久化和提供查询，复用已有执行工具与权限检查。

## 期望功能

- 标识原执行；任务适配器能够确定时，返回已完成阶段或工作单元、失败阶段及失败原因。
- 通过受支持的稳定产物／文件／版本标识，引用可复用结果和任务检查点，区分已验证的完整结果与未完成文件。
- 明确返回可续跑、不支持续跑或能力未知；支持时给出可用续跑入口及所需输入。
- 描述接续前需要检查的条件，例如原执行已经结束、输入和配置变化、环境可用性及结果有效性。
- 刷新或重连后仍能通过现有执行查询和 Agent 工具结果获取这些信息；兼容不提供恢复信息的已有工具。
- Agent 根据证据选择修复、接续或重新执行，沿用现有执行工具及权限检查；返回恢复信息本身不自动启动替代任务。

具体字段设计应复用现有执行记录和工具结果架构。框架保持通用，由任务适配器提供具体业务阶段及恢复信息。

## 验收标准

- [ ] 提供有文档说明、可选的统一恢复信息契约，供长任务工具／适配器使用。
- [ ] 至少一个受支持的长任务适配器或有代表性的测试夹具，能够展示已完成工作、失败工作、可复用结果／检查点引用及接续前提。
- [ ] 重连后 Agent 能读取持久化信息，识别受支持的接续点，无须仅依赖自由文本日志推断。
- [ ] 不支持或能力未知时明确返回；框架不虚构检查点，也不把文件存在直接当作步骤已完成。
- [ ] 原执行仍在运行或结果未知时，不会因为返回恢复信息而自动重复提交。
- [ ] 测试覆盖支持／不支持／未知续跑能力、部分或无效结果、前提条件变化及持久化读取。

## 范围与关联

- #398 负责找回原 NPU 任务、恢复状态和结果、避免重复提交；本需求为确认失败后的 Agent 接续决策提供结构化证据。
- #278 负责对话内配置和任务接续。
- 首版不包含任意历史 Agent 状态回滚、进程／NPU 内存恢复，也不代替具体模型实现计算检查点。实际计算续跑依赖任务程序支持。
- 目标版本：**2026 年 10 月 30 日 v0.3.0**，在 #249 跟踪。
items.title: [Feature] Support recovery of failed long-running tasks

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Problem

On Windows, killing a runner child with POSIX-style signals does not tear down the full process tree. Desktop Windows work needs a platform adaptation that terminates the child **and** its grandchildren (e.g. `taskkill /T /F`).

PR #478 (`Closes #477` / F3.1 CAS) already embeds `terminateTree` under `services/runner/src/platform/`. That belongs to **F3.2**, not F3.1 — track and accept it here (or split it out of #478).

## Expected

- `services/runner` (and any required API call sites) obtain tree-kill via `platform/index.ts` only.
- POSIX path remains signal-based; Windows uses an explicit tree terminate.
- Unit tests tagged `os:windows` cover child + grandchild cleanup.

## Verification cases

### Case 1 — Windows tree kill
- **Preconditions:** Windows host; spawn a Node/cmd child that itself spawns a grandchild that stays alive.
- **Steps:** Call `terminateTree(child)`; wait briefly; inspect process list for child and grandchild PIDs.
- **Expected / pass:** Both PIDs are gone; helper returns success/true.

### Case 2 — POSIX unchanged
- **Preconditions:** Linux or macOS.
- **Steps:** Run existing runner process-lifecycle / posix platform tests.
- **Expected / pass:** No behaviour change vs `main`; suite green.

### Case 3 — Facade only
- **Preconditions:** PR diff for this issue.
- **Steps:** Grep runner call sites for raw `taskkill` / `process.platform === \"win32\"` outside `platform/`.
- **Expected / pass:** No direct platform branches in consumer code; all go through `platform/index.ts`.

## Related

- Split from / Follow-up for PR #478 and #477 (F3.1)
- Parent: #400
items.title: [Feature] [F3.2] Runner/API process tree terminate on Windows (terminateTree / taskkill)

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Problem

#494 adds `scripts/lib/venv-launchers.mjs` (trampoline replace + runtime DLL copy) with portable unit tests, but:

1. Nothing in-tree calls `replaceVenvTrampolines` / `copyVenvRuntimeDlls` (`assemble-backend.mjs` / bootstrap not present yet).
2. Comments claim a closed loop with `fixVenvHome`, but that helper does not exist — after swapping the launcher, `pyvenv.cfg` `home` can still point at the build machine, so the real `python.exe` still fails off-machine.
3. Tests only compare bytes; they do not spawn `Scripts\python.exe`, so the field failures (entity not found / `0xC0000135`) are not covered.

## Expected

- Call sites in assemble-backend (pack-time) and bootstrap (first-run repair) invoke the module.
- `fixVenvHome` (or equivalent) rewrites `pyvenv.cfg` `home` to the bundled interpreter root.
- A Windows smoke test builds a uv venv, relocates it, spawns `Scripts\python.exe -c "..."`, and asserts exit 0 with `sys.prefix` at the new path.

## Verification cases

### Case 1 — pack-time wiring
- **Preconditions:** Payload contains a uv-created venv whose `Scripts\python.exe` is a trampoline; assemble-backend runs.
- **Steps:** Inspect `Scripts\python.exe` and `pyvenv.cfg` after assemble.
- **Expected / pass:** Launcher is a real CPython stub (no `uv trampoline` marker); `home` points at the bundled python root; runtime DLLs sit beside the launcher.

### Case 2 — first-run bootstrap repair
- **Preconditions:** `dataDir\envs` still has pre-fix trampolines (reinstall with valid unpack stamp).
- **Steps:** Start the shell once on a clean machine without system Python.
- **Expected / pass:** Bootstrap replaces trampolines, copies DLLs, fixes `home`; each venv `python.exe -c "import sys; print(sys.prefix)"` exits 0.

### Case 3 — Windows spawn smoke (CI or labeled job)
- **Preconditions:** `os:windows` (or equivalent) test runner with a bundled/minimal CPython + uv.
- **Steps:** Create uv venv → move tree → `spawn(Scripts/python.exe, ["-c", "import sys; print(sys.prefix)"])`.
- **Expected / pass:** Exit code 0; printed prefix equals the relocated venv path. Byte-only unit tests alone do not satisfy this case.

## Context

Refs #494, #493. Non-blocking Follow-up from HongyeZhou review of shell.04. #494 should use `Refs #493` until this loop lands (or fold wiring into the same PR).
items.title: [Feature] win-desktop-client: wire venv-launchers + fixVenvHome + Windows spawn smoke

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Problem

`win-desktop-client/` is an independent pnpm workspace (not listed in the root `pnpm-workspace.yaml` packages: `config / apps/* / services/* / packages/*`). Architecture checks and `tsconfig.tests.json` also skip it. As a result, install / typecheck / unit-test failures under this tree are invisible to GitHub Actions (see #486: missing patch and empty `tsconfig` include were only found by local runs).

## Expected

A CI job (or matrix entry) runs on changes under `win-desktop-client/**` and exercises at least:

- `pnpm install` (lockfile present)
- `pnpm typecheck` (when sources exist)
- `pnpm test` for portable Node tests

## Verification cases

### Case 1 — install gate
- **Preconditions:** PR that only touches `win-desktop-client/` and references a missing `patchedDependencies` file (or otherwise breaks install).
- **Steps:** Open the PR; wait for CI.
- **Expected / pass:** The new job fails with a clear install error; root jobs that ignore this tree may still be green.

### Case 2 — typecheck / test gate
- **Preconditions:** PR adds a TypeScript error under `win-desktop-client/src/` or a failing `test/*.test.ts`.
- **Steps:** Open the PR; wait for CI.
- **Expected / pass:** typecheck or test step fails; merge is blocked by the required check once wired.

### Case 3 — no-op on unrelated paths
- **Preconditions:** PR only changes `apps/web/` (or another root package).
- **Steps:** Open the PR.
- **Expected / pass:** The win-desktop-client job is skipped or stays green without installing Electron unnecessarily.

## Context

Refs #486, #485. Non-blocking Follow-up from HongyeZhou review of shell.01.
items.title: [Feature] win-desktop-client: add CI job for independent Electron workspace

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Problem

POSIX `chmod 0600` only toggles the read-only bit on Windows NTFS and does **not** strip inherited group/world access. Secrets, bootstrap tokens, and similar owner-only files need an ACL adaptation (`icacls` inheritance strip + grant current user).

PR #478 embeds `restrictToOwner` / `restrictToOwnerSync` under `services/api` and `services/runner` platform layers while claiming only F3.1 (#477). Track **F3.3** here so scope and AC are explicit (or split out of #478).

## Expected

- Sensitive write sites that previously `chmod`'d to owner-only use `restrictToOwner` via `platform/os` (api) / `platform` (runner).
- POSIX keeps `chmod`; Windows uses icacls with inheritance removed.
- Highest-sensitivity stores (e.g. master key / SSH private key paths) are included or explicitly deferred with rationale.

## Verification cases

### Case 1 — Windows ACL tightened
- **Preconditions:** Windows host; create a temp file that inherits group-readable ACLs.
- **Steps:** Call `restrictToOwner(file)`; run `icacls <file>` and inspect DACL.
- **Expected / pass:** Inheritance removed; current user has access; unintended group/world ACE gone (or equivalent owner-only outcome documented in the test).

### Case 2 — POSIX unchanged
- **Preconditions:** Linux or macOS.
- **Steps:** Run posix platform + existing secrets/bootstrap unit tests.
- **Expected / pass:** Mode bits still applied as on `main`; suite green.

### Case 3 — Sync path at startup
- **Preconditions:** Windows; data dir owned by another principal (or simulated failure).
- **Steps:** Exercise `restrictToOwnerSync` on bootstrap/token paths.
- **Expected / pass:** Failure mode is explicit (error message), not a silent weaken; documented in PR/issue notes.

## Related

- Split from / Follow-up for PR #478 and #477 (F3.1)
- Parent: #400
- Note from #478 review: `store/secrets.ts` / `store/ssh-config.ts` may still rely on raw `chmod` — include or call out as residual risk.
items.title: [Feature] [F3.3] Owner-restrict file ACLs on Windows (icacls / restrictToOwner)

items.author: zhaochen39
items.body:
## Summary

Model setup is the first-run gate: with no provider configured, **Settings → Model registry** opens the *Connect model* wizard automatically (`apps/web/src/ProviderModelSettings.tsx:617-618`). The screen is meant to answer one question — "which model will my runs use?" — but it currently asks it in six different places, uses one label for two different actions, and commits some answers with a Save button while committing others the moment they are clicked. This report is about that flow, not about how any single control looks.

## What the screen offers today

| # | Control | Where | What it writes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `Connect model` → `Save & connect` | registry heading (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:897-904`) | creates the provider **and** registers every model the vendor lists, immediately |
| 2 | `Fetch model list` → tick rows → `Save & connect` | wizard footer (`ModelConnectWizard.tsx:828-841`) | same, narrowed to the ticked models |
| 3 | `Advanced configuration` → `Manual entries` / `Model identifier` | a fold inside the wizard (`ModelConnectWizard.tsx:745-794`) | same, for models the listing does not return |
| 4 | `Refresh list` → per-row `Add` | expanded provider (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:346-348`) | one model, immediately |
| 5 | `Add model` (toggle) → manual form | bottom of the expanded provider (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:505-515`) | one model, immediately |
| 6 | `Global default task model` select | registry heading (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:879-896`) | `globalSettings.modelId`, immediately |
| 7 | `Edit` provider → `Save` / `Cancel` | expanded provider (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:703-749`) | provider fields, staged until Save |

Above all of that sits a separate `Model catalog` strip with its own refresh (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:386-400`).

## Problems

### 1. `Add model` means two different things, one above the other

Inside the same expanded provider, the per-model row action uses `t("providers.models.add")` (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:348`) and the toggle that opens the manual form uses the *same* string (`:506`). So the row of a listed model offers "Add" (register this model) and a few pixels below the table another "Add model" opens a form. The wizard reuses the label a third time for its manual-entry toggle, but submits with a different one, `Add to list` (`ModelConnectWizard.tsx:779, 791`). A user cannot predict what any of these three controls will do from its label.

### 2. Two incompatible save models in the same panel

Provider fields are a draft: `Save` / `Cancel`, plus a `window.confirm` when another provider's `Edit` would discard the draft (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:679-687, 693-697`). Everything else writes immediately:

- adding a model — `addModel()` calls the API at once, no confirm (`:784-823`);
- deleting a model — immediate, but guarded by `window.confirm` (`:825-863`);
- deleting a provider — immediate, guarded by `window.confirm` (`:751-754`);
- the default-model select — immediate (`:879-896`).

The same panel therefore mixes revertible and irreversible actions with no visual cue for which is which. Collapsing the row or expanding another one hides an unsaved provider draft with no prompt at that moment (`:699-701`), and the prompt only arrives later, when the settings dialog is closed — by then the user has usually forgotten the draft exists.

### 3. Registering *every* listed model is the silent default, and choosing models is hidden

With no explicit choice, `Save & connect` fetches the vendor list and registers all of it (`ModelConnectWizard.tsx:324-339`). To choose a subset the user must first press `Fetch model list` (`:828-841`) and only then do checkboxes appear. The only warning is the small plan line "Save & connect registers every model the provider lists" (`:838`), while the manual path that most users need when discovery fails is behind `Advanced configuration`, a fold that otherwise looks like protocol/proxy plumbing. Nothing states before saving that the first registered model will become the global default; that effect is only reported afterwards (`:414-421, 433-450`).

### 4. The default task model is edited in two places with different commit semantics

The registry heading has a `Global default task model` select that writes instantly (via `replaceDefaultModelOverride`, `App.tsx:5259-5269`). The same value is also edited in **Settings → Global → Task model**, which is a draft saved by the dialog's own Save (`App.tsx:5217-5219`). Two controls, one field, opposite commit behaviour — the difference is invisible until someone loses an edit.

### 5. Vocabulary: seven labels for four concepts

`Connect model`, `Save & connect`, `Add model`, `Add to list`, `Fetch model list`, `Refresh list`, `Advanced configuration` vs `Advanced connection settings` (`i18n/messages.ts:675-720, 738, 771`). "Connect", "register", "add" and "save" are used interchangeably for one operation, while "fetch"/"refresh" is the only genuinely different one.

### 6. Success does not end the flow

`resetPlan()` clears only the model plan (`ModelConnectWizard.tsx:157-164`); the API key, provider name, base URL and success banner stay (`:433-450`). Pressing `Save & connect` again therefore creates a second provider with the same display name — allowed by the store (`services/api/src/store.ts:2758-2779` has no name uniqueness check) — and there is no explicit "done" state to tell the user the wizard has finished.

## Actual vs expected

| | Actual | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| Entry points | Six ways to register a model across three levels (wizard, provider row, manual form), plus a default-model control duplicated in another tab | One way for each intent: add a provider; add models to a provider; pick the default model |
| Commit model | Provider fields staged, models and default immediate, deletes confirmed one by one | One commit model for the whole registry, with the same confirmation rule for every destructive action |
| Model choice | Register-all unless the user discovers `Fetch model list`; manual entry inside `Advanced configuration` | The listing visible by default with checkboxes, "register all" an explicit choice, manual entry next to it |
| Default model | Same field, two controls, two commit semantics, no indication of which wins | One control, or a link to the canonical one |
| After success | Form keeps the key and name; second press creates a duplicate provider | Clear, collapsed or "done" state; a duplicate name is warned about |

## Where

- `apps/web/src/ProviderModelSettings.tsx` — registry heading, wizard mount, provider rows, per-row add/delete, manual form toggle, default-model select, provider draft.
- `apps/web/src/ModelConnectWizard.tsx` — `resolveModelPlan` (register-all fallback), advanced fold, footer plan summary, success state.
- `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts:675-720, 722-723, 738, 771, 915` — the button and heading vocabulary.
- `apps/web/src/App.tsx:5217-5219, 5250-5280` — Mounting of the registry and of the Global settings group that edits the same default.

## Root cause

One component serves four jobs at once — registry list, provider editor, model picker, default-model setter — and each job brought its own persistence style and its own copy. The wizard was added later to make first-run setup one step, but it kept the provider editor's advanced fields *and* gained model registration, so provider creation and model registration now overlap instead of composing: the wizard can register models, the provider row can only add one at a time, and the provider editor cannot touch models at all. The `Add model` label was reused from the existing manual form for three controls that do different things.

## Suggested direction

1. **One control per intent.** `Add provider` (the wizard) and a single `Add model` per provider, opening one dialog that shows the fetched listing with checkboxes and keeps manual entry as a fallback in the same dialog. Remove the separate advanced/manual toggle, and stop using `Add` both for "register this listed model" and "open a form".
2. **Pick one commit model for the registry** and keep it: either stage every edit behind Save (provider fields, models, default) or make every action immediate with an undo. Apply the same confirmation rule to add, delete model and delete provider.
3. **Make model selection visible in the wizard.** Fetch the listing as soon as the key is entered, show it above the fold, and make "register all listed models" an explicit checkbox instead of the silent fallback. State the "first model becomes the global default" consequence before `Save & connect`.
4. **De-duplicate the default-model control.** Keep one, and link to it from the other place instead of rendering the same field twice with different commit semantics.
5. **End the flow on success.** Clear the key and name, collapse the wizard or show a `Done` state, and warn when a provider with the same name already exists.
6. **Copy pass.** Unify `Connect model` / `Save & connect` / `Add model` / `Add to list`, and keep `fetch`/`refresh` for the vendor listing only.

## Duplicate check

Searched open and closed issues for `model registry`, `Connect model`, `wizard`, `Add model`, `provider` and `usability`. #39 (closed) introduced the one-step connection wizard and is the origin of this overlap; #632 (closed) and #684 cover the *searchable model picker* rather than the registration flow; #686 covers the rendering of the provider `Test` control. None reports the overlapping entry points, the mixed save semantics or the duplicated default-model control.
items.title: [Usability] Model registration: overlapping entry points and inconsistent save semantics

items.body:
## Background and environment

During a source installation on a Debian 13 cloud desktop on 2026-10-11, using main commit `5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08`, two problems required manual investigation:

1. The desktop terminal did not inherit the outbound proxy environment. The initial managed micromamba download failed with `ECONNREFUSED`; an installation environment with the required network configuration could complete the download.
2. When the adapter inherited a SOCKS proxy configuration, it failed to start because `socksio` was missing, affecting access to the application.

The first observation is an environment-triggered failure, not proof of a downloader implementation defect. The second has a concrete dependency declaration gap.

## Conditions and observed behavior

### A. Different proxy environments across installation and runtime entry points

- External access required a proxy, but the terminal initiating scientific-environment preparation did not inherit the corresponding configuration.
- The micromamba connection was refused and scientific-environment preparation could not complete.
- Installation succeeded through an official download/install path with the necessary network configuration, retaining the pinned version and SHA-256 verification.
- The scientific environment subsequently became ready, with Python 3.12, NumPy, pandas, SciPy, and Matplotlib available.

### B. SOCKS configuration prevents adapter startup

- Create a clean adapter environment from the declared project dependencies and start it with a valid SOCKS proxy configuration.
- During HTTP client initialization, the missing socksio dependency prevents adapter startup.
- In this installation, adding socksio from official PyPI to the adapter's isolated environment restored startup; API health and page HTML checks then passed.

Source references:
- [Adapter declares plain httpx](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/adapter/pyproject.toml#L19-L25).
- [HTTP clients are constructed during startup](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/app.py#L47-L63).

## User impact

- Users may have already installed the source and other dependencies, yet still be blocked at first startup or scientific-environment preparation, preventing access to the workbench or relevant computations.
- Users must investigate differences between terminal and child-process proxy environments, and may need to install undeclared dependencies manually.
- A component-level failure can look like a failed installation of the entire application, leading to unnecessary reinstalls. This is not evidence that micromamba itself is unsuitable or unavailable.

## Expected behavior and proposed improvements

1. Unify installation/startup preflight checks: inspect the actual child process's proxy configuration, connectivity to required download sources, and dependencies for the selected proxy protocol. Report redacted status, never credentials.
2. Declare and lock SOCKS support, for example through `httpx[socks]`. Define the proxy boundary between loopback service calls and external requests, including correct `NO_PROXY` handling.
3. Identify the failing component, stage, underlying cause, and actionable next step. After configuration is corrected, allow retrying the failed step while reusing verified tools and caches.
4. Report Web entry point, adapter, and scientific-environment readiness separately instead of treating partial readiness as an all-or-nothing result.

The repository already has [download retry and cache mechanisms](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/scripts/fetch-managed-micromamba.mjs#L179-L295), as well as [classified errors and mirror/preinstalled-tool recovery guidance](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/runner/src/environment-store.ts#L1138-L1173). The goal is to connect these capabilities into a coherent first-run experience, not to replace the downloader.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A clean adapter environment starts with HTTP/SOCKS proxy configurations without manually installing undeclared dependencies.
- [ ] Missing or incorrect proxy configuration produces redacted, actionable diagnostics while retaining the underlying error.
- [ ] Correcting configuration allows retrying the failed step and reusing verified artifacts, without clearing all data or reinstalling.
- [ ] Version pinning and hash verification remain enforced; recovery does not disable TLS verification.
- [ ] Tests cover no proxy, HTTP/SOCKS proxies, unreachable download sources, and successful retry after correction; installation documentation is updated.

Related: #29 (actionable dependency preflight), #213 and #229 (onboarding feedback). This issue focuses on the observed proxy-related failures and first-install recovery experience.
items.title: [Bug] Improve proxy-aware installation: declare SOCKS support and unify preflight and recovery

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
> Cross-tracking: [GitCode #91](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/91) (Chinese counterpart of this issue).

## What I was trying to do

Start the server and confirm "I can actually run analyses now".

## What I saw instead

- On Linux, when sandbox (bwrap) probing fails (e.g. the host disables unprivileged user namespaces), `services/launcher/src/preflight.ts` only prints a `WARNING` line; `services/launcher/src/serve.ts` ignores the result, keeps starting, and finally prints `ScienceDiscovery is ready at ...`.
- The green connection dot in the top bar only means the frontend can talk to the local API (`Connection OK`). It says nothing about sandbox availability, the scientific Python environment, or model quota.
- Users believe everything is ready, then the run fails mid-analysis — often with raw low-level errors.

## Why this is confusing

"Ready" and the green light create false confidence; the failure happens only after the user has invested time writing a prompt and uploading data.

## Suggested user-observable outcome

- When startup preflight finds the sandbox unusable, surface a prominent in-app notice ("analyses cannot run in this environment", with the reason) instead of a single terminal warning.
- Separate "frontend connected" from "compute ready" in the status indicator.
- Open question (needs a product decision): when compute is unavailable, should the app block new analyses entirely, or allow read-only browsing of past sessions and artifacts? The two strategies differ a lot in UX; decide before implementing.

Design note: the preflight result already exists in the startup chain (`runPreflight`); what is missing is exposing it to the web UI and layering the status display.
items.title: [Bug] Sandbox unavailability only warns in the terminal while serve still reports ready; surface real compute readiness

## Cross-check needed

cc @zhaozhaozz @zy95-12 @HongyeZhou

### Three-layer defaults (important)
These coexist and are easy to conflate:

1. **Schema fallback**: `DEFAULT_SKILL_SELECTION_MODE = "all"` when unset (`packages/schema/src/runtime-settings.ts`).
2. **New Project product default**: `withDefaultProjectSkillSettings` writes `skillSelectionMode: "selected"` + empty `enabledSkillIds` / libraries (Skill Library intent: avoid silently expanding capability).
3. **JiuwenSwarm force-all**: on start, `http/index.ts` calls `store.useEverySkillEverywhere()` so the **effective** mode is `all` while Swarm is the backend (stored `selected` is kept and applies again when switching back to native).

Box smoke on Swarm therefore seeing `all` is **expected**, not accidental.

### Observation (box smoke, 2026-10-24 Asia/Shanghai)
- SHA: `main@9eb45d75`
- Backend: **JiuwenSwarm** (force-all path)
- Model: Zhipu `glm-5.3-flash`
- ~17 shipped skills effective, `thinkingEffort: high`
- Trivial user prompt → **~38k input tokens** (chat/history ≈ **165 bytes**)
- First visible assistant text ≈ **20s** wall

Progressive disclosure is **already implemented** (`docs/en/developer-docs/skill-progressive-disclosure.md`: metadata/path in prompt, body on demand). It does **not** prevent metadata/tool-surface growth when the effective selected set is the whole catalog under `all` / Swarm force-all.

### Questions for maintainers
1. Should end-user UX optimize for **Project `selected`** or accept **Swarm force-all** as the primary path?
2. Is there appetite to change schema DEFAULT, Swarm force-all, or both?
3. Have you seen the same **TTFT / cost** under Swarm vs native?

### Proposed performance watch split (do not mix into one Nightly bucket)
1. **UX / API latency lane** — queue → context → **TTFT** → run wall; short daily probe (`live.mjs ttft` + one real short chat), measure under **both** native and JiuwenSwarm, and under `all` vs `selected`.
2. **Correctness lane (existing L3 ×9)** — tool/files/cancel/etc.; keep **out of** TTFT gates.
3. **Research quality lane (L4 Nightly)** — DRB/Biomni/etc. as quality signal, **not** first-token UX.

### Possible directions (not proposing a fix yet)
- Keep progressive disclosure; also shrink **effective set** under Swarm (or stop force-all)
- Align schema DEFAULT with new-Project `selected`
- Cap / warn when resolved skill metadata size exceeds a threshold
- Surface skill-token cost in Usage / composer

### Non-goals
- Nightly research-bench red streak root-cause (separate)
- Tool-call accuracy eval (separate)

### Test coverage gap
- Unit coverage exists for settings semantics (`store.test.ts`: selected / all / `useEverySkillEverywhere`).
- **No CI gate** on TTFT or skill-token size; `live.mjs ttft()` logs only.
- Progressive disclosure tests do not cap catalog size under `all`.

Cross-check so far: skills-side review agrees the three-layer story; DigitalMate has no parallel issue. Nearby: #508, #93, #141.

Implementation: ScienceDiscovery (ours) — PR follows within 24h. Do not pick up without a `pickup-ok` comment on this issue.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Lead
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Lead
Claim-Id: dae5b8d1b8af4de3885faca176d3c50a
Branch: dev2/fix/cas-has-corrupt-object
Base: ad34dd7847f6
At: 2026-10-29T05:08:29Z

## What is wrong

`CasStore.has()` in `packages/cas/src/index.ts:74-82` answers the boolean existence question by calling `read()`. `read()` re-hashes the bytes and throws `CAS integrity failure` when a stored object no longer matches its digest, and `has()` only maps `ENOENT` to `false` (`:79`), so a corrupt object makes `has()` throw. Its sibling `verify()` (`:84-92`) deliberately maps the same condition to `false`. Two predicates over the same store therefore disagree: `verify()` says "not valid", `has()` raises.

## Reproduction (live main `ad34dd7847`, file blob `584cf1eaefc7ec9b5c4c2125de7bf13c39039ba0`)

```
$ node --import tsx -e '<put "hello world" via CasStore, then overwrite the blob with "HELLO WORLD">'
put -> b94d27b9934d 11
has before -> true
verify after corruption -> false
has after corruption -> THREW CAS integrity failure
```

The overwrite keeps the byte length, so this is exactly the "same size, different bytes" corruption case the store already detects elsewhere.

## Expected

`has(hash)` is a total boolean predicate: `true` only when the object is present and valid, `false` when it is missing **or corrupt** - the same answer `verify()` gives. A caller deciding "is this object still usable, or must I republish?" must not have to catch an untyped integrity error to find out.

## Why it matters

The store is used as a cache in front of publication paths (`put` / `retain` / republish decisions): those call `has()` to choose between "reuse" and "write it again". With a corrupt blob they crash with `CAS integrity failure` instead of taking the republish branch, and the error is thrown from a method whose contract is a boolean. PR `#657` made vanished refs republish; corrupt bytes are the neighbouring case and still have this shape.

## Fix scope

Extend the `has()` catch to map the integrity failure to `false` the way `verify()` already does (about two lines), plus one test next to the existing `index.test.ts` cases. No new dependency, no behaviour change for a valid or a missing object.
items.title: [Bug] CAS has() throws on a corrupted object while verify() returns false

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Problem
PR #460 delivered default local namespace isolation for embedded JiuwenSwarm. The product decision on #257 requires a **complete config/runtime boundary**, not only a renamed default directory: SD must not silently adopt standalone Swarm configuration via inherited env vars, home/registry lookup, or runtime service discovery, and must not let port collision silently attach SD to another Swarm service.

## Expected
- Embedded Swarm config and state are owned by ScienceDiscovery; discovering a user’s standalone Swarm (including same instance name) must not replace or merge SD’s model/skill/agent/tool behavior.
- Outer-process Swarm-specific environment variables, default SDK paths, and service discovery must not bypass the SD-owned boundary unless the user explicitly configured an SD-supported override with clear ownership.
- setup/start/status/env/stop, logs, and connection endpoints resolve to the same SD-owned instance; port conflicts are handled without silently connecting to a sibling Swarm.

## Verification cases

1. **Standalone config does not drive SD**
   - **Preconditions:** Disposable home/namespace; standalone Swarm instance (including same name `sciencediscovery`) with deliberately different identifiable config.
   - **Steps:**
     1. Start ScienceDiscovery with default embedded settings.
     2. Change standalone model/skill/agent settings and start/stop the standalone instance.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** SD behavior and backend ownership remain SD’s; standalone changes do not alter SD settings or which instance SD uses.

2. **Env / discovery bypass**
   - **Preconditions:** Outer environment carries standalone Swarm-specific variables and/or occupied ports that could point at a non-SD instance.
   - **Steps:**
     1. Launch SD without an explicit user opt-in to that standalone endpoint.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** SD does not silently read standalone registry/config or connect to the foreign service; conflicts surface safely rather than mis-binding.

3. **SD lifecycle leaves standalone intact**
   - **Preconditions:** Both SD embedded and standalone instances live in the disposable namespace.
   - **Steps:**
     1. Run SD setup/start/stop and change SD settings.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** Standalone registry/config/sessions remain unmodified and the standalone process is not stopped by SD lifecycle.

## Context
- Env: Evidence from #257 product decision comment (`embedded-swarm-isolation-decision`) and #460 partial scope (local isolation done; broader boundary still called out).
- Refs: Parent #257; fixing PR #460 (merged). Default path isolation landed in #460; this Issue tracks remaining boundary / env / discovery acceptance from that decision.
- Notes: Do not auto-migrate or delete ambiguous standalone data. Explicit SD-supported overrides remain allowed when ownership is clear.
items.title: [Bug] Embedded JiuwenSwarm must not adopt standalone config via env or discovery

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Lead
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Lead
Claim-Id: 8a1b7dbd95c149489c75d01defcd079d
Branch: dev1/fix/fetch-document-codepoint-truncation
Base: 1e8865838ce8
At: 2026-10-29T04:57:48Z

## What is wrong

`document()` in `packages/data-source/src/web/native/fetch.ts:105-107` truncates the vendor's text with a raw `slice(0, 4_096)`, so a UTF-16 surrogate pair that straddles the budget is cut in half and the document handed to the model ends with a lone high surrogate.

## Reproduction (live main `1e8865838ce80b8519063e26b5910a5b23ff2027`)

`renderExaContents`/`renderTavilyExtract` both funnel through `document()`. Same logic copied verbatim, run with `node`:

```
$ node -e 'const MAX=4096; const text="x".repeat(MAX-1)+"😀"; console.log(JSON.stringify(text.slice(0,MAX).slice(-2)))'
"\ud83d"
```

The last code unit is `0xd83d` (high surrogate) with no low surrogate after it - an unpaired surrogate in the fetched document.

## Expected

Truncate at a code-point boundary, the way `#663` now does it for the artifact preview: drop the whole character instead of half of it, so the result is never longer than the budget and never contains a new unpaired surrogate.

## Why it matters

`web_fetch` output is fed back into prompts and can be cached and re-serialised as JSON; an unpaired surrogate is invalid UTF-8 text and `JSON.stringify` escapes it into a `\ud83d` sequence the model reads as a broken glyph. The same defect was reported for the artifact preview in `#660` and fixed there by `#663`; this call site is a different module (`packages/data-source/src/web/native/fetch.ts`) and is still raw, so this is not a duplicate.

## Fix scope

One small helper in the same file (or reuse of an existing code-point truncation helper if one is exported) plus its call in `document()`; tests next to the existing `renderExaContents`/`renderTavilyExtract` ones. About 10-15 lines, no new dependency.
items.title: [Bug] web_fetch document truncation splits a surrogate pair at the 4096-char budget

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Problem and user outcome

Researchers need to retrieve domain-specific scientific data through MCP and use it in traceable ScienceDiscovery workflows. Literature search alone does not satisfy this need: the objects are expression datasets, bioactivity measurements, variant assertions, and protein structures.

Provide supported, discoverable connections to **GEO, ChEMBL, ClinVar, RCSB PDB, and AlphaFold Protein Structure Database**, with reliable retrieval, explicit data boundaries, and provenance that survives downstream analysis.

## Context and existing implementation

Request inspired by this article: https://x.com/servasyy_ai/article/2112052770287284550
Related project documentation: https://aipoch.com/docs/guides/connectors/

Source inspection of ScienceDiscovery at baseline `0d31e155` found existing MCP implementations for GEO, ChEMBL, ClinVar, and PDB in `services/gateway/src/sciencediscovery_gateway/public_biomed_mcp.py`, plus manifests in `packages/mcp-sources/src/public-biomed.ts`. UniProt, Ensembl, and Reactome provide additional reusable patterns. No built-in AlphaFold DB adapter was found in that inspection.

This is a request to complete and validate domain database support, reusing existing adapters. It does not assume these databases are entirely unsupported. The baseline assessment was static inspection, not a live end-to-end availability test; recheck the target version before implementation.

## Requested scope

| Database | Required user-facing capabilities | Domain details to preserve |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GEO | Search studies, retrieve study/sample metadata, discover actual processed/supplementary files, and download selected analysis-ready data | GSE/GSM/GPL identifiers, organism, sample conditions, platform, and whether data are raw counts, normalized values, or other processed data |
| ChEMBL | Search molecules/targets, retrieve bioactivity measurements with useful filters, and perform similarity searches | Molecule/target/assay IDs, assay type, organism, relation, value, units, confidence, and source references |
| ClinVar | Search/lookup variants and retrieve individual clinical assertions | VCV/RCV/SCV identifiers where applicable, assembly, condition, review status, dates, and conflicting submissions |
| RCSB PDB | Search/lookup experimental structures and download supported structure files | PDB ID, experimental method, resolution where applicable, chains/entities, ligands, and source/version metadata |
| AlphaFold DB | Retrieve available predictions by protein accession and download model/confidence files when available | UniProt accession, model identifier/version, source URLs, and confidence information |

AlphaFold DB retrieval is separate from running AlphaFold prediction software. New prediction compute infrastructure is outside this request. PubMed and other literature databases are also outside this scope.

## Integration requirements

- Reuse the MCP client, connector selection, permission/audit, and artifact download mechanisms. Prefer official provider APIs behind MCP adapters; do not require providers to expose MCP themselves.
- Make supported sources and operations discoverable, with setup instructions and any credential requirements. Enable the source for the intended Session and support both Inspector validation and Agent use.
- Return structured domain data and standard evidence records with stable identifiers, source links, retrieval time, and provider version/release when available. Retain source caveats and attribution.
- A generic custom MCP connection currently preserves raw/structured content but produces empty standardized `records`; calling a tool successfully alone must not count as complete evidence integration.
- Transfer large datasets and structure files through governed artifact jobs, with source metadata and integrity checks. Keep file bytes out of model context and distinguish a proposed download from a completed, verified artifact.
- Handle pagination, provider rate limits, timeouts, invalid identifiers, missing records/files, and partial failures explicitly. Do not silently present a capped subset as the complete dataset.
- Document scientific limits: GEO standard matrix/SOFT candidate paths do not enumerate all supplementary files; not every expression matrix is suitable for count-based analysis; ClinVar submissions can conflict; experimental and predicted structures must remain distinguishable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On the target version, document the existing capability and remaining gap for each of the five databases.
- [ ] All five sources can be configured/enabled and successfully called from the intended Session; tool inputs and results are inspectable and audited.
- [ ] Each database has a representative live provider validation with recorded identifiers, commands/steps, expected results, and actual results. Record unavailable-provider cases as blocked rather than passed.
- [ ] GEO: discover actual files for a public study, retrieve relevant sample annotations, and download/verify a real selected matrix. Validate its data type and dimensions before downstream analysis; report when count-based analysis is inappropriate.
- [ ] ChEMBL: retrieve a target/molecule-linked activity set with explicit assay/measurement constraints, preserving units and relations, and verify pagination or clearly disclosed limits.
- [ ] ClinVar: retrieve assertions and preserve conflicting classifications/review status without reducing them to one unsupported consensus.
- [ ] PDB: retrieve an experimental structure, complete a verified CIF/PDB download, and demonstrate that a downstream analysis step can read the artifact and inspect its metadata.
- [ ] AlphaFold DB: retrieve a known available prediction by accession, verify a model download and available confidence metadata, and clearly identify it as predicted.
- [ ] Returned evidence and downloaded artifacts retain their source identifiers/URLs and retrieval metadata in subsequent analysis outputs.
- [ ] Automated tests cover domain result normalization and representative missing-record, malformed-input, rate-limit, and download-failure paths. Product-level validation covers connector selection, Inspector/Agent execution, and completed artifacts; mocked success alone is insufficient.
- [ ] User documentation describes supported operations, limitations, configuration, and reproducible examples for each source.

Implementation may be split into linked changes, but this feature remains open until the full five-database acceptance scope is verified.

## Child work item — PDB entity and chemical-component identity verification (migrated from #448)

The PDB connector must let researchers verify a structure’s protein target and ligand identity against a ChEMBL record without relying on structure titles or compound names. This is a bounded sub-item of the PDB acceptance scope above, not a separate database integration.

### Required MCP operations

- Expose discoverable polymer and nonpolymer entity identifiers from an entry lookup (or an equivalent bounded entry expansion).
- `pdb_get_polymer_entity(pdb_id, entity_id)`: entity description/type, organism, UniProt/reference mappings, label/auth chain identifiers, sequence/coverage and construct/mutation information where available.
- `pdb_get_nonpolymer_entity(pdb_id, entity_id)`: ligand/component identity, label/auth chain mappings and provider cross-references.
- `pdb_lookup_chemical_component(component_id)`: CCD name, formula/charge, InChI, complete InChIKey, available SMILES and mapped external identifiers with provenance. Extended CCD IDs such as five-character `A1CEA` are valid.

All results must provide structured domain fields and nonempty standardized evidence records with stable identifiers, canonical URLs, retrieval time, attribution and provider version/revision where available. Missing UniProt/InChIKey mappings must remain missing; do not replace them with name-based identity assertions. Preserve salt/parent relationships, stereochemistry-aware complete identifiers, covalent/modified-component qualifications, and label versus author chain IDs.

### Required validation cases

- Positive chain: through MCP, enumerate `9OS6` entities; verify polymer entity `1` maps to UniProt `P00533`, nonpolymer entity `2` maps to CCD `A1CEA`, and `A1CEA` has complete InChIKey `OMZCMEYTWSXEPZ-UHFFFAOYSA-N`, matching ChEMBL free Canertinib `CHEMBL31965`. Preserve the distinct dihydrochloride `CHEMBL545315` and its parent relation. Display protein label/auth chain `A/A` and ligand `B/A` without conflation.
- Negative chain: retrieve `5VCW` polymer entity `1` and show UniProt `Q99640`; it must not be reported as an EGFR complex merely because Pelitinib has EGFR activity elsewhere.
- Complete a selected mmCIF artifact download using the governed artifact path, verify its checksum, read the file downstream and retain the linked cross-database evidence in saved outputs.
- Complete an Agent journey using MCP metadata tools without direct HTTPS/web-fetch fallback; separately record Inspector, stub-model and real-model evidence.
- Cover extended CCD IDs; invalid/missing entities; missing protein/chemical mappings; timeout/rate-limit/partial failure feedback; and label/auth-chain distinctions.
- Add English and Chinese documentation with the positive and negative identity-matching examples and limits.

Official reference endpoints: `/rest/v1/core/polymer_entity/9OS6/1`, `/rest/v1/core/nonpolymer_entity/9OS6/2`, `/rest/v1/core/chemcomp/A1CEA`, and `/rest/v1/core/polymer_entity/5VCW/1` at `data.rcsb.org`.
items.title: [Feature] Complete MCP integration for domain-specific scientific databases

items.body:
## Goal

Make literature reports and review outcomes honestly verifiable: readers should see the evidence supporting material claims, know when evidence could not be verified, and never mistake a partial Quick review for full claim-fidelity verification.

## Workstream A — claim-to-evidence excerpts (from #415)

- [ ] For each material quantitative or clinical claim in a literature report, retain a short source excerpt or structured claim-to-evidence table with stable identifier and usable locator (for example PMID/DOI plus abstract/full-text location where available).
- [ ] Include the evidence in saved report/review artifacts without flooding model context; preserve source provenance and retrieval metadata.
- [ ] When an excerpt cannot be obtained, record an explicit evidence gap rather than silently presenting the claim as fully supported.

## Workstream B — visible unverifiable states (from #560)

- [ ] Extend the evidence/review schema with a visible `UNVERIFIABLE` status (or equivalent reasoned states such as identity unresolved and provider unavailable).
- [ ] Preserve the reason, affected claim/citation and review coverage in reports and review summaries. Do not silently discard identity-resolution or provider-availability findings.
- [ ] Keep the existing policy distinction: provider failure is not proof that a citation is false; it is an explicit limitation on verification.
- [ ] Align reviewer Skill instructions and runtime normalization so emitted states are representable and auditable.

## Workstream C — truthful automatic-review scope (follow-up to closed #414)

- [ ] A format/provenance-only Quick review must present itself as partial/format-only and disclose skipped claim checks with a reason.
- [ ] A claim-checked literature review must identify which claims were checked, supported, unsupported or unverifiable.
- [ ] Add regressions for stale report reviews, missing primary deliverables and the prior false-looking `ACCEPT_AND_PROCEED` Quick outcome.

## Validation

- [ ] Reproduce the CRISPR base-editing literature-report scenario from #415 and verify human-readable claim evidence or explicit gaps.
- [ ] Cover identifier mismatch, unresolved identity, unavailable provider, conflicting evidence, missing locator and provider timeout paths.
- [ ] Test Quick/Deep UI and saved artifact semantics independently; mocked provider success alone is insufficient.
- [ ] Document the distinction among supported, unsupported, unverifiable and not-reviewed claims.

Consolidates the unfinished scope of #415 and #560 and retains the relevant transparency regression from closed #414.
items.title: [Feature] Make literature evidence verifiable and review coverage explicit
