items.author: moShangLouTou
items.body:
Model-facing tool results currently serialize more canonical execution and MCP state than an agent needs, repeating output and exposing implementation metadata while leaving large results unbounded. This change introduces explicit, bounded result projections while retaining canonical records for audit and governed follow-up operations.

## Tool result projection

- Allowlist actionable `run_shell` fields: state, exit status, output, file changes, network denial, recovery guidance, and produced artifacts.
- Keep environment values, snapshots, authorization identifiers, session paths, hashes, and provisioner internals out of model text.
- Project execution management, workspace transfer, NPU, environment revision, and Skill draft results through similarly narrow contracts.
- Persist credential-redacted metadata for product traces and governed recovery, with raw payload omission and a defensive 128-level nesting limit. Interactive limits remain separate.

## MCP and arXiv results

- Bound model-visible MCP JSON to 48 KiB while preserving complete normalized details for audit.
- Deduplicate warnings, compact citation metadata, and make omissions explicit and recoverable.
- Keep artifact invocation and candidate identifiers needed by governed downloads while retaining license, attribution, and expected size for an informed download decision; provider URLs remain outside the model view.
- Add paged arXiv search metadata and a governed `get_paper` operation for retrieving a complete selected record after compact search.

## Test and journey alignment

- Align deterministic model fixtures and browser assertions with projected Shell and MCP result contracts.
- Poll managed scientific-environment readiness before environment-dependent journeys.
- Make environment creation failures explicit instead of timing out on a missing UI card.
- Read retained logs after a background execution reaches a terminal state because `execution_status` intentionally omits streams.
- Validate the artifact viewer's `76ch` prose measure against the active font instead of a host-dependent pixel constant.

## Current-head serialization safety and selective retention

Current head: `88b3960af52217f9500c4c79f2c2c9a17b5be363`.

- Build the safe model view without first stringifying/parsing the raw provider object. A credential-redacting and untrusted-tag-neutralizing copy uses a 128-level depth boundary and ancestor-based cycle detection. Deep/cyclic payloads keep a usable bounded preview instead of failing the MCP call.
- Serialize the safe complete copy only when the projection actually omits business information. If the safety boundary cut a cycle/deep branch, report that complete retention is unavailable; never attach a false full-result reference. Serialization failure is similarly non-fatal.
- Treat redundant record presentation metadata and empty artifact envelopes as intentional compaction. Complete small records and download plans no longer force storage or display an unnecessary recovery notice. Distinct supporting citations, unknown business fields and actual truncation still trigger retention.
- Make LR-14 exercise real truncation: the arXiv fixture has a long supporting-evidence field with a tail marker beyond the preview; the model recovers it through `read_tool_output`. The same actual model input contains an intact small PubMed result without a recovery reference.

Final verification on `88b3960a`, WSL2 Linux amd64 / Node 22:

- PASS: affected registry, guard/store, workspace projection, production AgentRun/versioning and literature fixture suites — 143 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- PASS: tools and workspace package typechecks.
- PASS: LR-14 supported product/browser journey — 1 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, using JiuwenSwarm, a local sandbox Runner, and local mocked model/literature transport.
- PASS: `git diff --check`.

The two new regressions failed on `5b5f43be` before the fix: deep/cyclic results failed the tool call, and an intact small record received an unnecessary retained-output reference. Final coverage includes 10,000-level nesting, cycles, credential/endpoint protection, source immutability, duplicate versus distinct citations, actual below-threshold truncation, complete download plans and unavailable storage.

Only affected tests, package typechecks and LR-14 were rerun for this update. Earlier/full results below remain scoped to their own commits; full local gates were not rerun. Native Windows/macOS/arm64 and live-model/provider paths were not exercised. New remote checks must run on this exact head before a CI/CodeCheck pass can be claimed.

## Previous MCP evidence and recovery fix

Previous tested head: `5b5f43be42d7832e0e9e78ea84d50a2523a187fd`.

- Preserve bounded `structuredData`, `crossReferences`, and result-level business `data`, including analysis summaries when `records` is empty. This keeps curated lookup payloads, Wiki bodies/references, and pathway statistics available to the model.
- Track projection loss explicitly, independently of `bounded`. A lossy projection supplies a complete safe `retainedContent` value to the registry/guard, forcing retention even when the compact preview is below the normal 8 KiB threshold. The model receives a `read_tool_output` reference inside the JSON response.
- Retain the complete safe provider result rather than the compressed view. Credential keys are redacted, untrusted control tags are neutralized, and provider `sourceUrl` fields remain hidden in both preview and retained output. These structural rules do not detect arbitrary secrets embedded in free text.
- Reserve space for recovery metadata inside the 48 KiB MCP JSON contract. Storage failure produces an explicit unavailable-recovery notice without a false reference.
- Extend LR-14 to check the structured effects in the actual model input and issue a real `read_tool_output` call to recover the original evidence.

Validation on `5b5f43be` in WSL2 Linux amd64, Node 22.19.0:

- PASS: affected registry, output guard/store, workspace projection, and production AgentRun/versioning suites — 136 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- PASS: tools and workspace package typechecks.
- PASS: LR-14 browser journey through an isolated product stack, JiuwenSwarm executor and sandbox Runner — 1 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. External literature transport and the model are local deterministic fixtures. The model receives effects `1.25` and `0.8`, then reads the retained original source evidence through `read_tool_output`.
- PASS: `git diff --check`.

The initial three regressions failed on the preceding `05df4868` implementation because structured data was missing and lossy results had no reference. Coverage also includes small array/depth/key losses, large custom text, non-arXiv abstracts, malformed record entries, Unicode JSON budgets, source immutability, storage failure, and download consent metadata/endpoint boundaries.

Only affected checks and the LR-14 journey were run for this update, as requested by the author. Full gates were not rerun. All earlier results below belong to their explicitly named commits and are not evidence for this head. Native Windows/macOS/arm64 and live-model/provider paths were not exercised.

Targeted test command: `node --import tsx --test packages/tools/src/registry.test.ts packages/tools/src/bounded-output.test.ts packages/tools/src/tool-output-store.test.ts packages/workspace/src/workspace.test.ts packages/workspace/src/mcp-result-view.test.ts services/api/src/native-agent/versioning.test.ts`.

Journey selection: `CI_E2E_FIXTURE=literature CI_E2E_SPEC=literature-review-sources-mocked.spec.ts CI_E2E_GREP=LR-14`, using the documented local wrapper, pinned Chromium and isolated instance/ports.

## Review follow-up

- Restore credential-key redaction and raw-payload omission before durable recording, independently of interactive size limits.
- Guard deeply nested provider metadata at 128 levels so recording and serialization cannot fail a turn from recursive nesting. A 5,000-level mixed object/array regression fails with `RangeError` before the fix and completes after it.
- Retain license, attribution, and expected bytes in artifact candidate model results before download consent. A governed browser journey checks the actual model request before approval.

## Previous CodeCheck follow-up validation

Previous tested head: `05df486891868479ef91beaf37619a409a68de6c`.

The exported unresolved CodeCheck report identified 14 findings: 12 redundant non-null assertions in `mcp-result-view.ts` and 2 hardcoded-credential findings in the registry redaction test. This follow-up:

- Validates all candidate/record objects with type predicates before projection, removing the flagged non-null assertions while preserving invalid-result fallback behavior.
- Generates the synthetic credential at runtime and checks redacted fields individually. Coverage still asserts that the credential never reaches the audit record, shared/cyclic references remain safe, and the source credential is unchanged. No rule suppression or redaction assertion was removed.

Verification on `05df4868` in WSL2 Linux amd64 / Node 22:

- PASS: registry and workspace suites — 95 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- PASS: tools and workspace typechecks.
- PASS: `git diff --check`.

Only affected tests were run, per the author's instruction. Earlier journey and gate results below remain scoped to their stated commits; no browser or full-gate result is asserted for this follow-up. External CodeCheck must rescan the new head before its result can be claimed as passing.

Commands: `node --import tsx --test packages/tools/src/registry.test.ts packages/workspace/src/workspace.test.ts`; `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/tools --filter @sciencediscovery/workspace typecheck`.

## Previous validation

Previous tested commit: `74509fc1a3337bfeac242c593e16f95e47df4d29`.

- PASS: `pnpm typecheck`.
- PASS: L1 — 4 planned, 4 executed, 4 passed, 0 failed or skipped.
- PASS: targeted registry, workspace-tool projection, and production AgentRun/versioning suites — 99 passed, 0 failed or skipped.
- PASS: governed-download browser shard with JiuwenSwarm — 5 planned, 5 executed, 5 passed, 0 failed or skipped.
- PASS: `git diff --check`.

The 5,000-level mixed object/array regression reproduced `RangeError` through `ToolRegistry.execute` before the depth guard; it now completes the turn and serializes the redacted audit record with a `[max-depth]` marker. Existing coverage retains ordinary deep/wide metadata, credential redaction, raw-payload omission, and persistence readback.

The immediately preceding production-code candidate `84a6459412258ba76428729d2256d825faf33990` also passed full UT (6,065 planned/executed/passed) and ST (51 planned/executed/passed), with 0 failures or skips. The final commit changes only the browser assertion's context-capture call and envelope handling. Full UT/ST/E2E were not rerun on the final commit at the author's request; final-head evidence above is explicitly targeted. The earlier full browser attempt was stopped after the new assertion failed because context capture was miswired; a focused follow-up exposed the JiuwenSwarm result envelope assumption. Both test defects are corrected and the final governed shard passes 5/5. Neither earlier attempt is counted as a full passing E2E suite.

Validation ran in WSL2 Linux amd64 with the documented wrapper, pinned dependencies, and isolated mutable runtime/results. Native Windows, macOS, arm64, and live-model paths were not exercised in this follow-up.

## E2E user journeys

PASS on final commit `74509fc1` for all 5 governed-download browser journeys using the JiuwenSwarm backend and an offline source fixture:

- Candidate resolution exposes license, attribution, and a positive expected byte count in the actual model request before consent; the source URL remains omitted. The researcher approves the download and receives the completed artifact.
- Denial prevents download; a matching grant permits another file from the same source; a pending approval survives reload; another Session inherits neither the pending request nor the grant.

Command: `sciencediscovery-env pnpm ci:e2e -- --backend jiuwenswarm --shard governed` with isolated service ports. No live model or external download was used.

## External checks

The CodeCheck failure on the preceding head was traced to the 14 exported findings addressed above. Those fixes were validated locally on `05df4868`. External checks must be read on the current head `88b3960a`; no external CodeCheck pass is claimed for it yet. Previous GitHub Actions runs were `action_required` with no jobs, requiring a privileged maintainer to approve the fork workflows.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix`

Applied GitHub release label: `release:fix`.

User impact: agents receive smaller, bounded, actionable tool results and can recover omitted safe MCP evidence with `read_tool_output` and page from compact arXiv search results into a complete selected paper record.

Compatibility and migration: none. Canonical audit records remain available; only model-facing projections are narrowed.

# 学科知识引擎：摄取/生长/消解/消费全链 + 会话绑库与反幻觉运行时

> 与 GitCode MR [!125](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/merge_requests/125) 内容一致（对应 GitCode issue #86）。

把「学科知识」做成 SD 的一等资产：文献与结构化源摄取为带锚点溯源的知识图谱，图谱可离线生长、实体消解、社区聚类；对话内绑定知识库（kb scope）后，图谱成为受约束的知识来源，输出必须引用锚点，与证据账本 / 新颖性检查 / 引用核验构成多层反幻觉链路。

**283 文件，+50.8k，4 个按路径分组的 commit**（KE 核心 / agent 运行时 / Web / 技能与测试）。

---

## 新增功能

### 1. 知识引擎核心（`packages/knowledge-engine` + `services/api/src/knowledge-engine`）

- **存储域**：SQLite（知识库/文档/锚点/实体/边/社区/合并/作业/引用/公式），带迁移机制；算法核与存储分离，可独立评测
- **摄取**：LaTeX-first arXiv 通路（tar.gz 解包 + `\input` 递归内联）、JATS XML、视觉增强 PDF 解析；溯源门抽取——每个抽取结论挂文档锚点
- **生长**：离线 grow job，MMR + anchor-aware 多样本选择、收敛信号、结构化反思 directive 反哺下一轮
- **实体消解**：在线门 + 离线 job、物理合并与回滚（`ke_entity_merges`）、louvain 社区、根实体、社区报告
- **消费面**：`kb_search` / `kb_expand` / `doc_grep` 工具、entity_unified_search、三级文档阅读器（全文/结构/锚点）、引用 API（意图徽章 supporting / contrasting / mentioning + Similar / References / Cited-By）
- **REST**：`/api/ke/*` 全套 + 前端知识引擎页（cytoscape 图谱画布、生长控制面板、阅读器、引用面板）

### 2. 会话绑库（kb scope）

- session 设置新增 `kbScopeKbIds` / `kbScopeWebSearch` 运行时覆盖项；composer 底部选择器一键绑定/解绑，写路径为 fresh-GET 读改写，避免并发选择器互相回滚
- resident-summary 上下文贡献者持续注入**在库**图谱摘要（成熟度分级）；范围外知识库对工具面与摘要均不可见（防泄漏包装）
- 系统 prompt m8.3.1：上下文时钟、kb-scope 自管理指引、反编造纪律句——均在既有 5000 字符保护段预算内

### 3. 反幻觉与研究运行时

- 三级注入：证据账本（`evidence_ledger`）、新颖性检查（`novelty_check`）、引用核验（`verify_citation`）；KE 工具输出逐字文本打 nonce 不可信围栏
- finish-gate 收尾审计：技能声明 `metadata.pre-finish-audit` 即在收尾前注入审计 directive，有界续跑（≤2 次）
- 研究世界模型 `research_state`：目标钉住 / 计划生命周期 / 未决问题 / 已排除路径防复活 / 已试去重，JSON 文件锁崩溃可恢复
- 审批门计划生命周期（`packages/plan-mode`）：`propose_plan` / `revise_plan` 工具、约束级审批、版本绑定决策、决策日志；与上游 `update_plan` 快照机制共存（`AgentRunBindings` 同时携带 `planRepository` 与 `planStore`）
- stall-guard：模型调用无进展按空闲窗踢出重试（≤3 次），外层空闲看门狗兜底
- 记忆图谱镜像 `observeSessionPlan`；MCP 配置文件内容签名失效（保留上游按服务器签名比较，叠加文件级变更检测）

### 4. 技能包与评测

- 15 个方法论技能：knowledge-engine-explore/grow、evidence-notes、hypothesis-tournament、tree-search、robin-chain、virtual-lab、idea-debate、systematic-review、precise-qa、long-form-writing/audit、progressive-report、report-writer、table-analysis（多数声明 pre-finish-audit）
- 评测套件 `scripts/ke-*-eval.mjs`：growth delta-recall、discoverer 诚信维度、pairwise、citation（ALCE 三指标）、resolution、bench 539 题；`skill-test-runner` + ER 数据集构建器
- KE 旅程 E2E 9 条 + kb-scope / finish-gate 旅程，ke-stub 离线可跑

## 验证

Linux（Ubuntu WSL2），分支 `pr/knowledge-engine`（基于 upstream/main 最新 `ef65b6f`，4 个按路径分组的 commit）。

- 29 个 workspace 项目全量构建通过（含 web vite build）；`architecture:check` 通过（293 文件）
- 触及包测试全绿：workspace 119/119、context 50/50、tools 61/61、runtime-core 36/36、memory 35/35、schema 12/12、plan 5/5、plan-mode 2/2
- **services/api 全量套件 1020 tests / 1019 pass / 0 fail**（`node --test dist/*.test.js dist/**/*.test.js`，123s 干净退出）
- 与纯 upstream/main 对照树同环境跑 server.test.js 验证无回归：upstream 86/86，本分支 86/86；期间修复了三处合并引入的问题（MCP transport 双重 close、内置技能清单落位、保护段预算超限），并把 KE sqlite 连接补上服务器关闭回收（否则每个 boot 泄漏 db+wal+shm 句柄并在进程退出时挂起 drain）
- 双计划系统共存验证：propose_plan 审批门与 update_plan 快照在同 run 注册、互不干扰（context-assembly 集成测试覆盖）

items.body:
## Problem

Evolve is the one capability that keeps running and producing results after the turn that started it ends, but the desktop app had no way to reach it: `/evolve-design` opened nothing, so a search could only be designed, confirmed and watched in the web client. A user working in the desktop app has to switch surfaces mid-task, and the run they left behind is unreachable from where they are.

## What this adds

- **Create dialog** — collects the two things a person actually knows (what should get better, which search algorithm fits) and hands that sentence to the conversation as the command the user would have typed. The agent still designs the scorecard, runs the probe and owns the checkpoints.
- **Checkpoint pace switch** — on by default. Turning it off sends `/evolve-design --no-confirm`: the agent still does the work of every step and still reports each checkpoint, labelled as automatic, but does not wait for a reply between them. Checkpoint 3's cost summary is kept, and a blocker that needs a decision (missing dataset, ambiguous goal, an approval the agent cannot give) still stops. The pace is recorded on the goal as `checkpointMode`; an absent field reads as `confirm`, which is what every existing run did.
- **Checkpoint cards** — each of the four checkpoints is drawn as a card in the transcript rather than as more prose: the step (`检查点 1/4`), the question, the few lines to read, and two answers — confirm and continue, or put "I'd like to change this step:" in the composer. A run with the pace switch off still shows the card, marked automatic, with no buttons. The card is read from the answer's own `evolve-checkpoint` fence, so it survives a reload; a client that does not draw cards falls back to the block as readable code.
- **Session shelf** — a thin row under the session header. A running search stays reachable when the panel is closed, and a session that never used evolve renders exactly as before.
- **Result panel** — follows the run's SSE stream, falls back to polling the run list, and answers in order: best score and how it moved, the candidate table, a selected candidate's diff, and why it was rejected. The inspector becomes a drawer on a narrow window.

## Tests

- `apps/desktop`: `npm run typecheck`; `npm test` — 752 pass, including new command parsing, dialog, shelf, panel, pace-switch, checkpoint-fence and checkpoint-card cases.
- `services/api` evolution suites (proposal, pre-flight, call budget, thinking control) — 51/51.
- `packages/evolve` 11/11, `packages/schema` 29/29.
- The desktop e2e suite gains `apps/desktop/e2e/evolve.spec.ts` with a mocked evolve runtime, including three checkpoint-card journeys: confirm sends the reply, an automatic card asks for nothing, and the change button fills the composer without sending. Playwright is not installed in this worktree, so it runs in CI rather than locally.

## Acceptance

The end-to-end path is the tutorial sample in `docs/en/domains/evolve-a-solution.md` (Chinese: `docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`), and the UI review tracked in #798 is the other acceptance item.

Related to #798 — this PR does not close it.

items.body:
Windows direct execution provides managed Bash, but persisted environments can lack the Unix utilities that the tool contract implies, causing commands such as `head` to fail without actionable capability or recovery information. This change makes the managed Windows shell contract explicit, upgradeable, and diagnosable.

## Managed Windows shell contract

- Provision MSYS2 coreutils, grep, and sed with `m2-bash` in the managed starter environment.
- Add `Library\\usr\\bin` to the Windows activation path so the managed utilities resolve without relying on an incidental Git Bash installation.
- Probe the managed Bash executable and guaranteed utility set, expose the platform and shell capability through Runner readiness, and refresh the probe after setup.
- Update `run_shell` and `check_runner` descriptions so the agent follows the target Runner capability rather than assuming host commands.

## Persisted environment upgrade and diagnostics

- Detect required starter packages missing from an existing environment, install only the missing specifications, and retain an audit revision.
- Avoid repeating migration for a newly created starter that already received the complete package contract.
- Attach a bounded `COMMAND_NOT_FOUND` diagnostic only when exit code 127 is accompanied by Bash's standard simple-command failure, preserving stderr as evidence and recommending an available utility or Python equivalent.

## Windows stack command shims

Route `.cmd` and `.bat` service entry points through `cmd.exe`, passing argument values through the child environment. Native executables keep their direct spawn path. This handles command shims while preserving spaces and literal argument metacharacters.

## Validation

Final tested commit: `82a8be4a0468008a1d49b4f5e14ba803c6313789`.

**The Windows product environment uses Node 22.** All operator-reported Windows product journeys below were performed with Node 22.

- PASS: affected Runner/workspace packages and their workspace dependency builds.
- PASS: schema, Runner and workspace typechecks.
- PASS: targeted environment-store, readiness, shell-diagnostics and workspace-tool suites on WSL2 Linux amd64 / Node 22.19.0 — 89 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- PASS: `git diff --check`; worktree clean.

Commands:

```text
pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/runner... --filter @sciencediscovery/workspace... build
pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/schema --filter @sciencediscovery/runner --filter @sciencediscovery/workspace typecheck
sciencediscovery-env node --import tsx --test services/runner/src/environment-store.test.ts services/runner/src/readiness.test.ts services/runner/src/shell-diagnostics.test.ts packages/workspace/src/workspace.test.ts
node --test scripts/stack-platform.test.mjs
```

At the author's explicit request, final-head validation is limited to affected tests and relevant product journeys; full local gates were not repeated. Earlier full runs on `f028f2fb` remain non-green: UT 6,046/6,051 passed (5 failures), ST 50/51 passed (1 failure), and mocked browser E2E 124/133 passed (9 failures, 0 skipped). Their root causes were not all established by baseline comparison; these historical results are not claimed as passes or definitively unrelated failures.

## E2E user journeys

PASS, operator-reported on final head `82a8be4` using native Windows Node 22 and local caches, through the real product setup API and chat/run_shell entry points:

1. Fresh installation: the product setup API created the starter environment offline and it reached `ready`.
2. Shell utilities: actual chat/run_shell verified managed Bash and the output of head, tail, wc, sort, grep and sed.
3. Missing command: error code and actionable recovery guidance matched expectations.
4. Persisted installation: an isolated legacy starter migrated, retained its prior revision, and passed subsequent chat/run_shell verification.
5. Idempotent restart: no additional revision was created and the catalog remained unchanged.

Execution attribution: the operator performed and reported these Windows Node 22 journeys. Raw command transcripts/logs were not supplied for independent review, and no additional automated-test counts are inferred. The agent's native Windows Runner TypeScript-suite attempt from the WSL checkout could not load `tsx`; no test body ran in that attempt, and it is not counted as Windows suite coverage. macOS and arm64 were not exercised in this follow-up.

## Supplemental script check

Separately from the Windows Node 22 product environment, the agent invoked a Windows Node 26.13.0 executable through WSL interop to run the stack-platform helper tests: 11 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. This checked command-shim argument handling, including a path with spaces and the literal `shim & %PATH% ready` argument. It is supplemental script evidence only; it does not describe the operator's Windows runtime or establish Node 22 coverage for that helper suite.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix`

GitHub label pending a maintainer: this contributor account lacks label-write permission, as confirmed when updating companion PR #717.

User impact: Windows `run_shell` gains a declared managed Bash utility set, upgrades persisted starter environments, and returns actionable command-not-found guidance instead of encouraging unchanged retries.

Compatibility and migration: existing managed starter environments are upgraded in place; prior audit revisions are retained and no manual reset is required.

## Review coordination

Ready for review. GitHub readback confirms review requests for CODEOWNERS `zhaozhaozz`, `zy95-12` and `HongyeZhou` after leaving draft state. The latest GitHub Actions run requires maintainer approval (`action_required`, no jobs executed). CodeCheck and CLA are successful. The `release:fix` label needs a maintainer.

Fixes #777

Owner: Dev2
Written-by: Dev-2
Tip SHA: 0bb3ee16884843a09d30278a63db007ba3f4da5d
Base: a429ba1d4eca17af8cfabb9f28abe9d651e38e6c (main at push; branch rebased onto it, no overlap)

`web_fetch`/`web_search` handed search-result titles and snippets to the model with named HTML references still encoded. Only `amp`, `lt`, `gt`, `quot` and `nbsp` decoded, so a page title like `Café — a review` reached the prompt and the report verbatim, and the sources a science search cites most often (encyclopedias, European sites) are exactly the entity-heavy ones. This decodes every named reference a browser resolves, in the same single pass as before.

## What changed

- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts`: the five-name map is replaced by the full WHATWG named character reference set — 2125 semicolon-terminated names — expanded into a `Map` once at module load. `nbsp` keeps its existing ordinary-space mapping; numeric references, the single-pass rule (`&lt;` → `<`) and unknown names (`&bogus;` stays literal) are unchanged. The decoding loop is the same one-scan replace it was; only the data changed shape and moved out of this module.
- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html-entities.ts` (new): the table itself — a `name;code point;…` constant, 246 folded lines — under a 37-line header that states the source (WHATWG named character references via CPython's `html.entities.html5`, 2231 keys of which the 2125 semicolon forms are what this pattern accepts), the retrieval date, the exact `python3` snippet that regenerates the body, and the licence position: the standard's table reproduced as factual data — names and code points any HTML parser needs — not copied from another project's source. `html.ts` keeps the decoder and goes from 79 lines to 90 (+11); 368 is only the shape this branch's previous commit had with the table inline, and this commit moves it out. The data is 246 of the new file's 284 lines.
- `tsconfig.base.json`: one line, `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions`. The import in `html.ts` keeps a `.ts` extension so `node --experimental-strip-types` — the command the issue reproduces with — resolves the sibling source instead of failing with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`; that option is what lets tsc accept the specifier and still emit `./html-entities.js` (verified: the built `dist/web/native/html.js` line is `import { NAMED_ENTITIES_PACKED } from "./html-entities.js";`). It belongs in the base config rather than the package one: the root tests config used by `pnpm typecheck` extends only `tsconfig.base.json`, and with the option in `packages/data-source/tsconfig.json` alone that check fails with `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts(73,39): error TS5097: An import path can only end with a '.ts' extension when 'allowImportingTsExtensions' is enabled.` From the base config both the package build and that check pass. It changes nothing else in the tree — the only `test/` file that `tsc` type-checks imports `.js` paths; the Playwright specs under `test/` are not in any tsconfig.
- `html-entities.ts` is force-added: `.gitignore`'s `data-*/` rule also matches the `packages/data-source/` directory (`git check-ignore -v` reports `.gitignore:91`). I left that rule alone to keep this PR single-purpose; say the word if you would rather have it anchored as `/data-*/` and I will open a separate issue.
- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.test.ts`: cases for the names in the issue (`eacute`, `mdash`, `ndash`, `hellip`, `apos`, `diams`, `rsquo`, `ldquo`/`rdquo`, Latin-1, symbols), case sensitivity, an unknown name, the single-pass rule after the table widened, and a guard that the exported table still has exactly 2125 entries plus one two-scalar value (`NotEqualTilde`), so a dropped or mis-chunked line cannot pass as a smaller table. The test file is unchanged by the move.

Size, whole PR: 4 files, 344 insertions, 8 deletions (`html-entities.ts` +284, `html.test.ts` +41/−1, `html.ts` +18/−7, `tsconfig.base.json` +1).

## Red first

Decoder tests. Command:

```
$ cd packages/data-source && node --import tsx --test src/web/native/html.test.ts
```

Before the fix:

```
# Subtest: decodes the named references a browser renders in titles and snippets
not ok 3 - decodes the named references a browser renders in titles and snippets
  expected: "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"
  actual: 'café — 5–10 … O'Brien'
# Subtest: decodes names case-sensitively and leaves an unknown name literal
not ok 4 - decodes names case-sensitively and leaves an unknown name literal
  expected: 'Ää'
  actual: 'Ää'
# pass 5
# fail 2
```

Table guard. The guard lands in its own commit before the export exists, so it is red on the change that adds only the test:

```
# pass 0
# fail 1
SyntaxError: The requested module './html.js' does not provide an export named 'NAMED_ENTITIES'
```

and it fails the way it is meant to when one entry is dropped from the packed constant (mutation check, one `AElig;c6;` field removed, then restored):

```
not ok 8 - keeps every entry of the generated WHATWG table
  expected: 2125
  actual: 2124
# pass 7
# fail 1
```

Green after the implementation, same command as the decoder run: `# pass 8`, `# fail 0`. The package suite goes from 74 to 75 tests with the guard: `# tests 75 / # pass 75 / # fail 0`.

## The issue's reproduction

Command from #777:

```
$ cd packages/data-source && node --experimental-strip-types -e '
  import("./src/web/native/html.ts").then(m => {
    for (const s of ["café — 5–10 … O'Brien", "&lt;b&gt; stays text", "♦ … ’"])
      console.log(JSON.stringify(s), "->", JSON.stringify(m.textOf(s)));
  })'
```

On this tip:

```
"café — 5–10 … O'Brien" -> "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"
"&lt;b&gt; stays text" -> "<b> stays text"
"♦ … ’" -> "♦ … ’"
```

The middle line is the single-pass guarantee: the decoded ampersand does not start a second scan.

## Gates

On this tip, in `packages/data-source` unless noted:

```
$ npx tsc -p tsconfig.json                                        # exit 0 (build)
$ npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit                               # exit 0
$ node --experimental-strip-types -e 'import("./src/web/native/html.ts").then(...)'
  café — 5–10 … O'Brien                                          # exit 0
$ npm test                                                        # # tests 75 / # pass 75 / # fail 0
$ cd ../.. && node scripts/check-architecture.mjs                 # 333 source files, boundaries OK
$ cd ../.. && node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json        # exit 0
$ cd ../.. && pnpm --recursive typecheck                          # 34 packages Done, exit 0
```

`pnpm architecture:check` is **98 passed / 1 failed** on this host: `scripts/race-contract.test.mjs` shells out to `.ci/run-research-python.sh race`, which needs a writable uv Python install and network (`Read-only file system` at `~/.local/share/uv/python`); it does not touch `packages/data-source`. `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs` itself is green, as shown above.

## Not run

- Repo-level UT/ST/E2E, CodeCheck (GitCode) and the Docker/binary layers: CI. This PR changes one package's text extractor and its test, plus one compiler option; the package tests, both tsc configurations, the architecture check and the recursive typecheck were run locally.

Fixes #673

`packages/data-source/src/web/native/fetch.ts` capped an extracted page with a bare `text.slice(0, MAX_DOCUMENT_CHARS)` (4096 UTF-16 units), so a character that straddles the cut left a lone high surrogate at the end of the body handed to the model.

Reproduction (`main` before the fix, logic copied verbatim):

```
$ node -e 'const MAX=4096; const text="x".repeat(MAX-1)+"😀"; console.log(JSON.stringify(text.slice(0,MAX).slice(-2)))'
"\ud83d"
```

Red commit `6c47106b` on this branch, before the fix:

```
not ok 11 - document truncation never ends in half a surrogate pair
  ---
  duration_ms: 7.465272
  failureType: 'testCodeFailure'
  error: 'Expected values to be strictly equal: ... actual ends in \ud83d'
```

## What changed

- `document()` in `fetch.ts` now drops a dangling high surrogate after the cut, so the result ends on a code point, never exceeds the 4096-unit budget, and creates no new lone surrogate. The same rule the artifact preview uses.
- New test `document truncation never ends in half a surrogate pair` covers both `renderTavilyExtract` and `renderExaContents` with an emoji straddling the boundary, plus a lone-surrogate check on the rendered document.
- Nothing else changes: same cap, same `# title\n\n` prefix, same vendor normalizers.

## Verified locally

Red commit `6c47106b` (test only):

```
# tests 14
# pass 13
# fail 1
not ok 11 - document truncation never ends in half a surrogate pair
```

Green commit `bb87febe`:

```
$ node_modules/.bin/tsx --test packages/data-source/src/web/native/providers.test.ts
# tests 14
# suites 0
# pass 14
# fail 0
```

```
$ node_modules/.bin/tsc -p packages/data-source/tsconfig.json --noEmit
tsc exit=0
```

Ran: the native-provider test file (14/14 pass), `tsc -p packages/data-source/tsconfig.json --noEmit` (exit 0).

Not run: the full `packages/data-source` suite, `pnpm -r typecheck` / `build` (the local pnpm store is read-only here), CI.

items.author: HugoXK
items.body:
Fixes #662

Owner: Dev2 / Written-by: Dev-2

**Label note.** `agent-ready` could not be applied from this account (403); this PR is proposed ahead of the 24 h label window because of the owner's sprint deadline. Claim record: Lead's pickup-ok on #662 — issue comment 6487523184.

## The defect

`ipv6Blocked` (`packages/data-source/src/web/native/url-guard.ts:58-69`) extracted an embedded IPv4 only from a dotted-quad tail. IPv4-mapped and IPv4-compatible IPv6 literals written in hex carry no dots, so they fell through to `return false`; `isBlockedAddress` then reported them as public and `assertPublicUrl` accepted them. `web_fetch` takes a model-supplied URL, so this is the SSRF gate itself, not a downstream check.

## What changes

- Expand the IPv6 literal to its eight hextets (compressed `::` and full form both).
- When the address is IPv4-mapped (80 zero bits, then `ffff`) or IPv4-compatible (96 zero bits), rebuild the dotted quad from the last two hextets and hand it to the existing `ipv4Blocked`.
- `ipv4Blocked` and the existing dotted-quad path are untouched; public IPv6 keeps being accepted.

## Commits

- `b9a10c6b1aac5554c6382bee030156f335de871e` — red tests for the hex mapped/compatible literals and the reverse direction.
- `b3d6112fbb228f3787816a6014f0410882b9240d` — red tests for delegation to the existing IPv4 range table and for the resolver path.
- `fc803262da45092ccc184bc27f9c38c9569db00a` — the guard change above.

No amend, no force-push.

## Tests

`packages/data-source/src/web/native/providers.test.ts`:

- `web_fetch judges IPv4-mapped and IPv4-compatible IPv6 literals by their embedded IPv4` — hex mapped and compatible literals are blocked, including the full eight-hextet spelling; the gate rejects them; the dotted-quad path keeps its behaviour.
- Reverse direction in the same test: public mapped and compatible forms stay unblocked and the gate still accepts them, so the change cannot become an over-block.
- Delegation in the same test: embedded addresses outside the `127/10/192.168` prefixes (carrier-grade NAT, benchmarking) are blocked, proving the judgement is delegated to the existing IPv4 range table rather than re-implemented.
- `web_fetch applies the same judgement to resolved addresses, not only literals` — a resolver returning a mapped literal must reject, so the DNS path stays covered.

Before (red-test commits, on `a074172f`):

```
not ok 1 - web_fetch judges IPv4-mapped and IPv4-compatible IPv6 literals by their embedded IPv4
  error: |-
    false !== true
# pass 0
# fail 1

not ok 2 - web_fetch applies the same judgement to resolved addresses, not only literals
  error: 'Missing expected rejection (PublicUrlError).'
# pass 0
# fail 2
```

After (fix commit):

```
# tests 15
# pass 15
# fail 0
```

## Out of scope

The guard still does not decode embedded IPv4 from NAT64 (`64:ff9b::/96` and `64:ff9b:1::/48`), 6to4 (`2002::/16`), Teredo (`2001::/32`), the IPv4-translated range (`::ffff:0:0:0/96`) or the deprecated site-local range (`fec0::/10`). Those are a separate next fix; this PR does not claim the gate is fully closed.

What this change closes: the two spellings that need no translator to reach a target, namely IPv4-mapped (`::ffff:a.b.c.d` in hex) and IPv4-compatible (`::a.b.c.d` in hex), on both the literal path and the resolved-address path. What it does not close: any address family that only reaches a target through a gateway or translator, listed above. Keeping the judgement delegated to the existing IPv4 range table is what makes the next fix a decoder addition rather than a second policy.

## Validation

Ran:
- `cd packages/data-source && node --import tsx --test src/web/native/providers.test.ts` — **15/15 pass, 0 fail**.
- `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p packages/data-source/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — exit 0.

Not run locally: repository-wide layers (`ci:ut` / `ci:st` / `ci:e2e`), because the pnpm wrapper aborts with `ERR_PNPM_ABORTED_REMOVE_MODULES_DIR_NO_TTY` in this container; this PR's own CI run is the authority for those.

Fixes #647

Owner: Dev1
Written-by: Dev-1
Branch: `dev1/fix/647-web-test-module-resolution`

## Problem

A clean tree cannot run the web test suite. Every workspace package publishes its runtime entry from `dist/` (`packages/*/package.json` → `"default": "./dist/*.js"`) and no `dist/` is committed, so a package-level run that does not build first resolves those imports to files that do not exist:

```
$ cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx
# tests 448
# pass 385
# fail 63
# Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '.../apps/web/node_modules/@sciencediscovery/operational-logging/dist/diagnostics.js'
#   imported from .../apps/web/src/ErrorDiagnosticActions.tsx
# Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '.../@sciencediscovery/schema/dist/index.js'
#   imported from .../apps/web/src/Markdown.tsx
```

The repo's own `pnpm test` hides this because it runs `pnpm build` first; the per-package script (`tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx`) does not. The 63 victims are not defects — they fail at import time, before any assertion runs.

The failure is not specific to `operational-logging`: `schema`, `skill`, `plugin-sdk` and their transitive workspace dependencies fail the same way.

## Commits (red first)

1. `test(web): prove the suite dies when the workspace packages are unbuilt` — one test asserting that every `@sciencediscovery/*` entry the web app imports resolves to a file that exists. Red on the unbuilt tree:

```
$ cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/workspace-package-dist.test.ts
not ok 1 - every workspace package the web app imports resolves from its built entry
  error: '@sciencediscovery/artifact-json/manifest resolves to
   .../apps/web/node_modules/@sciencediscovery/artifact-json/dist/manifest.js,
   which does not exist; the workspace packages need building first'
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

Full suite on the same tree: **449 tests / 385 pass / 64 fail** (63 pre-existing + this one).

2. `fix(web): build the workspace packages the test suite imports` — `apps/web`'s `test` script now runs `scripts/ensure-workspace-dist.mjs .` before `tsx --test`. The script walks `apps/web`'s workspace dependencies transitively and builds only the packages whose `dist/` is missing, using the repo's `typescript` and each package's own `tsconfig.json` — exactly what `pnpm build` would produce. It is a no-op once they are built, so the CI path that already ran `pnpm build` pays one directory listing and nothing else.

No test file is modified, and production resolution is untouched: the runtime entry stays `dist/`, which `node dist/server.js` and vite both need.

3. `test(scripts): pin the ensure-workspace-dist skip and build order` — the builder had no test of its own behaviour. Two cases run against a throwaway workspace (a copy of the script, fixture packages, and a stand-in `tsc` that records where it was pointed and writes the `dist/` the compiler would emit, so no TypeScript build is paid for):

- a package without `dist/` is built, a package that already has `dist/` is not rebuilt (its `dist/` is left untouched), and a second run of the script is silent;
- a package is built only after everything it depends on (`leaf` → `middle` → `top`, plus an unrelated sibling, built in that order).

Both cases are green as written. Their red side is a mutation, checked locally on the working tree and not committed: dropping the `dist/` skip fails the first case (`a second run must not rebuild a built package`), and moving `ordered.push(dep)` before the dependency visit fails the second.

## Verification

Red (clean tree, before the fix) → green:

```
$ cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx     # no dist/
# tests 449   # pass 385   # fail 64
$ node scripts/ensure-workspace-dist.mjs apps/web
built workspace packages without dist: @sciencediscovery/operational-logging,
@sciencediscovery/external-urls, @sciencediscovery/schema, @sciencediscovery/cas, …
$ cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx     # deps built
# tests 1131   # pass 1131   # fail 0
```

The suite grows from 449 to 1131 because the files that could not load now run. Typechecks: `apps/web` `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` → 0; repo `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` → 0. A second run of the builder prints nothing (idempotent).

## Labels and timing

`agent-ready` could not be applied to the issue by the team (the token gets 403 on label writes) and the owner's 60-minute deadline takes precedence over the usual 24-hour wait, so this is pushed ahead of the label being restored.

## Ran

- `cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/workspace-package-dist.test.ts` → 0/1 before the fix, 1/1 after
- `cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx` → 385/449 before, **1131/1131 after**
- `cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` → 0
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` (repo root) → 0
- `node scripts/ensure-workspace-dist.mjs apps/web` twice → 17 packages the first time, silent the second
- `node --test scripts/ensure-workspace-dist.test.mjs` → 2/2, and the same two cases fail under the two mutations above
- `node --test scripts/*.test.mjs` → 70/71: the one failure is `scripts/race-contract.test.mjs`, which shells out to `uv` and dies on the read-only `~/.cache/uv` on this host, unrelated to this change
- `node .ci/test-selector.mjs check` → `CI test catalog OK: 7 cases, 24 tags, 4 layers`

## Not run

- The shared tagged plan end to end (`node test/support/tagged/shared.mjs list`): on this tree it stops during collection with `DYNAMIC_REGISTRATION: apps/web/tests/markdown-math.test.ts:16`, a file this branch does not touch and which fails the same way alone at the base commit. The new file was collected on its own instead (`node-collect.mjs` → 2 cases, `category:ut`).
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test` verbatim: on this host pnpm's dependency-status check aborts with `ERR_PNPM_ABORTED_REMOVE_MODULES_DIR_NO_TTY` / `EROFS` on the pnpm store (outside the workspace, read-only), so the script's two commands were run directly, in order.

Release: fix

## What does this PR do / why do we need it

Implements the **full three-layer plan** for natural-language program evolution (GitHub issue #310): turn `/evolve-design` from a hidden slash command into something a natural-language sentence can trigger, with the framework actively recommending a tree-search evolution and the interaction staying natural-language end to end.

Today `/evolve-design` is a hidden slash command: a user must already know the prefix to start an evolution search, and the only visible entry is a button in the artifact detail modal that fills the composer with `/evolve-design make the artifact X better: ` (still requiring manual completion). The interaction is command-shaped, not natural-language.

### Layer 1 — Composer intent recognition (frontend)

- **`apps/web/src/evolve/intent.ts`** (new): pure `detectEvolveIntent(message)` — true only when an improvement verb pairs with an evolvable target (`program` / `code` / `algorithm` / `function` / `model` / `script` / `artifact` …). Non-evolvable targets (`formatting` / `layout` / `description` / `explanation`) never match, and bare "better" with no target never matches. `isEvolveDesignCommand()` separates the explicit slash command from natural language.
- **`EvolveSuggestionBar`** (new): a low-intrusion confirmation bar. Detection only *offers*; the user must explicitly accept before the algorithm picker opens — an evolution search spends real budget (mutations + sandboxed evaluations), so a false positive is worse than a missed suggestion.
- **`App.tsx`**: an explicit `/evolve-design` command opens the algorithm picker directly (existing behavior preserved); a natural-language intent shows the confirmation bar first, and only an accepted suggestion opens the picker. Both flags reset when the message leaves evolve intent.

### Layer 2 — Agent-driven recommendation (backend)

- **`packages/evolve/src/index.ts`**: the `create_evolve_run` tool description now tells the agent to **recommend** an evolution search when the user asks in natural language to improve a program / code / algorithm / model / result against a measurable target — not only when they type `/evolve-design`. The agent phrases it as a plain suggestion ("this looks like a search-shaped problem; want me to run an automated search that keeps the best-scoring variant?") and starts only after the user confirms. This builds on the evolve-design skill, whose description already lists natural-language triggers.

### Layer 3 — Visible entry points (frontend)

- **Composer**: a new sparkle "program evolution" button fills a natural-language prompt (`Improve the program: ` / `改进一下这个程序：`) instead of a slash command; `detectEvolveIntent` recognises it and offers the suggestion bar.
- **Artifact detail modal**: the evolve button now fills a natural-language seed prompt (`Make the artifact X better: ` / `让产物 X 变得更好：`) instead of the `/evolve-design ...` command text.
- **`intent.ts`**: adds `artifact` / `产物` as evolvable targets and `变得更好` as an improvement verb so both seed prompts are recognised.

### Why confirmation before the picker?

A search spends real budget. Detection is a guess, so it must only offer; the user's explicit accept is the gate. This is the core false-positive guard — a user saying "优化一下" while discussing formatting is never routed into an expensive search.

### Why verb+target pairing?

Intent detection is deliberately narrow: `优化一下界面布局` / `improve workflow steps` / `这个更好` / `make this better` all stay silent; only sentences pointing at an evolvable target (program / code / algorithm) match.

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes

Closes #310.

## Review follow-up (2026-10-29)

- Closing keyword corrected to plain `Closes #310`; the earlier markdown-link form left GitHub's `closingIssuesReferences` empty, so the merge would not have auto-closed the issue.
- Blocking item "CI green on this tip" is already satisfied **on this tip**: run [40645827814](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40645827814) (attempt 2) is `success`, 17 checks success (L1, ST, UT, Coverage, merge-gate, 5x L2, Freeze mocked E2E, CodeCheck); L3/L4-L5/Docker/Binary are `skipped` by policy.
- Remaining blocker is the human one: re-approval and the `needs-human` product-risk decision. The tip is unchanged (`070820a6`), so no CI re-run was triggered by this edit; the label is left untouched.

## Test Plan and Test result

Verification commit: `f9fe5846` (9 files, +192/-5, single commit, based on GitHub main `cc974a14`)

- Web typecheck: `tsc --noEmit` passed, 0 errors
- Web unit tests: **107 passed / 0 failed** (includes 8 new evolve-intent tests)
- Web vite build: passed
- evolve package typecheck + tests: passed

Intent recognition behaviour verified:

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| `improve the program` / `优化一下这个程序` / `让程序跑得更好` | triggers |
| `Make the artifact X better` / `让产物 X 变得更好` | triggers (seed prompts) |
| `make this better` / `这个更好` | no trigger (no explicit evolvable target) |
| `优化一下界面布局` / `improve workflow steps` / `改进一下说明文字` | no trigger (non-evolvable target) |
| `the first one is better` | no trigger (ordinary conversation) |
| explicit `/evolve-design` command | opens the picker directly, no confirmation bar (existing behavior preserved) |

## Self-checklist

- [x] **Design**: follows the issue's three-layer plan; confirmation-bar guard and narrow verb+target detection address false positives and budget protection
- [x] **Tests**: `evolve-intent.test.tsx` (8 tests) ships with this PR; typecheck and web unit tests pass
- [x] **Verification**: behaviour matrix recorded above with the verification commit
- [x] **Interface**: no public API change; reuses the existing `/api/evolve/runs` chain, `EvolveToolRuntime` and `EvolveAlgorithmPicker`
- [x] **Docs**: no website-doc change required for this frontend layer

## Review follow-up (sciencediscovery-bot review 5697796828, 2026-10-30)

Both points from that review are closed in code, not in prose. The branch was rebased onto today's `main` (`4e4837a9`) with no conflicts, and now carries three commits: the feature commit, the red test commit `85a78ad8`, and the fix `54889783`. New tip: `54889783e4831af67df7df517f7bd65912ea1da4`. Diff against `4e4837a9`: 15 files, +846/−14 (the two new files are the gate and its tests).

### 1. `requestConfirmation` is required, and the gate itself fails closed

- **`services/api/src/runs/index.ts:587`** — `EvolveTurnContext.requestConfirmation` is now required (`RequestEvolveConfirmation`, declared at `:203`), so any new evolve construction site that forgets it is a compile error instead of a silent spend. `tsc -p services/api` is what enforces it.
- **`services/api/src/bootstrap/platform.ts:385-387`** — the `turn.approvalMode !== "ask_for_dangerous"` fallback is gone; the runtime asks the gate and returns its refusal.
- **`services/api/src/evolution/confirmation.ts:88-97`** — when the callback is absent (only reachable from a caller outside the type system: an untyped script, a stale build, a test double), the gate returns
  `{ confirmed: false, refusedBecause: "confirmation unavailable: this turn has no approval path, so the evolution search was not started" }`.
  **Caller-visible behaviour:** `createEvolveRun` returns that string as its `refusedBecause`; the tool layer hands it to the agent, which relays it; no run is created, no discrimination probe runs, no budget is spent. It is the same data-not-exception shape as the existing "not confirmed by the user" refusal.
- **Why required rather than only fail-closed:** the field is what makes the *next* construction site safe at compile time; the runtime guard alone would only cover callers the type system never sees, and those must still be refused rather than allowed.

On `always_allow`: with the gate wired, an `always_allow` session still short-circuits inside `store.requestPermission` (`services/api/src/store.ts:5532`) — that is the product's meaning of the mode for every privileged action (`run_shell`, `direct_code`, …). The defect the review named was the *absent* gate falling back to that mode; a missing gate can no longer start a search. Making evolve pop a card in `always_allow` would make it stricter than every other privileged action, which is a permission-model decision rather than this PR's change.

### 2. Grant matching is by `resource`, so the resource now names the search

Read, not inferred:

- **`services/api/src/store.ts:5545-5552`** — `const matcherResource = permissionMatcherResource(action, resource)`, then `permissionGrants.find(grant => grant.action === action && (grant.resource === matcherResource || grant.resource === resource) && grant.state === "active" && grant.scope !== "once" && (global / project / conversation / session …))`. A standing grant is matched by **action + resource**, and non-`once` scopes are reusable.
- **`services/api/src/store.ts:5621-5629`** — deciding `allow_matching` creates a grant with `resource: permissionMatcherResource(request.action, request.resource)` and `scope: "session"`.
- **`packages/governance/src/permission-policy.ts:56-62`** — for `code` the matcher resource is the resource verbatim, so any suffix survives matching.
- **`services/api/src/store.ts:5471-5485`** — `authorizeByJiuwenSwarm` does look a record up by `toolCallId`, but only to avoid double-booking the decision row; it is not the grant lookup.

So the old `evolve-search:<sessionId>` really did let one "allow matching" click cover every later search in the session. Fixed at **`services/api/src/evolution/confirmation.ts:64-76`**: the key is now `evolve-search:<sessionId>:<fresh id>`, one per attempt — the card approves the search the user was shown and nothing after it, and even a retried call asks again. Wording follows the implementation in **`packages/evolve/src/index.ts:361`** ("That card approves one search: a later search in the same conversation raises its own card") and in the card label **`apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts:449`** / **`:3422`** ("this evolution search only" / "仅限本次演进搜索").

### Revert proof (fix reverted on the same tree, then restored)

```
$ git checkout 85a78ad8 -- services/api/src/evolution/confirmation.ts
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/evolution/confirmation.test.ts
not ok 1 - a turn with no approval path refuses the search instead of allowing it
not ok 2 - each search attempt gets its own grant key, even for a repeated call
not ok 3 - a grant from one search does not authorize the next search in the same session
not ok 4 - the gate asks with the call's identity and the search it is paying for
# tests 4
# pass 0
# fail 4
$ git checkout 54889783 -- services/api/src/evolution/confirmation.ts   # restored
```

The red commit `85a78ad8` carries the same four tests, failing on the unfixed gate. Test 3 drives the real `SessionStore`: it decides `allow_matching` on the first search's resource, shows the same search is then allowed, and asserts the next search is still pending (a card).

### Ran on this tip

- `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/evolution/confirmation.test.ts` → **4/4 pass**
- `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/evolution/*.test.ts` → **165/165 pass**
- `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` → **exit 0** (this is the check that enforces the required field)
- `cd packages/evolve && node --import tsx --test "src/**/*.test.ts"` → **10/10 pass**; `tsc -p packages/evolve` → **exit 0**
- `cd apps/web && tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx` → **1183/1183 pass**; `tsc -p apps/web` → **exit 0**

**Not run:** L2/L3, Docker and binary layers, and the full `pnpm check`.

CI: pushing a new tip re-triggers the pull-request gates for it; the previous tip's green run does not carry over to `54889783`.

## Low finding follow-up (sciencediscovery-bot review 5706765348, inline 4419359334)

`PermissionDecisionActions` no longer offers **Allow same type** for an `evolve-search:` request. Each evolution search asks with a fresh single-use key (`evolve-search:<session>:<uuid>`), and a `code` grant is matched on the whole resource, so a same-type grant could never authorize a later search: the button promised a decision the backend drops, and it printed the attempt id in the help text and left a dead grant in `PermissionGrantManager`. That card now offers **Allow once** or **Deny**; ordinary `code` requests keep the button.

`RunTimeline` shows the localized scope (`permissions.evolveResource`) in its details **Resource** row instead of the raw per-attempt resource, matching the collapsed card that already hid it.

Coverage: `apps/web/tests/Permissions.test.tsx` and `apps/web/tests/RunTimeline.test.tsx` assert the evolve confirmation has one secondary action, no "Allow same type", and no `evolve-search:` string in the rendered markup. Reverting the two component files turns exactly those two tests red (`# tests 81 / # pass 79 / # fail 2`); restoring them returns 81/81.

Ran: `apps/web` `tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx` **1185/1185**; `tsc -p apps/web` exit 0; `services/api` `node --import tsx --test src/evolution/confirmation.test.ts` **4/4**.
Not run: full `pnpm check`, L2/L3, Docker/binary.

## Typecheck-gate fix

Deleting the type field left two test literals setting it; only the root `tsconfig.tests.json` checks extraneous properties (`tsc -p services/api` does not include test files), so the local run missed it.

Ran: `pnpm --recursive typecheck` exit 0; `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` exit 0; `tsc -p services/api` exit 0; `node --import tsx --test src/evolution/confirmation.test.ts` 4/4.

Fixes #679

Owner: Dev2 / Written-by: Dev-2

## What the problem is

`CasStore.has()` answered the existence question by calling `read()` and mapped only `ENOENT` to `false`. `read()` re-hashes the bytes, so an object whose bytes no longer match its digest made `has()` throw `CAS integrity failure` — from a method whose contract is a boolean. Its sibling `verify()` already maps the same condition to `false`, so the two predicates over one store disagreed:

```
put -> b94d27b9934d 11
has before -> true
verify after corruption -> false
has after corruption -> THREW CAS integrity failure
```

The overwrite keeps the byte length (11 → 11), i.e. exactly the "same size, different bytes" corruption the store detects elsewhere. Callers use `has()` as a cache probe in front of `put` / `retain` / republish decisions: with a corrupt blob they crashed instead of taking the republish branch.

## What changes

`has()` now maps the integrity failure to `false` the way `verify()` does:

```ts
// A corrupt object is not usable, so has() answers as verify() does: absent.
if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT" || (error as Error).message === "CAS integrity failure") return false;
```

`has(hash)` is a total boolean predicate again: `true` only when the object is present and valid, `false` when it is missing **or corrupt**. `read()` still rejects a corrupt object with `CAS integrity failure` — the detection is unchanged, only the boolean answer is. A valid object and a missing object behave exactly as before. Two lines of production code; no new dependency.

## Commits

- `15247383034b21965143ab7e21d0aa681b77a6ad` — the red test only.
- `dfbc783d4a24913d113fcab6e7516271c292ee23` — the fix.

The red test is the first commit, the fix is appended on top; no amend, no force-push.

## Red → green

Red on base `ad34dd7847` (test commit only):

```
cd packages/cas
node --import tsx --test src/index.test.ts

not ok 3 - a corrupted object is absent for has() and verify(), and read() still rejects it
  error: 'CAS integrity failure'
  stack: |-
    CasStore.read (.../packages/cas/src/index.ts:98:43)
    async CasStore.has (.../packages/cas/src/index.ts:76:7)
# tests 4
# pass 3
# fail 1
```

The test pins all three answers in one place: `verify()` is `false`, `has()` is `false`, and `read()` still rejects with `CAS integrity failure` (so the fix cannot be "stop checking digests").

Green on this tip:

```
node --import tsx --test src/index.test.ts
# tests 4 / # pass 4 / # fail 0

node --import tsx --test "src/**/*.test.ts"
# tests 37 / # pass 37 / # fail 0
```

## Validation

Ran:
- `cd packages/cas && node --import tsx --test src/index.test.ts` — **4/4 pass, 0 fail** on this tip.
- `cd packages/cas && node --import tsx --test "src/**/*.test.ts"` — **37/37 pass, 0 fail** on this tip.
- `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p packages/cas/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — **exit 0**.
- standalone repro against this tip: `has before -> true`, `verify after corruption -> false`, `has after corruption -> false` (base threw).

Not run locally:
- repository-wide layers (`ci:ut` / `ci:st` / `ci:e2e`): the pnpm wrapper aborts with `ERR_PNPM_ABORTED_REMOVE_MODULES_DIR_NO_TTY` in this container; this PR's own CI run is the authority for those.

## Release

`release:fix` — label to be applied by a maintainer (labels are not writable from this account, 403).

**What type of PR is this?**

/kind feature

**What does this PR do / why do we need it**:

This PR adds a ScienceFlow Skill package to the project, enabling users to integrate and execute ScienceFlow-related tasks through the Skill interface.

Key changes:
- Add the ScienceFlow Skill package and its supporting files.
- Provide the necessary configuration structure for API integration.
- Enable users to configure their API settings before running the Skill.

**Important configuration requirement:**

Before using this skill, you must configure the API settings in `config/api.env`.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

N/A — This PR introduces a new Skill package and is not currently linked to an existing issue.

**What scenarios were tested, and what were the verification results（Function, performance, reliability, etc.）**:

1. **Skill Installation**: Verify that the Skill package can be installed and recognized by the target environment.
2. **API Configuration**: Verify that the Skill correctly loads the API settings from `config/api.env`.
3. **Functional Verification**: Execute a basic ScienceFlow task to verify the Skill's functionality.
4. **Reliability**: Verify that missing or invalid API configurations produce appropriate error messages.

**Special notes for reviewers**:

- API configuration is required before executing the Skill.
- Users must configure `config/api.env` with their own API settings.
- Sensitive API credentials should not be committed to the repository.

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
A terminal user can start an evolve search or an Idea Tree research and then only see an id. Progress and stop live on the Web cards. `evolve` and `idea` call the HTTP routes those cards already use, and they read the bearer token from the same data directory as `run`.

Fixes #50

## Commands

```text
ScienceDiscovery evolve list [--session <id>]
ScienceDiscovery evolve get <run-id> [--candidate <hash>]
ScienceDiscovery evolve watch <run-id> [--after <sequence>]
ScienceDiscovery evolve stop <run-id>

ScienceDiscovery idea list --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea get <research-id> --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea watch <research-id> --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea pause|continue|stop <research-id> --session <id>
```

`evolve stop` posts `POST /api/evolve/runs/<id>/stop`, the dashboard Stop route. `idea stop` posts `operation: "end"`, the card's End research route. Pause and continue are only on Idea Tree, because an evolve search has no pause. `evolve list` stays global; `--session` only forwards the route's existing `sessionId` filter. There is no `run --wait`. A long run is followed with `watch`.

Output matches `run`: readable text on a terminal, and one JSON object per line when stdout is a pipe, so `jq` works. `watch` adds `reconnect` lines and a final `result` line. A failure is an `error` line.

`watch` replays, then follows live, and returns when the engine stops running. A dropped connection reconnects for about three minutes. Evolve continues after the last printed event sequence, so an event is not repeated. An Idea Tree frame is a full snapshot with no sequence, so a reconnect shows the current state and skips a frame already shown. `--after <sequence>` continues an evolve watch in a new process.

Ctrl-C stops watching and exits 130. It does not stop the engine. `stop` does that. This is different from `run`, where Ctrl-C cancels the turn `run` started.

Exit status follows `run` (0 completed, 1 failed, 130 cancelled):

| Exit status | evolve | idea |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `succeeded` | `completed` |
| 130 | `stopped` | `ended` or `paused` |
| 1 | `failed` or `budget_exhausted` | `interrupted` |

A paused Idea Tree research exits 130 whether a person paused it or the token budget paused it. The engine records both as `paused`. `watch` also exits 1 when the run is missing, the token is refused, or the stream cannot be recovered.

## Validation

On `dada3d08c9ac343492e26e87cf95141eac92b28e` (parent `9c33627b5ffc3c3ef397c114e267de6e6cc6dd10`, clean worktree):

- `node --import tsx --test services/launcher/src/engine-commands.test.ts` — 26 pass, 0 fail
- `cd services/launcher && pnpm typecheck` — no errors
- `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` — exit 0
- `cd services/launcher && pnpm test` — 188 pass, 0 fail (includes the CLI journey below)
- `node test/api/engine-cli-journey.mjs` — `outcome` PASS, repeated 5 times on this commit
- L1: architecture boundaries OK; CI test catalog OK; `docs:check` 0 issues; e2e metadata 0 errors (11 pre-existing legacy warnings)

`pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, and `pnpm ci:e2e` were not run. The single-file binary smoke was not run; `run --help` is unchanged.

## E2E user journeys

PASS on `dada3d08c9ac343492e26e87cf95141eac92b28e`. Surface: CLI against the API process. Not a browser journey.

Command: `node test/api/engine-cli-journey.mjs`

The built CLI reads the token from the data directory. The journey uses a local fake model server and the evolve sidecar venv.

| Scenario | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Recorded evolve search: list, get, candidate source, watch, `--after`, stop, missing id | Piped output is JSON. Watch of a finished success exits 0. Resume does not replay earlier events. Stop of an already finished success stays `succeeded`. A missing id exits 1. | PASS. Watch printed 6 events and exited 0. `--after 4` printed 2 events. |
| Live evolve watch, dropped connection, then CLI stop | Event sequences stay contiguous with no repeat. Stop uses the dashboard route. The run becomes `stopped` and watch exits 130. | PASS |
| Idea Tree watch, then pause | Watch follows the running research and exits 130 once it is paused. | PASS |
| Continue that research, then stop | Stop sends the card's end operation. The research ends. | PASS |
| A second research runs to completion | Watch exits 0. | PASS |

The live evolve step mounts the real evolve route handlers and orchestrator inside the API process. The public HTTP API has no route that creates a search, and API startup marks an unfinished search failed, so that step is not a separately started product process. Its sidecar is a stub. The same SSE routes forwarded through the default JiuwenSwarm adapter were not run. The CLI calls the same paths the Web cards call.

## Release

Release category: release:feature

User impact: from a terminal, evolve searches and Idea Tree researches can be listed, inspected, watched, and stopped. Idea Tree research can also be paused and continued. The commands, options, and exit statuses are in `help` and in the English and Chinese CLI reference.

Compatibility and migration: none. Existing `run` behavior is unchanged.

## Update after merging main

Head is now `fa363435e4c2a57d6439797319a7fed0a5c7bc53`, a merge of `dada3d08` with `origin/main` `f4ceca57`. The merge keeps `--effort` and `--thinking` for `run` only, and keeps `--token` on `run`, `evolve`, and `idea`. The diff against main is still the same 13 files, +1961/−43. No `run --wait` was added.

On this head, launcher tests were 198 pass / 0 fail, including this CLI journey and the thinking tests from main. Typecheck, the test-project typecheck, and the four local L1 checks passed. GitHub Actions run 40210068505 succeeded for L1, UT, ST, Coverage, the four mocked L2 E2E jobs, and merge-gate. `CodeCheck (GitCode)` failed on both `dada3d08` and `fa363435`. The public result is only a failed status plus an OpenLibing link; that page does not include the rule, file, or line, and the MR has no line comments for it. No code was changed for that check.

## CodeCheck

`eca1478253d2ca170ee7669dfcd0266a7d8aaab0` removes the one CodeCheck finding. The rule was an unnecessary non-null assertion at `services/launcher/src/cli.ts:106`: `This assertion is unnecessary since it does not change the type of the expression`, on `invocation.engineSettings!`. The call now checks that the parsed engine settings exist and passes them on, so a missing action is a usage error. List scope, watch exit status, and stop behavior are unchanged.

GitCode pipeline `379944a082974e65b5317297e3031528` reports SCA, Anti-poison, CodeCheck, and Blacklist PASSED. On this head, GitHub `CodeCheck (GitCode)`, L1, UT, ST, Coverage, the four mocked L2 E2E jobs, merge-gate, and license/cla succeeded. Real E2E, binary, and Docker were skipped by policy.

Importing a research evidence package restores the conversation and the evidence needed to inspect and continue the original work. The `.sdresearch` plugin exports and imports workspace file versions, artifacts and provenance, execution history, trajectory details, and scientific memory.

## Behavior

- Imported sessions are read-only snapshots. **Create a new session to continue research** creates an independent, writable copy of the imported conversation and evidence. The copy runs as a background task that remains tracked after switching sessions; new research preserves the original snapshot.
- Workspace files open in a preview dialog. Text previews are limited to 256 KiB, supported images including PNG use the original bytes, and downloads preserve the original filename and complete contents.
- Trajectory export preserves model inputs, reasoning fragments, and tool-detail payloads. Import, restart, and continuation retain access to verified detail objects. Older packages cannot recover evidence they never contained.
- Necessary exports omit optional history and diagnostics while retaining required evidence dependencies. Complete exports offer independent checkboxes for full trajectory details and the full scientific-memory graph; deselecting the graph retains its summary. Export selections and source limitations survive import and repeat export.
- Export-size previews are keyed to the session revision and selection. Relevant changes invalidate previous results and trigger background preparation; unchanged sessions reuse their results without a fixed one-minute expiry. Pending results are shown as calculating rather than as a stale final size.
- Exports can run as persistent background jobs with status tracking, completion feedback, and original-name downloads. Downloading a job after its source revision changes is rejected rather than silently returning outdated evidence. Gzip compression is asynchronous; archive assembly still uses an in-memory tar buffer and is not a streaming implementation.
- User messages have a copy action; assistant reply copy actions remain available. Completed assistant replies offer **Branch to a new chat**, creating a writable conversation prefix through that reply. A persistent **Continue from chat** link returns to the immediate source reply. Imported read-only snapshots cannot be branched directly.
- Branching preserves attributable historical evidence, execution results, and reviewer-audit records, and discloses unavailable history. Busy sessions are rejected and request retries are idempotent. Import and continuation integrity checks compare the supported restored representation without inventing missing evidence.
- Importing a legacy package without scientific memory no longer fails snapshot capture solely because the graph service is unavailable. Packages containing scientific memory still require successful graph restoration. The scientific-memory summary is included in the snapshot payload type.

## Validation

Candidate: `d756f0173d3724e6808084259aeab75411151b95`, rebased onto official `main` at `52e345b29f3554743e43f4c5ef9d568801d72a7b`. Exactly one feature commit; author and committer are `zhaochen39 <zhaojichenjc@126.com>`.

Validation uses an isolated LF checkout of this exact candidate, independent dependencies and test data. No assertions, selectors, or retries were weakened to obtain a passing result.

| `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline` | PASS |
| `pnpm build` | PASS, including API and web |
| `pnpm typecheck` | PASS, including root test-source typecheck |
| `pnpm ci:l1` | PASS: 4 planned, 4 executed, 4 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped |
| Targeted feature regressions | PASS: 37 executed, 37 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped |
| `pnpm ci:ut` | IN PROGRESS; no final result claimed |
| `pnpm ci:st` | IN PROGRESS; 24 planned identities, no final result claimed |
| `pnpm ci:e2e` | IN PROGRESS; 131 planned identities, no final result claimed |

Targeted command:

```bash
node --import tsx --test \
  packages/research-package/src/index.test.ts \
  apps/web/tests/ResearchPackageActions.test.tsx \
  apps/web/tests/research-background-tasks.test.ts \
  services/api/src/research-export-previews.test.ts \

```

The full UT and ST commands are also running against a pristine checkout of the base above. Their outcomes are not yet available, so no candidate failure is attributed to main in this report. Previous revisions' test counts are not presented as results for this candidate. A passing full suite is **not** claimed; this PR remains Draft.

## E2E user journeys

Changed goals: import and inspect evidence; continue a snapshot in an independent writable session; preview/download workspace files; inspect trajectory and export scopes; copy messages; branch from a reply and navigate to its source; choose trajectory/graph export options; run an export in the background.

Expected outcomes: persistent inspectable evidence, original-name downloads, complete selected detail payloads, independent writable sessions, source navigation, revision-correct size previews, and background export completion/download feedback.

The research restore/export journey has been updated to select the full graph, inspect manifest/node contents, and exercise the immediate/background export controls. Browser execution uses the normal `pnpm ci:e2e` entry point with its pinned Playwright and Chromium preparation, the shipping JiuwenSwarm backend, mocked models, and isolated services/data. **Current status: IN PROGRESS, not a passing journey certification.** No real/paid model journey was run. Targeted component/API regressions do not replace browser or external-client journey coverage.
